H1.d: a primitive word; father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application). Compare names in "Abi-".

H3.d: from the same as אָבִיב ; a green plant.

H5.d: of foreign origin; Abagtha, a eunuch of Xerxes.

H6.d: a primitive root; properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy).
H6.k: break, destroy(- uction), + not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, X and surely, take, be undone, X utterly, be void of, have no way to flee

H8.d: active of participle of אָבַד ; (concrete) wretched or (abstract) destructin.

H9.d: from אָבַד ; concrete, something lost; abstract, destruction, i.e. Hades. Compare אֲבַדֹּה .

H10.d: the same as אֲבֵדָה , miswritten for אֲבַדּוֹן ; a perishing.

H11.d: intensive from אָבַד ; abstract, a perishing; concrete, Hades.

H14.d: a primitive root; to breathe after, i.e. (figuratively) to be acquiescent.
H14.k: consent, rest content will, be willing

H16.d: from אָבָה (in the sense of bending toward); the papyrus.

H17.d: from אָבָה (in the sense of desiring); want.

H18.d: from אָבַס ; a manger or stall.

H19.d: from an unused root (apparently meaning to turn); brandishing of a sword.

H20.d: of uncertain derivation; a melon (only plural).

H21.d: from אָב ; fatherly; Abi, Hezekiah's mother.

H22.d: from אָב and אֵל ; father (i.e. possessor) of God; Abiel, the name of two Israelites.

H23.d: from אָב and אָסַף ; father of gathering (i.e. gatherer); Abiasaph, an Israelite.

H24.d: from an unused root (meaning to be tender); green, i.e. a young ear of grain; hence, the name of the month Abib or Nisan.
H24.k: Abib, ear, green ears of corn (not maize)

H25.d: from אָב and גִּבְעוֹן ; father (i.e. founder) of Gibon; Abi-Gibon, perhaps an Israelite.

H26.d: or shorter Abiygal ; from אָב and גִּיל ; father (i.e. source) of joy; Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses.

H27.d: from אָב and דִּין ; father of judgment (i.e. judge); Abidan, an Israelite.

H28.d: from אָב and יָדַע ; father of knowledge (i.e. knowing); Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah.

H29.d: or prolonged Abiyahuw ; from אָב and יָהּ ; father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses.

H30.d: from אָב and הוּא ; father (i.e. worshipper) of Him (i.e. God); Abihu, a son of Aaron.

H31.d: from אָב and הוֹד ; father (i.e. possessor) of renown; Abihud, the name of two Israelites.

H32.d: or (more correctly) Abiychayil ; from 1 and חָ֫יִל ; father (i.e. possessor) of might; Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses.

H33.d: from אֲבִיעֵ֫זֶר with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite; an Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer; -- Abiezrite.

H34.d: from אָבָה , in the sense of want (especially in feeling); destitute.

H35.d: from אָבָה ; provocative of desire; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste).

H36.d: from אָב and טוּב ; father of goodness (i.e. good); Abitub, an Israelite.

H37.d: from אָב and טָל ; father of dew (i.e. fresh); Abital, a wife of King David.

H38.d: from אָב and יָם ; father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman); Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah.

H39.d: from אָב and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); Abimael, a son of Joktan.

H40.d: from אָב and מֶ֫לֶך ; father of (the) king; Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites.

H41.d: from אָב and נָדַב ; father of generosity (i.e. liberal); Abinadab, the name of four Israelites.

H42.d: from אָב and נֹ֫עַם ; father of pleasantness (i.e. gracious); Abinoam, an Israelite.

H43.d: contracted from אֲבִיאָסָף ; Ebjasaph, an Israelite.

H44.d: from אָב and עֵ֫זֶר ; father of help (i.e. helpful); Abiezer, the name of two Israelites.

H45.d: from אָב and and an unused root of uncertain. derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant); Abialbon, an Israelite.

H47.d: for אֲבִיר ; --angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout(-hearted), strong (one), valiant.

H48.d: from אָב and רוּם ; father of height (i.e. lofty); Abiram, the name of two Israelites.

H49.d: from אָב and שָׁגָה ; father of error (i.e. blundering); Abishag, a concubine of David.

H50.d: from אָב and שׁ֫וֹעַ ; father of plenty (i.e. prosperous); Abishua, the name of two Israelites.

H51.d: from אָב and שׁוּר ; father of (the) wall (i.e. perhaps mason); Abishur, an Israelite.

H52.d: or (shorter) Abshay ; from אָב and שָׁי ; father of a gift (i.e. probably generous); Abishai, an Israelite.

H53.d: or (shortened) Abshalowm ; from אָב and שָׁלוֹם ; father of peace (i.e. friendly); Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite.

H54.d: contracted from אָב and יָתַר ; father of abundance (i.e. liberal); Ebjathar, an Israelite.

H55.d: a primitive root; probably to coil upward.

H58.d: from an unused root (meaning to be grassy); a meadow. Compare also the proper names beginning with Abel-.

H59.d: from אָבֵל ; a meadow; Abel, the name of two places in Palestine.

H61.d: apparently from אָבַל through the idea of negation; nay, i.e. truly or yet.

H62.d: from אָבֵל and בָּ֫יִת and מַעֲכָה ; meadow of Beth-Maakah; Abel of Beth-maakah, a place in Palestine:--Abel-beth-maachah, Abel of Beth-maachah,

H63.d: from אָבֵל and the plural of שִׁטִּים , with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias; Abel hash- Shittim, a place in Palestine.

H64.d: from אָבֵל and the plural of כָּ֫רֶם ; meadow of vineyards; Abel-Keramim, a place in Palestine.

H65.d: from אָבֵל and מְחֹלַת ; meadow of dancing; Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine.

H66.d: from אָבֵל and מָ֫יִם ; meadow of water; Abel-Majim, a place in Palestine.

H67.d: from אָבֵל and מִצְרָ֫יִם ; meadow of Egypt; Abel-Mitsrajim, a place in Palestine.

H68.d: from the root of בָּנָה through the meaning to build; a stone.
H68.k: + carbuncle, + mason, + plummet, (chalk-, hail-, head-, sling-)stone(-ny), (divers) weight(-s)

H70.d: from the same as אָ֫בֶן ; a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between).

H71.d: perhaps feminine of אָ֫בֶן ; stony; Abanah, a river near Damascus. Compare אֲמָנָה .

H72.d: from אָ֫בֶן and עֵ֫זֶר with the article inserted; stone of the help; Eben-ha-Ezer, a place in Palestine.

H74.d: or (fully) Abiyner ; from אָב and נֵר ; father of light (i.e. enlightening); Abner, an Israelite.

H76.d: (by reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); an inflammatory pustule (as eruption).

H77.d: from an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous; Ebets, a place in Palestine.

H78.d: from the same as אֲבַעְבֻּעֹת ; splendid; Ibtsan, an Israelite.

H79.d: a primitive root, probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from אָבָק ; to bedust, i.e. grapple.

H80.d: from root of אָבַק ; light particles (as volatile).

H85.d: contracted from אָב and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude; Abraham, the later name of Abram.

H86.d: probably an Egyptian word meaning kneel.

H87.d: contracted from אֲבִירָם ; high father; Abram, the original name of Abraham.

H88.d: plural of אוֹב ; water-skins; Oboth, a place in the Desert.

H89.d: of uncertain derivation (compare אֲגָג ); Age, an Israelite.

H90.d: or Agag ; of uncertain derivation (compare אָגֵא ); flame; Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings.

H91.d: patrial or patronymic from אֲגָג ; an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag.

H92.d: feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind); a band, bundle, knot, or arch.

H93.d: prob of Persian origin; a nut.

H94.d: passive participle of אָגַר ; gathered (i.e. received among the sages); Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon.

H95.d: from the same as אָגוּר ; properly, something gathered, i.e. perhaps a grain or berry; used only of a small (silver) coin.

H96.d: from an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); a reservoir.

H97.d: dual of אֶגְלֵי .; a double pond; Eglajim, a place in Moab.

H98.d: from an unused root (meaning to collect as water); a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds.

H99.d: probably from the same as אֲגַם (in the sense of stagnant water); figuratively, sad.

H100.d: from the same as אֲגַם ; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes.

H101.d: probably from נָגַן ; a bowl (as pounded out hollow).

H102.d: probably from נָגַף (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap; i.e. (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops.

H104.d: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman).

H106.d: from גָּרַף (in the sense of grasping); the clenched hand.

H108.d: from the same as אוּד (in the sense of enveloping); a fog.

H110.d: probably from אָדַב (in the sense of chastisement) and אֵל ; disciplined of God; Adbeel, a son of Ishmael.

H111.d: probably an orthographical variation for חֲדַד ; Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite.

H112.d: of uncertain derivation; Iddo, an Israelite.

H113.d: or (shortened) adon ; from an unused root (meaning to rule); sovereign, i.e. controller (human or divine). Compare also names beginning with "Adoni-".

H114.d: probably intensive for אָדוֹן ; powerful; Addon, apparently an Israelite.

H115.d: dual from אָדַר (in the sense of eminence); double mound; Adorajim, a place in Palestine.

H117.d: from אָדַר ; wide or (generally) large; figuratively, powerful.
H117.k: excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty(- ier one), noble, principal, worthy

H118.d: of Persian derivation; Adalja, a son of Haman.

H119.d: to show blood (in the face), i.e. flush or turn rosy.

H120.d: from אָדַם ; ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.).
H120.k: X another, + hypocrite, + common sort, X low, man (mean, of low degree), person

H121.d: the same as אָדָם ; Adam the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine.

H123.d: or (fully) Edowm ; from אָדֹם ; red (see Gen. 25:25); Edom, the elder twin-brother of Jacob; hence the region (Idumaea) occupied by him.

H124.d: from אָדַם ; redness, i.e. the ruby, garnet, or some other red gem.

H126.d: contracted for אֲדָמָה ; earthy; Admah, a place near the Dead Sea.

H127.d: from אָדַם ; soil (from its general redness).

H128.d: the same as אֲדָמָה ; Adamah, a place in Palestine.

H129.d: from אֲדָמָה ; earthy; Adami, a place in Palestine.

H130.d: or (fully) Edowmiy ; patronymic from אֱדוֹם ; an Edomite, or descendants from (or inhabitants of) Edom. See אֲרֹמִים .

H131.d: plural of אָדָם ; red spots; Adummim, a pass in Palestine.

H132.d: or (fully) admowniy ; from אָדַם ; reddish (of the hair or the complexion).

H133.d: probably of Persian derivation: Admatha, a Persian nobleman.

H134.d: from the same as אָדוֹן (in the sense of strength); a basis (of a building, a column, etc.).

H135.d: intensive from the same as אָ֫דֶן ; firm; Addan, an Israelite.

H136.d: am emphatic form of אָדוֹן ; the Lord (used as a proper name of God only).

H137.d: from אָדוֹן and בָּ֫זֶק ; lord of Bezek; Adoni-Bezek; a Canaanitish king.

H138.d: original (prolonged) Adoniyahuw ; from אָדוֹן and יָהּ ; lord (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Adonijah, the name of three Israelites.

H139.d: from אָדוֹן and צֶ֫דֶק ; lord of justice; Adoni-Tsedek, a Canaanitish king.

H140.d: from אָדוֹן and קוּם ; lord of rising (i.e. high); Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites.

H141.d: from אָדוֹן and רוּם ; lord of height; Adoniram, an Israelite.

H142.d: a primitive root; to expand, i.e. be great or (figuratively) magnificent.

H143.d: probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire; Adar, the 12th Hebrew month.

H145.d: from אָדַר ; amplitude, i.e. (concrete) a mantle; also (figuratively) splendor.

H146.d: intensive from אָדַר ; ample; Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite.

H147.d: (Aramaic) intensive, from a root corresponding to אָדַר ; ample, i.e. a threshing-floor.

H148.d: (Aramaic) from the same as אּדְּרֵי , and גְּזַר ; a chief diviner, or astrologer.

H149.d: (Aramaic) probably of Persian origin; quickly or carefully.

H150.d: of Persian origin; a daric or Persian coin.

H151.d: contracted for אֲדֹנִירָם ; Adoram (or Adoniram), an Israelite.

H152.d: from אָדַר and מֶ֫לֶך ; splendor of (the) king; Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib.

H153.d: (Aramaic) an orthographical variation for דְּרָע ; an arm, i.e. (figuratively) power.

H154.d: from the equivalent of אֶדְרָע ; mighty; Edrei, the name of two places in Palestine.

H155.d: feminine of אַדִּיר ; something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress); also the same as אֶ֫דֶר.

H156.d: a primitive root; to tread out (grain).

H157.d: or raheb ; a primitive root; to have affection for (sexually or otherwise).

H158.d: from אָהַב ; affection (in a good or a bad sense).

H159.d: from אָדַשׁ ; meaning the same as אֲהָבִים.

H160.d: feminine of אֲהָבִים and meaning the same.

H161.d: from an unused root meaning to be united; unity; Ohad, an Israelite.

H162.d: apparently a primitive word expressing pain exclamatorily; Oh!.

H163.d: probably of foreign origin; Ahava, a river of Babylonia.

H164.d: from the same as אֹ֫הַד ; united; Ehud, the name of two or three Israelites.

H165.d: apparently an orthographical variation for אַיֵּה ; where. 13:10, 14) (which is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from הָיָה ).

H166.d: a primitive root; to be clear.

H167.d: a denominative from אֹ֫הֶל ; to tent.

H168.d: from יַאֲהִיל ; a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance).

H169.d: the same as אֹ֫הֶל ; Ohel, an Israelite.

H170.d: in form a feminine of 'ohel , but in fact for.Oholahh ; from אֹ֫הֶל ; her tent (i.e. idolatrous sanctuary); Oholah, a symbol. name for Samaria.

H171.d: from אֹ֫הֶל and אָב ; tent of (his) father; Oholiab, an Israelite.

H172.d: (similarly with אָהֳלָה ) for Oholiybahh ; from אֹ֫הֶל ; my tent (is) in her; Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah.

H173.d: from אֹ֫הֶל and בָּמָה ; tent of (the) height; Oholibamah, a wife of Esau.

H174.d: or (feminine) ahalowth (only used thus in the plural); of foreign origin; aloe wood (i.e. sticks).

H175.d: of uncertain derivation; Aharon, the brother of Moses.

H176.d: presumed to be the "constructive" or genitival form of -av ; short for אַוַּת ; desire (and so probably in Prov. 31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if.
H176.k: also, and, either, if, at the least, X nor, or, otherwise, then, whether

H177.d: from אַו and אֵל ; wish of God; Uel, and Israelite.

H178.d: from the same as אָב (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); properly, a mumble, i.e. a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar).

H179.d: probably from אָבַל ; mournful; Obil, an Ishmaelite.

H180.d: or (shortened) ubal ; from יָבַל (in the sense of יִבְלֵי ); a stream.

H181.d: from an unused root meaning to rake together; a poker (for turning or gathering embers).

H182.d: or (shortened) rodowth (only thus in the plural); from the same as אוּד ; turnings (i.e. occasions); (adverb) on account of.

H183.d: a primitive root; to wish for.
H183.k: covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after)

H184.d: a primitive root; to extend or mark out.

H186.d: perhaps by permutation for עֻזִּי , strong; Uzai, an Israelite.

H187.d: of uncertain derivation; Uzal, a son of Joktan.

H188.d: probably from אָוָה (in the sense of crying out after); lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!.

H189.d: probably from אָוָה ; desirous; Evi, a Midianitish chief.

H191.d: from an unused root (meaning to be perverse); (figuratively) silly.

H192.d: of Aramaic derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak; Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king.

H193.d: from an unused root meaning to twist, i.e. (by implication) be strong; the body (as being rolled together); also powerful.

H194.d: or (shortened) rulay ; from אַו ; if not; hence perhaps.
H194.k: if so be, may be, peradventure, unless

H195.d: of Persian derivation; the Ulai (or Eulaeus), a river of Persia.

H196.d: from אֱוִיל ; silly, foolish; hence (morally) impious.

H197.d: or (shortened) ulam ; from אָלַם (in the sense of tying); a vestibule (as bound to the building).

H198.d: appar, from אָלַם (in the sense of dumbness); solitary; Ulam, the name of two Israelites.

H199.d: apparently a variation of אוּלַי ; however or on the contrary.
H199.k: as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore

H200.d: from the same as אֱוִיל ; silliness.

H201.d: from אָמַר ; talkative; Omar, a grandson of Esau.

H202.d: probably from the same as אָ֫וֶן (in the sense of effort, but successful); ability, power, (figuratively) wealth.

H203.d: the same as אוֹן ; On, an Israelite.

H204.d: or (shortened) On ; of Egyptian derivation; On, a city of Egypt.

H205.d: from an unused root perhaps meaning properly, to pant (hence, to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol. Compare אַ֫יִן .
H205.k: affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners(-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked(-ness)

H206.d: the same as אָ֫וֶן ; idolatry; Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele-Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel). See also אֹן , בֵּית אָ֫וֶן .

H207.d: or (shortened) ;Onow ; prolonged from אוֹן ; strong; Ono, a place in Palestine.

H208.d: a variation of אוֹנָן ; strong; Onam, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite.

H209.d: a variation of אוֹנוֹ ; strong; Onan, a son of Judah.

H210.d: perhaps a corruption of אוֹפִיר ; Uphaz, a famous gold region.

H211.d: or (shortened) Ophiyr ; and Owphir ; of uncertain derivation; Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East.

H212.d: or (shortened) pophan ; from an unused root meaning to revolve; a wheel.

H213.d: a primitive root; to press; (by implication) to be close, hurry, withdraw.

H215.d: a primitive root; to be (causative, make) luminous (literally and metaphorically).
H215.k: X break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine

H216.d: from אוֹר ; illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.).
H216.k: bright, clear, + day, light (-ning), morning, sun

H217.d: from אוֹר ; flame; hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light). See also אוּרִים .

H218.d: the same as אוּר ; Ur, a place in Chaldaea; also an Israelite.

H219.d: feminine of אוֹר ; luminousness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright).

H220.d: by transposition for אֻרָוֹת ; a stall.

H221.d: from אוּר ; fiery; Uri, the name of three Israelites.

H222.d: from אוּר and אֵל ; flame of God; Uriel, the name of two Israelites.

H223.d: or (prolonged) Uwriyahuw ; from אוּר and יָהּ ; flame of Jah; Urijah, the name of one Hittite and five Israelites.

H224.d: plur of אוּר ; lights; Urim, the oracular brilliancy of the figures in the high-priest's breastplate.

H225.d: a primitive root; properly, to come, i.e. (implied) to assent.

H226.d: probably from אוּת (in the sense of appearing); a signal (literally or figuratively), as a flag, beacon, monument, omen, prodigy, evidence, etc.

H227.d: a demonstrative adverb; at that time or place; also as a conjunction, therefore.
H227.k: beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet

H228.d: (Aramaic) or iazah (Aramaic); to kindle; (by implication) to heat.

H229.d: probably from אֵזוֹב ; hyssop-like; Ezbai, an Israelite.

H232.d: from אֲזִקִּים ; something girt; a belt, also a band.

H233.d: probably from אָז ; at that time.

H234.d: from זָכַר ; a reminder; specifically remembrance- offering.

H235.d: a primitive root; to go away, hence, to disappear. 27:19 the word is rendered by many "from Uzal," by others "yarn"), be gone (spent).
H235.k: fail, gad about, go to and fro (but in Ezek

H236.d: (Aramaic) the same as אָזַל ; to depart.

H237.d: from אָזַל ; departure; Ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine.

H238.d: a primitive root; probably to expand; but used only as a denominative from אֹ֫זֶן ; to broaden out the ear (with the hand), i.e. (by implication) to listen. See אָזַן .

H239.d: a primitive root (rather identical with הֶאֱזִין through the idea of scales as if two ears); to weigh, i.e. (figuratively) ponder.

H240.d: from הֶאֱזִין ; a spade or paddle (as having a broad end).

H241.d: from הֶאֱזִין ; broadness. i.e. (concrete) the ear (from its form in man).
H241.k: + advertise, audience, + displease, ear, hearing, + show

H242.d: from הֶאֱזִין and שֶׁאֱרָה ; plat of Sheerah (i.e. settled by him); Uzzen-Sheerah, a place in Palestine.

H243.d: from הֶאֱזִין and תָּבוֹר ; flats (i.e. tops) of Tabor (i.e. situated on it); Aznoth-Tabor, a place in Palestine.

H244.d: from אֹ֫זֶן ; having (quick) ears; Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendant.

H245.d: from הֶאֱזִין and יָהּ ; heard by Jah; Azanjah, an Israelite.

H248.d: a variation for זְר֫וֹעַ ; the arm.

H249.d: from זָרַח (in the sense of springing up); a spontaneous growth, i.e. native (tree or persons).
H249.k: bay tree, (home-)born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation)

H250.d: patronymic from חֹבָב ; an Ezrachite or descendant of Zerach.

H251.d: a primitive word; a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like אָב )). Compare also the proper names beginning with "Ah-" or "Ahi-".

H253.d: a variation for אֲהָהּ ; Oh! (expressive of grief or surprise).

H254.d: of uncertain derivation; a fire-pot or chafing dish.

H255.d: probably from אָח ; a howler or lonesome wild animal.

H256.d: once (by contraction) Echab (Jer. 29:22); from אָח and אָב ; brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father; Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon.

H257.d: from אָח and בִּין ; brother (i.e. possessor) of understanding; Achban, an Israelite.

H258.d: perhaps a primitive root; to unify, i.e. (figuratively) collect (one's thoughts).

H259.d: a numeral from אָחַד ; properly, united, i.e. one; or (as an ordinal) first:--a, alike, alone, altogether, and, any(-thing), apiece, a certain, (dai-)ly, each (one), + eleven, every, few, first, + highway, a man, once, one, only, other, some, together,

H260.d: of uncertain (perhaps Egyptian) derivation; a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile).

H261.d: from אָחַד ; united; Echud, the name of three Israelites.

H262.d: from חָוָה (in the sense of חֲוָא ); an utterance.

H265.d: by reduplication from אָח ; brotherly; Achoach, an Israelite.

H266.d: patronymic from אַחֲוָה ; an Achochite or descendant of Achoach.

H267.d: perhaps from אָח and מָ֫יִם ; brother (i.e. neighbour) of water; Achumai, an Israelite.

H268.d: or (shortened) achor ; from אֲחִירַע ; the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West.
H268.k: after(-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-)hind(-er part), time to come, without

H269.d: irregular feminine of אָח ; a sister (used very widely (like אֶזְרָחִי ), literally and figuratively).

H270.d: a primitive root; to seize (often with the accessory idea of holding in possession).
H270.k: + be affrighted, bar, (catch, lay, take) hold (back), come upon, fasten, handle, portion, (get, have or take) possess(-ion)

H271.d: from אָחַז ; possessor; Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite.

H272.d: feminine passive participle from אָחַז ; something seized, i.e. a possession (especially of land).

H273.d: from אָחַז ; seizer; Achzai, an Israelite.

H274.d: or (prolonged) Achazyahuw ; from אָחַז and יָהּ ; Jah has seized; Achazjah, the name of a Jewish and an Israelite king.

H275.d: from אָחַז ; seizure; Achuzzam, an Israelite.

H276.d: a variation of אֲחֻזָּה ; possession; Achuzzath, a Philistine.

H277.d: from אָח ; brotherly; Achi, the name of two Israelites.

H278.d: probably the same as אֲחִי ; Echi, an Israelite.

H279.d: from אָח and אֵם ; brother of the mother (i.e. uncle); Achiam, an Israelite.

H281.d: or (prolonged) Achiyahuw ; from אָח and יָהּ ; brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Achijah, the name of nine Israelites.

H282.d: from אָח and הוֹד ; brother (i.e. possessor) of renown; Achihud, an Israelite.

H283.d: prolonged from אָח ; brotherly; Achio, the name of three Israelites.

H284.d: from אָח and חוּד ; brother of a riddle (i.e. mysterious); Achichud, an Israelite.

H285.d: from אָח and טוּב ; brother of goodness; Achitub, the name of several priests.

H286.d: from אָח and יָלַד ; brother of one born; Achilud, an Israelite.

H287.d: from אָח and מוּת ; brother of death; Achimoth, an Israelite.

H288.d: from אָח and מֶ֫לֶך ; brother of (the) king; Achimelek, the name of an Israelite and of a Hittite.

H289.d: or Achiyman ; from אָח and מִן ; brother of a portion (i.e. gift); Achiman, the name of an Anakite and of an Israelite.

H290.d: from אָח and the equivalent of מַ֫עַץ ; brother of anger; Achimaats, the name of three Israelites.

H291.d: from אָח ; brotherly; Achjan, an Israelite.

H292.d: from אָח and נָדַב ; brother of liberality; Achinadab, an Israelite.

H293.d: from אָח and נֹ֫עַם ; brother of pleasantness; Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses.

H294.d: from אָח and סָמַך ; brother of support; Achisamak, an Israelite.

H295.d: from אָח and עֵ֫זֶר ; brother of help; Achiezer, the name of two Israelites.

H296.d: from אָח and קוּם ; brother of rising (i.e. high); Achikam, an Israelite.

H297.d: from אָח and רוּם ; brother of height (i.e. high); Achiram, an Israelite.

H298.d: patronymic from אֲחִירָם ; an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram.

H299.d: from אָח and רָע ; brother of wrong; Achira, an Israelite.

H300.d: from אָח and שָׁ֫חַר ; brother of (the) dawn; Achishachar, an Israelite.

H301.d: from אָח and שִׁיר ; brother of (the) singer; Achishar, an Israelite.

H302.d: from אָח and תָּפֵל ; brother of folly; Achithophel, an Israelite.

H303.d: from the same root as חֵ֫לֶב ; fatness (i.e. fertile); Achlab, a place in Palestine.

H304.d: the same as אַחֲלַי ; wishful; Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite.

H305.d: or achaley ; prob from אָח and a variation of לוּא ; would that!.

H306.d: perhaps from חָלַם (and thus dream-stone); a gem, probably the amethyst.

H307.d: of Persian derivation; Achmetha (i.e. Ecbatana), the summer capital of Persia.

H308.d: of uncertain derivation; Achasbai, an Israelite.

H309.d: a primitive root; to loiter (i.e. be behind); by implication to procrastinate.
H309.k: continue, defer, delay, hinder, be late (slack), stay (there), tarry (longer)

H310.d: from אָחַר ; properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses).
H310.k: after (that, -ward), again, at, away from, back (from, -side), behind, beside, by, follow (after, -ing), forasmuch, from, hereafter, hinder end, + out (over) live, + persecute, posterity, pursuing, remnant, seeing, since, thence(-forth), when, with

H312.d: from אָחַר ; properly, hinder; generally, next, other, etc.

H313.d: the same as אַחֵר ; Acher, an Israelite.

H314.d: or (shortened) ;acharon ; from אָחַר ; hinder; generally, late or last; specifically (as facing the east) western.
H314.k: after (-ward), to come, following, hind(-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward, ut(ter)most

H315.d: from אַחַר and אָח ; after (his) brother: Achrach, an Israelite.

H316.d: from אַחַר and חֵיל ; behind (the) intrenchment (i.e. safe); Acharchel, an Israelite:--Aharhel,

H319.d: from אַחַר ; the last or end, hence, the future; also posterity.
H319.k: (last, latter) end (time), hinder (utter) -most, length, posterity, remnant, residue, reward

H320.d: (Aramaic) from אַחֲרֵי ; the same as אַחֲרִית ; later.

H321.d: (Aramaic) from אַחֲרֵי ; the same as אָחֳרִי ; other.

H323.d: of Persian derivation; a satrap or governor of a main province (of Persia).

H325.d: or (shortened) Achashrosh (Esth. 10:1); of Persian origin; Achashverosh (i.e. Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king.

H326.d: probably of Persian derivation; an achastarite (i.e. courier); the designation (rather than name) of an Israelite. the article).

H328.d: from an unused root perhaps meaning to move softly; (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently.

H329.d: from an unused root probably meaning to pierce or make fast; a thorn-tree (especially the buckthorn).

H330.d: from an unused root (probably meaning to bind); properly, twisted (yarn), i.e. tapestry.

H331.d: a primitive root; to close (the lips or ears); by analology to contract (a window by bevelled jambs).

H332.d: a primitive root; to close up.

H333.d: from אָטַר ; maimed; Ater, the name of three Israelites.

H334.d: from אָטַר ; shut up, i.e. impeded (as to the use of the right hand).

H335.d: perhaps from מֵאַ֫יִן ; where? hence how?.
H335.k: how, what, whence, where, whether, which (way)

H336.d: probably identical with אַי (through the idea of a query); not.

H338.d: probably identical with אּי (through the idea of a doleful sound); a howler (used only in the plural), i.e. any solitary wild creature; --wild beast of the islands.

H339.d: from אָוָה ; properly, a habitable spot (as desirable); dry land, a coast, an island.

H340.d: a primitive root; to hate (as one of an opposite tribe or party); hence to be hostile.

H341.d: or (fully) owyeb ; active participle of אָיַב ; hating; an adversary.

H343.d: from the same as אוּד (in the sense of bending down); oppression; by implication misfortune, ruin.

H344.d: perhaps from אּי ; the screamer, i.e. a hawk.

H345.d: the same as אַיָּה ; Ajah, the name of two Israelites.

H347.d: from אָיַב ; hated (i.e. persecuted); Ijob, the patriarch famous for his patience.

H348.d: from אּי and זְבֻל ; Izebel, the wife of king Ahab.

H349.d: also eykah ; and teykakah ; prolonged from אַי ; how? or how!; also where.

H350.d: from אּי and כָּבוֹד ; (there is) no glory, i.e. inglorious; Ikabod, a son of Phineas.

H351.d: probably a variation for NONE , but not as an interogative; where.

H352.d: from the same as אוּל ; properly, strength; hence, anything strong; specifically a chief (politically); also a ram (from his strength); a pilaster (as a strong support); an oak or other strong tree.
H352.k: mighty (man), lintel, oak, post, ram, tree

H354.d: an intensive form of אָ֫יִל (in the sense of ram); a stag or male deer.

H355.d: feminine of אַיָּל ; a doe or female deer.

H356.d: or (shortened) ;Elown ; or Eylon ; from אָ֫יִל ; oak-grove; Elon, the name of a place in Palestine, and also of one Hittite, two Israelites.

H357.d: from אַיָּל ; deer-field; Ajalon, the name of five places in Palestine.

H358.d: from אֵילוֹן , בָּ֫יִת , and חָנַן ; oak-grove of (the) house of favor; Elon of Beth-chanan, a place in Palestine.

H359.d: or Eylath ; from אָ֫יִל ; trees or a grove (i.e. palms); Eloth or Elath, a place on the Red Sea.

H360.d: feminine of אֱיָל ; power; by implication, protection.

H361.d: or (shortened) ;elam ; or (feminine) ielammah ; probably from אָ֫יִל ; a pillar-space (or colonnade), i.e. a pale (or portico).

H362.d: plural of אָ֫יִל ; palm-trees; Elim, a place in the Desert.

H364.d: from אָ֫יִל and פָּארָן ; oak of Paran; El- Paran, a portion of the district of Paran.

H365.d: the same as אַיָּלָה ; a doe.

H366.d: from an unused root (meaning to frighten); frightful.

H367.d: or (shortened) remah ; from the same as אָיֹם ; fright; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear).
H367.k: dread, fear, horror, idol, terrible, terror

H368.d: plural of אֵימִים ; terrors; Emim, an early Canaanitish (or Maobitish) tribe.

H369.d: as if from a primitive root meaning to be nothing or not exist; a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle. Compare מֵאַ֫יִן .
H369.k: else, except, fail, (father-)less, be gone, in(-curable), neither, never, no (where), none, nor, (any, thing), not, nothing, to nought, past, un(-searchable), well-nigh, without

H370.d: probably identical with אַ֫יִן in the sense of query (compare אּי ); --where? (only in connection with prepositional prefix, whence).

H371.d: apparently a shortened form of אַ֫יִן ; but (like מֵאַ֫יִן ) an interrogative: is it not?.

H372.d: from אּי and עֵ֫זֶר ; helpless; Iezer, an Israelite.

H373.d: patronymic from אּיעֶ֫זֶר ; an Iezrite or descendant of Iezer.

H374.d: or (shortened) ephah ; of Egyptian derivation; an ephah or measure for grain; hence, a measure in general.

H375.d: from אַי and NONE ; what place?; also (of time) when?; or (of means) how?; --what manner, where.

H376.d: contracted for אֱנוֹשׁ (or perhaps rather from an unused root meaning to be extant); a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation). Compare נָשִׁים .
H376.k: also, another, any (man), a certain, + champion, consent, each, every (one), fellow, (foot-, husband-)man, (good-, great, mighty) man, he, high (degree), him (that is), husband, man(-kind), + none, one, people, person, + steward, what (man) soever, whoso(-ever), worthy

H377.d: denominative from אּישׁ ; to be a man, i.e. act in a manly way.

H378.d: from אּישׁ and בֹּ֫שֶׁת ; man of shame; Ish- Bosheth, a son of King Saul.

H379.d: from אּישׁ and הוֹד ; man of renown; Ishod, an Israelite.

H380.d: diminutive from אּישׁ ; the little man of the eye; the pupil or ball; hence, the middle (of night).

H381.d: from אּישׁ and חָ֫יִל ; man of might; by defect. transcription (2 Sam. 23:20) Iysh-Chay ; as if from אּישׁ and חָי ; living man; Ish-chail (or Ish-chai), an Israelite.

H382.d: from אּישׁ and טוֹב ; man of Tob; Ish-Tob, a place in Palestine.

H383.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to יֵשׁ ; properly, entity; used only as a particle of affirmation, there is.
H383.k: art thou, can, do ye, have, it be, there is (are), X we will not

H384.d: perhaps from אֹ֫שֶׁר and אֵל ; God has arrived; Ithiel, the name of an Israelite, also of a symbolical person.

H385.d: from אּי and תָּמָר ; coast of the palm-tree; Ithamar, a son of Aaron.

H386.d: or (shortened) ethan ; from an unused root (meaning to continue); permanence; hence (concrete) permanent; specifically a chieftain.

H387.d: the same as אֵיתָן ; permanent; Ethan, the name of four Israelites.

H388.d: plural of אֵיתָן ; always with the article; the permanent brooks; Ethanim, the name of a month.

H389.d: akin to אָכֵן ; a particle of affirmation, surely; hence (by limitation) only.
H389.k: also, in any wise, at least, but, certainly, even, howbeit, nevertheless, notwithstanding, only, save, surely, of a surety, truly, verily, + wherefore, yet (but)

H390.d: from an unused root probably meaning to strengthen; a fortress; Accad, a place in Babylon.

H391.d: from כָּזַב ; falsehood; by implication treachery.

H392.d: from אַכְזָב ; deceitful (in the sense of a winter- torrent which fails in summer); Akzib, the name of two places in Palestine.

H393.d: from an unused root (apparently meaning to act harshly); violent; by implication deadly; also (in a good sense) brave.

H396.d: feminine from אָכַל ; something eatable, i.e. food.

H397.d: of uncertain derivation; Akish, a Philistine king.

H398.d: a primitive root; to eat (literally or figuratively)..wise(-deed, plenty), (lay) meat, X quite.
H398.k: X at all, burn up, consume, devour(-er, up), dine, eat(-er, up), feed (with), food, X freely, X in

H400.k: eating, food, meal(-time), meat, prey, victuals

H401.d: or Ukkal ; apparently from אָכַל ; devoured; Ucal, a fancy name.

H403.d: from כּוּן (compare כֵּן ); firmly; figuratively, surely; also (advers.) but.
H403.k: but, certainly, nevertheless, surely, truly, verily

H404.d: a primitive root; apparently meaning to curve (as with a burden); to urge.

H405.d: from אָכַף ; a load; by implication, a stroke (others dignity).

H406.d: from an unused root meaning to dig; a farmer.

H407.d: from כָּשַׁף ; fascination; Acshaph, a place in Palestine.

H408.d: a negative particle (akin to לֹא ); not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing.
H408.k: nay, neither, + never, no, nor, not, nothing (worth), rather than

H410.d: shortened from אָ֫יִל ; strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity). Compare names in "-el."
H410.k: God (god), X goodly, X great, idol, might(-y one), power, strong

H411.d: a demonstrative particle (but only in a plural sense) these or those. Compare אֵ֫לֶּה .

H413.d: (but only used in the shortened constructive form sel ); a primitive particle; properly, denoting motion towards, but occasionally used of a quiescent position, i.e. near, with or among; often in general, to..and, by, concerning, for, from, X hath, in(- to), near, (out) of, over, through, to(-ward), under, unto, upon, whether, with(-in).
H413.k: about, according to, after, against, among, as for, at, because(-fore, -side), both

H414.d: a variation of אֵלָה ; oak; Ela, an Israelite.

H415.d: from אֵל and אֱלֹהִים and יִשְׂרָאֵל ; the mighty god if Jisrael; El-Elohi-Jisrael, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob.

H416.d: from אֵל and בֵּית־אֵל ; the God of Bethel; El-Bethel, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob.

H417.d: from אֵל and גָּבִישׁ ; hail (as if a great pearl).

H418.d: by transposition for אַלְמֻגִּים ; sticks of algum wood.

H419.d: from אֵל and דּוֹד ; God has loved; Eldad, an Israelite.

H420.d: from אֵל and יָדַע ; God of knowledge; Eldaah, a son of Midian.

H421.d: a primitive root (rather identical with אָלָה through the idea of invocation); to bewail.

H422.d: a primitive root; properly, to adjure, i.e. (usually in a bad sense) imprecate.

H424.d: feminine of אָ֫יִל ; an oak or other strong tree.

H425.d: the same as אֵלָה ; Elah, the name of an Edomite, of four Israelites, and also of a place in Palestine.

H428.d: prolonged from אֵל ; these or those.
H428.k: an- (the) other; one sort, so, some, such, them, these (same), they, this, those, thus, which, who(-m)

H430.d: plural of אֱל֫וֹהַּ ; gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative.
H430.k: angels, X exceeding, God (gods)(-dess, -ly), X (very) great, judges, X mighty

H432.d: probably from אַל ; nay, i.e. (softened) if.

H433.d: rarely (shortened) >eloahh probably prolonged (emphat.) from אֵל ; a deity or the Deity. See אֱלֹהִים .

H435.d: probably of foreign derivation; Elul, the sixth Jewish month.

H436.d: prolonged from אָ֫יִל ; an oak or other strong tree. See also אֵילוֹן .

H438.d: the same as אַלּוֹן ; Allon, an Israelite, also a place in Palestine.

H439.d: from אַלּוֹן and a variation of בְּכִית ; oak of weeping; Allon-Bakuth, a monumental tree.

H440.d: or rather (shortened) Eloniy ; patron from אַלּוֹן ; an Elonite or descendant (collectively) of Elon.

H441.d: or (shortened) talluph ; from אָלַף ; familiar; a friend, also gentle; hence, a bullock (as being tame; applied, although masculine, to a cow); and so, a chieftain (as notable, like neat cattle).
H441.k: captain, duke, (chief) friend, governor, guide, ox

H442.d: of uncertain derivation; Alush, a place in the Desert.

H443.d: from אֵל and זָבַד ; God has bestowed; Elzabad, the name of two Israelites.

H444.d: a primitive root; to muddle, i.e. (figuratively and intransitive) to turn (morally) corrupt.

H445.d: from אֵל and חָנַן ; God (is) gracious; Elchanan, an Israelite.

H446.d: from אֵל and אָב ; God of (his) father; Eliab, the name of six Israelites.

H447.d: from אֵל repeated; God of (his) God; Eliel, the name of nine Israelites.

H448.d: or (contraction) ;Eliyathah ; from אֵל and אוּת ; God of (his) consent; Eliathah, an Israelite.

H449.d: from the same as אֶלְדָּד ; God of (his) love; Elidad, an Israelite.

H450.d: from אֵל and יָדַע ; God (is) knowing; Eljada, the name of two Israelites and of an Aramaean leader.

H451.d: from אָלָה (in the original sense of strength); the stout part, i.e. the fat tail of the Oriental sheep.

H452.d: or prolonged Eliyahuw ; from אֵל and יָהּ ; God of Jehovah; Elijah, the name of the famous prophet and of two other Israelites.

H453.d: or (fully) Eliyhuwh ; from אֵל and הוּא ; God of him; Elihu, the name of one of Job's friends, and of three Israelites.

H454.d: or (shortened) Elyow`eynay ; from אֶל and יְהֹוָה and עַ֫יִן ; towards Jehovah (are) my eyes; Eljehoenai or Eljoenai, the name of seven Israelites.

H455.d: from אֵל and חָבָא ; God will hide; Eljachba, an Israelite.

H456.d: from אֵל and חֹ֫רֶף ; God of autumn; Elichoreph, an Israelite.

H457.d: apparently from אַל ; good for nothing, by anal. vain or vanity; specifically an idol.
H457.k: idol, no value, thing of nought

H458.d: from אֵל and מֶ֫לֶך ; God of (the) king; Elimelek, an Israelite.

H459.d: (Aramaic) or shorter oillen ; prolonged from אֵל ; these.

H460.d: from אֵל and יָסַף ; God (is) gatherer; Eljasaph, the name of two Israelites.

H461.d: from אֵל and עֵ֫זֶר ; God of help; Eliezer, the name of a Damascene and of ten Israelites.

H462.d: probably contracted for אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי ; Elienai, an Israelite.

H463.d: from אֵל and עָם ; God of (the) people; Eliam, an Israelite.

H464.d: from אֵל and פָּז ; God of gold; Eliphaz, the name of one of Job's friends, and of a son of Esau.

H465.d: from אֵל and פָּלַל ; God of judgment; Eliphal, an Israelite.

H466.d: from אֵל and פָּלָה ; God of his distinction; Eliphelehu, an Israelite.

H467.d: or (shortened) Elpelet ; from אֵל and פַּלֵּט ; God of deliverance; Eliphelet or Elpelet, the name of six Israelites.

H468.d: from אֵל and צוּר ; God of (the) rock; Elitsur, an Israelite.

H469.d: or (shortened) Eltsaphan ; from אֵל and צָפַן ; God of treasure; Elitsaphan or Eltsaphan, an Israelite.

H470.d: from אֵל and קוֹא ; God of rejection; Elika, an Israelite.

H471.d: from אֵל and קוּם ; God of raising; Eljakim, the name of four Israelites.

H472.d: from אֵל and שֶׁ֫בַע (in the sense of שָׁבַע ); God of (the) oath; Elisheba, the wife of Aaron.

H473.d: probably of foreign derivation; Elishah, a son of Javan.

H474.d: from אֵל and שׁ֫וּעַ ; God of supplication (or of riches); Elishua, the son of King David.

H475.d: from אֵל and שׁוּב ; God will restore; Eljashib, the name of six Israelites.

H476.d: from אֵל and שָׁמַע ; God of hearing; Elishama, the name of seven Israelites.

H477.d: contracted for אֱלִישׁ֫וּעַ .; Elisha, the famous prophet.

H478.d: from אֵל and שָׁפַט ; God of judgment; Elishaphat, an Israelite.

H481.d: a primitive root; to tie fast; hence (of the mouth) to be tongue-tied.
H481.k: bind, be dumb, put to silence

H482.d: from אָלַם ; silence (i.e. mute justice). Compare יוֹנַת אֵ֫לֶם רְחֹקִים .

H484.d: probably of foreign derivation (used thus only in the plural); almug (i.e. probably sandle-wood) sticks. Compare אַלְגּוּמִּים .

H485.d: or (masculine) ealum ; passive participle of אָלַם ; something bound; a sheaf.

H487.d: from אַלָּה and מֶ֫לֶך ; oak of (the) king; Allammelek, a place in Palestine.

H488.d: prolonged from אָלַם in the sense of bereavement; discarded (as a divorced person).

H489.d: from אָלַם as in אַלְמָן ; bereavement.

H490.d: fem of אַלְמָן ; a widow; also a desolate place.

H491.d: feminine of אַלְמָן ; concrete, a widow; abstract, widowhood.

H492.d: from אַלְמֹן in the sense of concealment; some one (i.e. so and so, without giving the name of the person or place).

H493.d: from אֵל and נָעֵם ; God (is his) delight; Elnaam, an Israelite.

H494.d: from אֵל and נָתַן ; God (is the) giver; Elnathan, the name of four Israelites.

H495.d: probably of foreign derivation; Ellasar, an early country of Asia.

H496.d: from אֵל and עוּד ; God has testified; Elad, an Israelite.

H497.d: from אֵל and עָדָה ; God has decked; Eladah, an Israelite.

H498.d: from אֵל and עוּז (in the sense of עֹז ); God (is) defensive; Eluzai, an Israelite.

H499.d: from אֵל and עָזַר ; God (is) helper; Elazar, the name of seven Israelites.

H500.d: or (more properly) GEl aleh ; from אֵל and עָלָה ; God (is) going up; Elale or Elaleh, a place east of the Jordan.

H501.d: from אֵל and עָשָׂה ; God has made; Elasah, the name of four Israelites.

H502.d: a primitive root, to associate with; hence, to learn (and causatively to teach).

H503.d: denominative from אָ֫לֶפ ; causative, to make a thousandfold.

H504.d: from אָלַף ; a family; also (from the sense of yoking or taming) an ox or cow.

H505.d: prop, the same as אֲלָפִים ; hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand.

H507.d: the same as אָ֫לֶפ ; Eleph, a place in Palestine.

H508.d: from אֵל and פָּעַל ; God (is) act; Elpaal, an Israelite.

H510.d: probably from אַל and קוּם ; a non-rising (i.e. resistlessness).

H511.d: from אֵל and קָנָה ; God has obtained; Elkanah, the name of several Israelites.

H512.d: patrial from a name of uncertain derivation; an Elkoshite or native of Elkosh.

H513.d: probably from אֵל and a masculine form of תּוֹלְדוֹת (compare תּוֹלָד ); God (is) generator; Eltolad, a place in Palestine.

H514.d: or (more properly) Eltqeh ; of uncertain derivation; Eltekeh or Elteke, a place in Palestine.

H515.d: from אֵל and תָּקַן ; God (is) straight; Eltekon, a place in Palestine.

H516.d: from אַל and שָׁחַת ; Thou must not destroy; probably the opening words to a popular song.

H517.d: a primitive word; a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively (like אָב ).

H518.d: a primitive particle; used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrog., whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not.
H518.k: (and, can-, doubtless, if, that) (not), + but, either, + except, + more(-over if, than), neither, nevertheless, nor, oh that, or, + save (only, -ing), seeing, since, sith, + surely (no more, none, not), though, + of a truth, + unless, + verily, when, whereas, whether, while, + yet

H519.d: apparently a primitive word; a maid-servant or female slave.

H520.d: prolonged from אֵם ; properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance).
H520.k: cubit, + hundred (by exchange for me'ah ), measure, post

H522.d: the same as אַמָּה ; Ammah, a hill in Palestine.

H523.d: from the same as אֵם ; a collection, i.e. community of persons.

H525.d: from אָמַן , probably in the sense of training; skilled, i.e. an architect (like אָמָּן ).

H526.d: the same as אָמוֹן ; Amon, the name of three Israelites.

H527.d: a variation for הָמוֹן ; a throng of people.

H528.d: of Egyptian derivation; Amon (i.e. Ammon or Amn), a deity of Egypt (used only as an adjunct of נֹא ).

H529.d: from אָמַן ; established, i.e. (figuratively) trusty; also (abstractly) trustworthiness.

H530.d: or (shortened) >emunah feminine of אֵמֻן ; literally firmness; figuratively security; morally fidelity.
H530.k: faith(-ful, -ly, -ness, (man)), set office, stability, steady, truly, truth, verily

H531.d: from אָמַץ ; strong; Amots, an Israelite.

H532.d: an abbrev. for אָמוֹן ; Ami, an Israelite.

H533.d: or (shortened) ammits ; from אָמַץ ; strong or (abstractly) strength.

H534.d: apparently from אָמַר (in the sense of self- exaltation); a summit (of a tree or mountain.

H535.d: a primitive root; to droop; by implication to be sick, to mourn.

H538.d: from אֵם ; gathering-spot; Amam, a place in Palestine.

H539.d: a primitive root; properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain; once (Isa. 30:21; interchangeable with תַאֲמִין ) to go to the right hand.
H539.k: hence, assurance, believe, bring up, establish, + fail, be faithful (of long continuance, stedfast, sure, surely, trusty, verified), nurse, (-ing father), (put), trust, turn to the right

H541.d: denominative from יָמִין ; to take the right hand road. See אָמַן .

H542.d: from אָמַן (in the sense of training); an expert.

H543.d: from אָמַן ; sure; abstract, faithfulness; adverb, truly.

H545.d: feminine of אֹ֫מֶן (in the specific sense of training); tutelage.

H546.d: feminine form of אֹ֫מֶן (in its usual sense); adverb, surely.

H547.d: feminine active participle of אֹ֫מֶן (in the original sense of supporting); a column.

H548.d: feminine of אָמֵן ; something fixed, i.e. a covenant. an allowance.

H549.d: the same as אֲמָנָה ; Amanah, a mountain near Damascus.

H550.d: or Amiynown ; from אָמַן ; faithful; Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David.

H551.k: indeed, no doubt, surely, (it is, of a) true(-ly, -th)

H553.d: a primitive root; to be alert, physically (on foot) or mentally (in courage).
H553.k: confirm, be courageous (of good courage, stedfastly minded, strong, stronger), establish, fortify, harden, increase, prevail, strengthen (self), make strong (obstinate, speed)

H554.d: probably from אָמַץ ; of a strong color, i.e. red (others fleet).

H557.d: from אָמַץ ; strong; Amtsi, an Israelite.

H558.d: or Amatsyahuw ; from אָמַץ and יָהּ ; strength of Jah; Amatsjah, the name of four Israelites.

H559.d: a primitive root; to say (used with great latitude).
H559.k: answer, appoint, avouch, bid, boast self, call, certify, challenge, charge, + (at the, give) command(-ment), commune, consider, declare, demand, X desire, determine, X expressly, X indeed, X intend, name, X plainly, promise, publish, report, require, say, speak (against, of), X still, X suppose, talk, tell, term, X that is, X think, use (speech), utter, X verily, X yet

H561.k: answer, X appointed unto him, saying, speech, word

H563.d: (Aramaic) perhaps from אֲמַר (in the sense of bringing forth); a lamb.

H564.d: from אָמַר ; talkative; Immer, the name of five Israelites.

H565.d: or memrah ; feminine of אֵ֫מֶר , and meaning the same.

H566.d: from אּמֵּר ; wordy; Imri, the name of two Israelites.

H567.d: probably a patronymic from an unused name derived from אָמַר in the sense of publicity, i.e. prominence; thus, a mountaineer; an Emorite, one of the Canaanitish tribes.

H568.d: or prolonged Amaryahuw ; from אָמַר and יָהּ ; Jah has said (i.e. promised); Amarjah, the name of nine Israelites.

H569.d: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; Amraphel, a king of Shinar.

H570.d: time past, i.e. yesterday or last night:--former time, yesterday(-night)

H571.d: contracted from אָמַן ; stability; (figuratively) certainty, truth, trustworthiness.
H571.k: assured(-ly), establishment, faithful, right, sure, true (-ly, -th), verity

H572.d: from מָתַח ; properly, something expansive, i.e. a bag.

H573.d: from אֱמֶת ; veracious; Amittai, an Israelite.

H574.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of מָתְנָ֫יִם ; well-loined (i.e. burly) or mighty.

H575.d: or manah ; contracted from מֵאַ֫יִן ; where?; hence, whither?, when?; also hither and thither.

H577.d: or mannah ; apparent contracted from אַהֲבָה and נָא ; oh now!.

H579.d: a primitive root (perhaps rather identical with אָנָה through the idea of contraction in anguish); to approach; hence, to meet in various senses.
H579.k: befall, deliver, happen, seek a quarrel

H581.d: (Aramaic) or (feminine) inniyn (Aramaic); corresponding to הֵם ; they.

H582.d: from אָנַשׁ ; properly, a mortal (and thus differing from the more dignified אָדָם ); hence, a man in general (singly or collectively). It is often unexpressed in the English versions, especially when used in apposition with another word. Compare אּישׁ .
H582.k: another, X (blood-)thirsty, certain, chap(-man); divers, fellow, X in the flower of their age, husband, (certain, mortal) man, people, person, servant, some ( X of them), + stranger, those, + their trade

H583.d: the same as אֱנוֹשׁ ; Enosh, a son of Seth; --Enos.

H586.d: (Aramaic) or ganachnah (Aramaic); corresponding to אֲנַ֫חְנוּ ; we.

H588.d: probably from the same root as נַ֫חַר ; a gorge or narrow pass; Anacharath, a place in Palestine.

H589.k: I, (as for) me, mine, myself, we, X which, X who

H590.d: probably from אָנָה (in the sense of conveyance); -a ship or (collectively)a fleet.

H593.d: from אָנָה and עָם ; groaning of (the) people; Aniam, an Israelite.

H594.d: probably from an unused root meaning to be narrow; according to most a plumb-line, and to others a hook.

H596.d: a primitive root; to mourn, i.e. complain.

H598.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָנַס ; figuratively, to distress.

H599.d: a primitive root; to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged.

H600.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַף (only in the plural as a singular); the face.

H601.d: from אָנַף ; an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility).

H604.d: the same as אֲנָקָה ; some kind of lizard, probably the gecko (from its wail).

H605.d: a primitive root; to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy.

H606.d: (Aramaic) or renash (Aramaic); corresponding to אֱנוֹשׁ ; a man.

H609.d: of uncertain derivation; Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite.

H610.d: from סוּך ; anointed, i.e. an oil-flask.

H612.d: from אָסַר ; a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner).

H614.d: or maciph ; from אָסַף ; gathered, i.e. (abstractly) a gathering in of crops.

H615.d: from אָסַר ; bound, i.e. a captive.

H617.d: the same as אַסִּיר ; prisoner; Assir, the name of two Israelites.

H618.d: from an unused root meaning to heap together; a storehouse (only in the plural).

H619.d: of uncertain derivation; Asnah, one of the Nethinim.

H620.d: of foreign derivation; Osnappar, an Assyrian king.

H621.d: of Egyptian derivation; Asenath, the wife of Joseph.

H622.d: a primitive root; to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.).
H622.k: assemble, bring, consume, destroy, felch, gather (in, together, up again), X generally, get (him), lose, put all together, receive, recover (another from leprosy), (be) rereward, X surely, take (away, into, up), X utterly, withdraw

H623.d: from אָסַף ; collector; Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first.

H624.d: passive participle of אָסַף ; collected (only in the plural), i.e. a collection of offerings).

H626.d: from אָסַף ; a collection of people (only adverbial).

H627.d: fem of אֲסֻפִּים .; a collection of (learned) men (only in the plural).

H628.d: by reduplication from אֲסֻפִּים ; gathered up together, i.e. a promiscuous assemblage (of people).

H630.d: of Persian derivation; Aspatha, a son of Haman.

H631.d: a primitive root; to yoke or hitch; by analogy, to fasten in any sense, to join battle.
H631.k: bind, fast, gird, harness, hold, keep, make ready, order, prepare, prison(-er), put in bonds, set in array, tie

H632.d: or riccar ; from אָסַר ; an obligation or vow (of abstinence).

H633.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אּסָּר in a legal sense; an interdict.

H634.d: of foreign derivation; Esar- chaddon, an Assyrian king.

H635.d: of Persian derivation; Ester, the Jewish heroine.

H636.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֵץ ; a tree or wood.

H637.d: a primitive particle; meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though.
H637.k: also, + although, and (furthermore, yet), but, even, + how much less (more, rather than), moreover, with, yea

H639.d: from אָנַף ; properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire.
H639.k: anger(-gry), + before, countenance, face, + forebearing, forehead, + (long-)suffering, nose, nostril, snout, X worthy, wrath

H640.d: a primitive root (rather a denominative from אֵפוֹד ); to gird on (the ephod).

H641.d: the same as אֵפוֹד shortened; Ephod, an Israelite.

H642.d: feminine of אֵפוֹד ; a girding on (of the ephod); hence, generally, a plating (of metal).

H643.d: apparently of foreign derivation; a pavilion or palace-tent.

H644.d: a primitive root; to cook, especially to bake.

H645.d: or hephowe ; from NONE ; strictly a demonstrative particle, here; but used of time, now or then:--here, now, where?

H646.d: rarely oephod ; probably of foreign derivation; a girdle; specifically the ephod or high-priest's shoulder- piece; also generally, an image.

H647.d: perhaps from פּ֫וּחַ ; breeze; Aphiach, an Israelite.

H648.d: from the same as אָפֵל (in the sense of weakness); unripe.

H649.d: dual of אַף ; two nostrils; Appajim, an Israelite.

H650.d: from אָסַף ; properly, containing, i.e. a tube; also a bed or valley of a stream; also a strong thing or a hero.
H650.k: brook, channel, mighty, river, + scale, stream, strong piece

H651.d: from an unused root meaning to set as the sun; dusky.

H652.d: from the same as אָפֵל ; dusk.

H653.d: feminine of אָפֵל ; duskiness, figuratively, misfortune; concrete, concealment.

H654.d: from פָּלַל ; judge; Ephlal, an Israelite.

H655.d: from an unused root meaning to revolve; a turn, i.e. a season.

H656.d: a primitive root; to disappear, i.e. cease.
H656.k: be clean gone (at an end, brought to nought), fail

H657.d: from אָפֵס ; cessation, i.e. an end (especially of the earth); often used adverb, no further; also (like פָּעַל ) the ankle (in the dual), as being the extremity of the leg or foot.
H657.k: ankle, but (only), end, howbeit, less than nothing, nevertheless (where), no, none (beside), not (any, -withstanding), thing of nought, save(-ing), there, uttermost part, want, without (cause)

H658.d: from אָ֫פֶס and the plural of דָּם ; boundary of blood-drops; Ephes-Dammim, a place in Palestine.

H659.d: from an unused root probably meaning to breathe; properly, a breath, i.e. nothing.

H660.d: from אָ֫פַע (in the sense of hissing); an asp or other venomous serpent.

H662.d: a primitive root; to contain, i.e. (reflex.) abstain.

H663.d: or Aphiyq ; from אָפַק (in the sense of strength); fortress; Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine.

H664.d: feminine of אֲפֵק ; fortress; Aphekah, a place in Palestine.

H665.d: from an unused root meaning to bestrew; ashes.

H666.d: from the same as אֵ֫פֶר (in the sense of covering); a turban.

H667.d: from פָּרַח (in the sense of bursting the shell); the brood of a bird.

H668.d: probably of Egyptian derivation; a palanquin.

H669.d: dual of masculine form of אֶפְרָת ; double fruit; Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory.

H670.d: (Aramaic) of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria.

H671.d: (Aramaic) or Apharcathkay (Aramaic); of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe.

H672.d: or Ephrathah ; from פָּרָה ; fruitfulness; Ephrath, another name for Bethlehem; once (Psa. 132:6) perhaps for Ephraim; also of an Israelitish woman.

H673.d: patrial form אֶפְרָת ; an Ephrathite or an Ephraimite.

H674.d: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; revenue; others at the last.

H675.d: or Etsbon ; of uncertain derivation; Etsbon, the name of two Israelites.

H676.d: from the same as צֶ֫בַע (in the sense of grasping); something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe.

H678.d: from אָצַל (in its secondary sense of separation); an extremity (Isa. 41:9), also a noble.

H679.d: from אָצַל (in its primary sense of uniting); a joint of the hand (i.e. knuckle); also (according to some) a party-wall (Ezek. 41:8).

H680.d: a primitive root; properly, to join; used only as a denominative from אֵ֫צֶל ; to separate; hence, to select, refuse, contract.

H681.d: from אָצַל (in the sense of joining); a side; (as a preposition) near. See also בֵּית הָאֵ֫צֶל .

H682.d: from אָצַל ; noble; Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine.

H683.d: from אָצַל and יָהּ prolonged; Jah has reserved; Atsaljah, an Israelite.

H684.d: from an unused root probably meaning to be strong; strength (i.e. strong); Otsem, the name of two Israelites.

H685.d: a variation from צְעָדָה ; properly, a step- chain; by analogy, a bracelet.

H686.d: a primitive root; to store up.

H687.d: from אָצַר ; treasure; Etser, an Idumaean.

H688.d: from קִדָּה ; burning, i.e. a carbuncle or other fiery gem.

H689.d: probably from אָנַק ; slender, i.e. the ibex.

H690.d: probably for אֲרִי ; lion; Ara, an Israelite.

H692.d: from אֶרְאֵל ; heroic; Areli (or an Arelite, collectively), an Israelite and his descendants.

H694.d: from אָרַב ; ambush; Arab, a place in Palestine.

H697.d: from רָבָה ; a locust (from its rapid increase).

H698.d: feminine of אֹ֫רֶב (only in the plural); ambuscades.

H699.d: feminine participle passive of אָרַב (as if for lurking); a lattice; (by implication) a window, dove-cot (because of the pigeon-holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water).

H700.d: plural of אֲרֻבָּה ; Arubboth, a place in Palestine.

H701.d: patrial from אֲרָב ; an Arbite or native of Arab.

H704.d: the same as אַרְבַּע ; Arba, one of the Anakim.

H707.d: a primitive root; to plait or weave.

H708.d: from אָרַג ; a weaving; a braid; also a shuttle.

H709.d: from the same as רְגָבִים ; stony; Argob, a district of Palestine.

H712.d: perhaps from רָגַז (in the sense of being suspended), a box (as a pannier).

H713.d: of foreign origin; purple (the color or the dyed stuff).

H714.d: from an unused root probably meaning to wander; fugitive; Ard, the name of two Israelites.

H715.d: from the same as אָרְדְּ ; roaming; Ardon, an Israelite.

H716.d: patronymic from אָרְדְּ ; an Ardite (collectively) or descendant of Ard.

H719.d: probably from רוּד ; a refuge for the roving; Arvad, an island-city of Palestine.

H720.d: an orthographical variation of אַרְוַד ; fugitive; Arod, an Israelite.

H721.d: patrial from אַרְוַד ; an Arvadite or citizen of Arvad.

H722.d: patronymic from אַרְוָדִי ; an Arodite or descendant of Arod.

H723.d: or rarayah ; from אָרָה (in the sense of feeding); a herding-place for an animal.

H724.d: or rarukah ; feminine passive participle of 748 (in the sense of restoring to soundness); wholeness (literally or figuratively).

H725.d: a variation of רוּמָה ; height; Arumah, a place in Palestine.

H726.d: a clerical error for אֲדֹמִי ; an Edomite (as in the margin).

H727.d: or laron ; from אָרָה (in the sense of gathering); a box.

H728.d: or (by transposition) Owrnah ; or Arniyah ; all by orthographical variation for אָרְנָן ; Aravnah (or Arnijah or Ornah), a Jebusite.

H729.d: a primitive root; to be firm; used only in the passive participle as a denominative from אָ֫רֶז ; of cedar.

H730.d: from אָרַז ; a cedar tree (from the tenacity of its roots).

H733.d: from אָרַח ; way faring; Arach, the name of three Israelites: Arah.

H734.d: from אָרַח ; a well-trodden road (literally or figuratively); also a caravan.
H734.k: manner, path, race, rank, traveller, troop, (by-, high-)way

H736.d: feminine active participle of אָרַח ; a caravan.

H737.d: feminine passive participle of אָרַח (in the sense of appointing); a ration of food.

H738.d: or (prolonged) earyeh ; from אָרָה (in the sense of violence); a lion.

H739.d: or ( arilel ; from אֲרִי and אֵל ; lion of God; i.e. heroic.

H740.d: the same as אֲרִיאֵל ; Ariel, a symbolical name for Jerusalem, also the name of an Israelite.

H741.d: either by transposition for אֲרִיאֵל or, more probably, an orthographical variation for הַרְאֵל ; the altar of the temple.

H742.d: of Persian origin; Aridai, a son of Haman.

H743.d: of Persian origin; Aridatha, a son of Haman.

H745.d: the same as אֲרִי ; lion; Arjeh, an Israelite.

H746.d: of foreign origin; Arjok, the name of two Babylonians.

H747.d: of Persian origin; Arisai, a son of Haman.

H748.d: a primitive root; to be (causative, make) long (literally or figuratively).
H748.k: defer, draw out, lengthen, (be, become, make, pro-)long, + (out-, over-)live, tarry (long)

H749.d: (Aramaic) properly, corresponding to אָרַך , but used only in the sense of reaching to a given point; to suit.

H751.d: from אָרַך ; length; Erek, a place in Babylon.

H755.d: (Aramaic) from an unused root corresponding to רָכַב (in the sense of bending the knee); the knee.

H756.d: (Aramaic) patrial from אֶ֫רֶך ; an Arkevite (collectively) or native of Erek.

H757.d: patrial from another place (in Palestine) of similar name with אֶ֫רֶך ; an Arkite or native of Erek.

H758.d: from the same as אַרְמוֹן ; the highland; Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of the son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite.

H759.d: from an unused root (meaning to be elevated); a citadel (from its height). Compare הַרְמ֫וֹנָה .

H760.d: from אֲרָם and צוֹבָה ; Aram of Tsoba (or Coele-Syria).

H761.d: patrial from אֲרָם ; an Aramite or Aramaean.

H762.k: in the Syrian language (tongue), in Syriac

H763.d: from אֲרָם and the dual of נָהָר ; Aram of (the) two rivers (Euphrates and Tigris) or Mesopotamia.

H764.d: from אַרְמוֹן ; palatial; Armoni, an Israelite.

H765.d: from רָנַן ; stridulous; Aran, an Edomite.

H766.d: from the same as אֲרָן (in the sense of strength); the ash tree (from its toughness).

H767.d: the same as אֹ֫רֶן ; Oren, an Israelite.

H769.d: or Arnon ; from רָנַן ; a brawling stream; the Arnon, a river east of the Jordan, also its territory.

H770.d: probably from the same as אַרְנוֹן ; noisy; Arnan, an Israelite.

H771.d: probably from אֹ֫רֶן ; strong; Ornan, a Jebusite. See NONE .

H772.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָ֫רֶץ ; the earth; by implication (figuratively) low.

H774.d: from רָפַד ; spread out; Arpad, a place in Syria.

H775.d: probably of foreign origin; Arpakshad, a son of Noah; also the region settled by him.

H776.d: from an unused root probably meaning to be firm; the earth (at large, or partitively a land).
H776.k: X common, country, earth, field, ground, land, X natins, way, + wilderness, world

H777.d: from אָ֫רֶץ ; earthiness; Artsa, an Israelite.

H778.d: (Aramaic) by transmutation for אַרְעָא ; the earth.

H780.d: of foreign origin; Ararat (or rather Armenia).

H781.d: a primitive root; to engage for matrimony.

H782.d: from אָרַשׂ (in the sense of desiring to possess); a longing for.

H783.d: or Artachshasht ; or by permutation Artachshactu ; of foreign origin; Artachshasta (or Artaxerxes), a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings.

H784.d: a primitive word; fire (literally or figuratively).

H786.d: identical (in origin and formation) with אֵשׁ ; entity, used only adverbially, there is or are. Compare יֵשׁ .

H787.d: (Aramaic) corresponding (by transposition and abbreviation) to אָשְׁוִיֹּת ; a foundation.

H788.d: probably from the same as שֹׁ֫בֶל ; flowing; Ashbel, an Israelite.

H789.d: patronymic from אַשְׁבֵּל ; an Ashbelite (collectively) or descendant of Ashbel.

H790.d: probably from the same as שֶׁבְנָה ; vigorous; Eshban, an Idumaean.

H791.d: from שָׁבַע ; adjurer; Asbea, an Israelite.

H792.d: from אּישׁ and בַּ֫עַל ; man of Baal; Eshbaal (or Ishbosheth), a son of Saul.

H793.d: from an unused root meaning to pour; an outpouring.

H795.d: from שָׁדַד ; ravager; Ashdod, a place in Palestine.

H796.d: patrial from אַשְׁדּוֹד ; an Ashdodite (often collectively) or inhabitant of Asdod.

H797.d: feminine of אַשְׁדּוֹדִי ; (only adverb) in the language of Ashdod.

H798.d: from the plural of אֲשֵׁדוֹת and פִּסְגָּה with the article interposed; ravines of the Pisgah; Ashdoth- Pisgah, a place east of the Jordan.

H799.d: from אֵשׁ and דָּת ; a fire-law.

H801.d: the same as מֵאֵשׁ , but used in a liturgical sense; properly, a burnt-offering; but occasionally of any sacrifice.

H802.d: feminine of אּישׁ or אֱנוֹשׁ ; irregular plural nashiym ; a woman (used in the same wide sense as אֱנוֹשׁ ). Often unexpressed in English.
H802.k: (adulter)ess, each, every, female, X many, + none, one, + together, wife, woman

H803.d: feminine passive participle from an unused root meaning to found; foundation.

H804.d: or Ashshur ; apparently from אָשַׁר (in the sense of successful); Ashshur, the second son of Shem; also his descendants and the country occupied by them (i.e. Assyria), its region and its empire. See אֲשׁוּר .

H805.d: or Ashshuwriy ; from a patrial word of the same form as אַשּׁוּר ; an Ashurite (collectively) or inhabitant of Ashur, a district in Palestine.

H806.d: probably from שָׁחַר ; black; Ashchur, an Israelite.

H807.d: of foreign origin; Ashima, a deity of Hamath.

H808.d: from the same as אֵשׁ (in the sense of pressing down firmly; compare אָשְׁוִיֹּת ); a (ruined) foundation.

H809.d: feminine of אֲשִׁישֵׁי ; something closely pressed together, i.e. a cake of raisins or other comfits.

H810.d: from an unused root (probably meaning to bunch together); a testicle (as a lump).

H811.d: or meshkol ; probably prolonged from אָ֫שֶׁך ; a bunch of grapes or other fruit.

H812.d: the same as אֶשְׁכּוֹל ; Eshcol, the name of an Amorite, also of a valley in Palestine.

H813.d: of foreign origin; Ashkenaz, a Japhethite, also his descendants.

H815.d: from a root of uncertain signification; a tamarisk tree; by extension, a grove of any kind.

H816.d: or mashem ; a primitive root; to be guilty; by implication to be punished or perish.
H816.k: X certainly, be(-come, made) desolate, destroy, X greatly, be(-come, found, hold) guilty, offend (acknowledge offence), trespass

H817.d: from אָשַׁם ; guilt; by implication, a fault; also a sin-offering.

H818.d: from אָשַׁם ; guilty; hence, presenting a sin- offering.

H819.d: feminine of אָשָׁם ; guiltiness, a fault, the presentation of a sin-offering.

H821.d: or bashmuwrah ; or -ashmoreth ; (feminine) from שָׁמַר ; a night watch.

H822.d: apparently from an unused root (probably meaning to leave interstices); A latticed window.

H823.d: probably a variation for יְשָׁנָה ; Ashnah, the name of two places in Palestine.

H824.d: from שָׁעַן ; support; Eshan, a place in Palestine.

H825.d: from an unused root (probably meaning to lisp, i.e. practice enchantment); a conjurer.

H827.d: perhaps (feminine) from the same as אַשָּׁפִים (in the sense of covering); a quiver or arrow-case.

H828.d: of foreign origin; Ashpenaz, a Babylonian eunuch.

H829.d: of uncertain derivation; a measured portion.

H830.d: or uashpowth ; or (contraction) shphoth ; plural of a noun of the same form as אַשְׁפָּה , from שָׁפָה (in the sense of scraping); a heap of rubbish or filth.

H831.d: probably from שָׁקַל in the sense of weighing-place (i.e. mart); Ashkelon, a place in Palestine.

H832.d: patrial from אַשְׁקְלוֹן ; Ashkelonite (collectively) or inhabitant of Ashkelon.

H833.d: or rasher ; a primitive root; to be straight (used in the widest sense, especially to be level, right, happy); figuratively, to go forward, be honest, proper.
H833.k: (call, be) bless(-ed, happy), go, guide, lead, relieve

H834.d: a primitive relative pronoun (of every gender and number); who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc. As it is indeclinable, it is often accompanied by the personal pronoun expletively, used to show the connection.
H834.k: X after, X alike, as (soon as), because, X every, for, + forasmuch, + from whence, + how(-soever), X if, (so) that ((thing) which, wherein), X though, + until, + whatsoever, when, where (+ -as, -in, -of, -on, -soever, -with), which, whilst, + whither(- soever), who(-m, -soever, -se)

H835.d: from אָשַׁר ; happiness; only in masculine plural construction as interjection, how happy!.

H836.d: from אָשַׁר , happy; Asher, a son of Jacob, and the tribe descended from him, with its territory; also a place in Palestine:--Asher

H838.d: or ashshur ; from אָשַׁר in the sense of going; a step.

H839.d: contracted for תְּאַשּׁוּר ; the cedar tree or some other light elastic wood.

H840.d: by orthographical variation from אָשַׁר and אֵל ; right of God; Asarel, an Israelite.

H841.d: from the same as אֲשַׂרְאֵל ; right toward God; Asarelah, an Israelite. Compare יְשַׂרְאֵ֫לָה .

H842.d: or masheyrah ; from אָשַׁר ; happy; Asherah (or Astarte) a Phoenician goddess; also an image of the same. Compare עַשְׁתֹּ֫רֶת .

H843.d: patronymic from אָשֵׁר ; an Asherite (collectively) or descendant of Asher.

H844.d: an orthographical variation for אֲשַׂרְאֵל ; Asriel, the name of two Israelites.

H845.d: patronymic from אַשְׂרִיאֵל ; an Asrielite (collectively) or descendant of Asriel.

H846.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to אָשַׁר ; a wall (from its uprightness).

H847.d: or Eshtafowl ; probably from שָׁאַל ; intreaty; Eshtaol, a place in Palestine.

H848.d: patrial from אֶשְׁתָּאֹל ; an Eshtaolite (collectively) or inhabitant of Eshtaol.

H849.d: (Aramaic) from שְׁדַר (in a bad sense); rebellion.

H850.d: probably from the same as שׁוּנִי ; restful; Eshton, an Israelite.

H851.d: or Eshtmowam ; or Eshtmoh ; from שָׁמַע (in the sense of obedience); Eshtemoa or Eshtemoh, a place in Palestine.

H853.d: apparent contracted from אוֹת in the demonstrative sense of entity; properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely).

H854.d: probably from אָנָה ; properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc. Often with another prepositional prefix.
H854.k: against, among, before, by, for, from, in(-to), (out) of, with

H855.d: of uncertain derivation; a hoe or other digging implement.

H856.d: from אוֹת and בַּ֫עַל ; with Baal; Ethbaal, a Phoenician king.

H857.d: or matha ; a primitive root (collateral to 225 contraction); to arrive.

H859.d: or (shortened) aatta ; or wath ; feminine (irregular) sometimes nattiy ; plural masculine attem ; feminine atten ; or oattenah ; or fattennah ; a primitive pronoun of the second person; thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you.

H860.d: probably from the same as אֵיתָן (in the sense of patience); a female donkey (from its docility).

H861.d: (Aramaic) probably from the corresponding to אֵשׁ ; probably a fire-place, i.e. furnace.

H862.d: or mattiyq ; from נָתַק in the sense of decreasing; a ledge or offset in a building.

H863.d: or Iythay ; from אוֹת ; near; Ittai or Ithai, the name of a Gittite and of an Israelite.

H864.d: of Egyptian derivation; Etham, a place in the Desert.

H865.d: or tithmowl ; or methmuwl ; probably from אוֹת or אוֹת and מוֹאל ; heretofore; definitely yesterday.
H865.k: + before (that) time, + heretofore, of late (old), + times past, yester(day)

H866.d: from תָּנָה ; a present (as the price of harlotry).

H867.d: perhaps from אֶתְנָה ; munificence; Ethni, an Israelite.

H868.d: the same as אֶתְנָה ; a gift (as the price of harlotry or idolatry).

H869.d: the same as אֶתְנָן in the sense of אֶתְנִי ; Ethnan, an Israelite.

H870.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of אֲתָרִים ; a place; (adverb) after.

H871.d: plural from an unused root (probably meaning to step); places; Atharim, a place near Palestine.

H872.d: from בּוֹא ; an entrance to a building.

H874.d: a primitive root; to dig; by analogy, to engrave; figuratively, to explain.

H875.d: from בָּאַר ; a pit; especially a well.

H876.d: the same as בְּאֵר ; Beer, a place in the Desert, also one in Palestine.

H878.d: from בְּאֵר ; a well; Beera, an Israelite.

H879.d: from בְּאֵר and the plural of אֵל ; well of heroes; Beer-Elim, a place in the Desert.

H880.d: the same as בְּאֵרָא ; Beerah, an Israelite.

H881.d: feminine plural of בְּאֵר ; wells; Beeroth, a place in Palestine.

H882.d: from בְּאֵר ; fountained; Beeri, the name of a Hittite and of an Israelite.

H883.d: from בְּאֵר and חָי (with prefix) and רֹאֶה ; well of a living (One) my Seer; Beer-Lachai-Roi, a place in the Desert.

H884.d: from בְּאֵר and שֶׁ֫בַע (in the sense of שָׁבַע ); well of an oath; Beer-Sheba, a place in Palestine.

H885.d: from the feminine plural of בְּאֵר , and the plural contraction of בֵּן , and יַעֲקָן ; wells of (the) sons of Jaakan; Beeroth-Bene-Jaakan, a place in the Desert.
H885.k: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan

H886.d: patrial from בְּאֵרוֹת ; a Beerothite or inhabitant of Beeroth.

H887.d: a primitive root; to smell bad; figuratively, to be offensive morally.
H887.k: (make to) be abhorred (had in abomination, loathsome, odious), (cause a, make to) stink(-ing savour), X utterly

H890.d: feminine of בְּאֹשׁ ; stink-weed or any other noxious or useless plant.

H892.d: feminine active participle of an unused root meaning to hollow out; something hollowed (as a gate), i.e. pupil of the eye.

H893.d: probably of foreign origin; Bebai, an Israelite.

H894.d: from בָּלַל ; confusion; Babel (i.e. Babylon), including Babylonia and the Babylonian empire.

H898.d: a primitive root; to cover (with a garment); figuratively, to act covertly; by implication, to pillage.
H898.k: deal deceitfully (treacherously, unfaithfully), offend, transgress(-or), (depart), treacherous (dealer, -ly, man), unfaithful(-ly, man), X very

H899.d: from בָּגַד ; a covering, i.e. clothing; also treachery or pillage.
H899.k: apparel, cloth(-es, ing), garment, lap, rag, raiment, robe, X very (treacherously), vesture, wardrobe

H900.d: feminine plural active participle of בָּגַד ; treacheries.

H902.d: probably of foreign origin; Bigvai, an Israelite.

H903.d: of Persian derivation; Bigtha, a eunuch of Xerxes.

H904.d: or Bigthanad ; of similar derivation to בִּגְתָא ; Bigthan or Bigthana, a eunuch of Xerxes.

H905.d: from בָּדַד ; properly, separation; by implication, a part of the body, branch of a tree, bar for carrying; figuratively, chief of a city; especially (with prepositional prefix) as an adverb, apart, only, besides.
H905.k: alone, apart, bar, besides, branch, by self, of each alike, except, only, part, staff, strength

H906.d: perhaps from בָּדַד (in the sense of divided fibres); flaxen thread or yarn; hence, a linen garment.

H907.d: from בָּדָא ; a brag or lie; also a liar.

H909.d: a primitive root; to divide, i.e. (reflex.) be solitary.

H911.d: from בָּדַד ; separation; Bedad, an Edomite.

H912.d: probably a shortened form עֹבַדְיָה ; servant of Jehovah; Bedejah, an Israelite.

H913.d: from בָּדַל ; alloy (because removed by smelting); by analogy, tin.

H914.d: a primitive root; to divide (in variation senses literally or figuratively, separate, distinguish, differ, select, etc.).
H914.k: (make, put) difference, divide (asunder), (make) separate (self, -ation), sever (out), X utterly

H916.d: probably from בָּדַל ; something in pieces, i.e. bdellium, a (fragrant) gum (perhaps amber); others a pearl.

H917.d: probably shortened for עַבְדּוֹן ; servile; Bedan, the name of two Israelites.

H918.d: a primitive root; to gap open; used only as a denominative from בֶּ֫דֶק ; to mend a breach.

H919.d: from בָּדַק ; a gap or leak (in a building or a ship).

H920.d: probably from דָּקַר with a prepositional prefix; by stabbing, i.e. assassin; Bidkar, an Israelite.

H921.d: (Aramaic) corresponding (by transposition) to פָּרַד ; to scatter.

H922.d: from an unused root (meaning to be empty); a vacuity, i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin.

H923.d: from an unused root (probably meaning to glisten); white marble or perhaps alabaster.

H924.d: (Aramaic) from בְּהַל ; a hurry; only adverb, hastily.

H925.d: from an unused root (meaning to be bright); shining.

H926.d: a primitive root; to tremble inwardly (or palpitate), i.e. (figuratively) be (causative, make) (suddenly) alarmed or agitated; by implication to hasten anxiously.
H926.k: be (make) affrighted (afraid, amazed, dismayed, rash), (be, get, make) haste(-n, -y, -ily), (give) speedy(-ily), thrust out, trouble, vex

H927.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to בָּהַל ; to terrify, hasten.

H929.d: from an unused root (probably meaning to be mute); properly, a dumb beast; especially any large quadruped or animal (often collective).

H930.d: in form a plural or בְּהֵמָה , but really a singular of Egyptian derivation; a water-ox, i.e. the hippopotamus or Nile- horse.

H931.d: from an unused root apparently meaning to be thick; the thumb of the hand or great toe of the foot.

H932.d: an orthographical variation of בֹּ֫הֶן ; thumb, Bohan, an Israelite.

H933.d: from an unused root meaning to be pale; white scurf.

H934.d: feminine active participle of the same as בָּהִיר ; a whitish spot on the skin.
