H2604.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָנַן ; to favor or (causatively) to entreat.

H2605.d: from חָנַן ; favor; Chanan, the name of seven Israelites.

H2606.d: from חָנַן and אֵל ; God has favored; Chananel, probably an Israelite, from whom a tower of Jerusalem was named.

H2607.d: from חָנַן ; gracious; Chanani, the name of six Israelites.

H2608.d: or Chananyahuw ; from חָנַן and יָהּ ; Jah has favored; Chananjah, the name of thirteen Israelites.

H2609.d: of Egyptian derivation; Chanes, a place in Egypt.

H2610.d: a primitive root; to soil, especially in a moral sense.
H2610.k: corrupt, defile, X greatly, pollute, profane

H2611.d: from חָנֵף ; soiled (i.e. with sin), impious.

H2612.d: from חָנֵף ; moral filth, i.e. wickedness.

H2614.d: a primitive root (compare חָנַך ); to be narrow; by implication, to throttle, or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope).

H2615.d: probably from חָנַן ; favored; Channathon, a place in Palestine.

H2616.d: a primitive root; properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only (compare חָנַן ) in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind; also (by euphem. (compare בָּרַך ), but rarely) to reprove.
H2616.k: shew self merciful, put to shame

H2617.d: from חָסַד ; kindness; by implication (towards God) piety: rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty.
H2617.k: favour, good deed(-liness, -ness), kindly, (loving-)kindness, merciful (kindness), mercy, pity, reproach, wicked thing

H2618.d: the same as חָ֫סֶד : favor; Chesed, an Israelite.

H2619.d: from חָ֫סֶד and יָהּ ; Jah has favored: Chasadjah, an Israelite.

H2620.d: a primitive root; to flee for protection (compare בָּטַח ); figuratively, to confide in.

H2621.d: from חָסָה ; hopeful; Chosah, an Israelite; also a place in Palestine.

H2623.d: from חָסַד ; properly, kind, i.e. (religiously) pious (a saint).

H2624.d: feminine of חָסִיד ; the kind (maternal) bird, i.e. a stork.

H2625.d: from חָסַל ; the ravager, i.e. a locust.

H2626.d: from חָסַן ; properly, firm, i.e. (by implication) mighty.

H2627.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָסֵר ; deficient.

H2628.d: a primitive root; to eat off.

H2629.d: a primitive root; to muzzle; by analogy, to stop the nose.

H2630.d: a primitive root; properly, to (be) compact; by implication, to hoard.

H2631.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָסַן ; to hold in occupancy.

H2635.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of מְחֻסְפָּס ; a clod.

H2636.d: reduplicated from an unused root meaning apparently to peel; a shred or scale.

H2637.d: a primitive root; to lack; by implication, to fail, want, lessen.
H2637.k: be abated, bereave, decrease, (cause to) fail, (have) lack, make lower, want

H2638.k: destitute, fail, lack, have need, void, want

H2643.d: from חָפַף (in the moral sense of covered from soil); pure.

H2644.d: an orthographical variation of חָפָה ; properly, to cover, i.e. (in a sinister sense) to act covertly.

H2645.d: a primitive root (compare חָפָא , חָפַף ); to cover; by implication, to veil, to encase, protect.

H2647.d: the same as חֻפָּה ; Chuppah, an Israelite.

H2648.d: a primitive root; properly, to start up suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, to fear.

H2650.d: plural of חֻפָּה (compare חוּפָם ); Chuppim, an Israelite.

H2651.d: from an unused root of uncertain signification; a fist (only in the dual).

H2652.d: from חָפְנַ֫יִם ; perhaps pugilist; Chophni, an Israelite.

H2653.d: a primitive root (compare חָפָה , יָחֵף ); to cover (in protection).

H2654.d: a primitive root; properly, to incline to; by implication (literally but rarely) to bend; figuratively, to be pleased with, desire.
H2654.k: X any at all, (have, take) delight, desire, favour, like, move, be (well) pleased, have pleasure, will, would

H2655.k: delight in, desire, favour, please, have pleasure, whosoever would, willing, wish

H2656.d: from חָפֵץ ; pleasure; hence (abstractly) desire; concretely, a valuable thing; hence (by extension) a matter (as something in mind).
H2656.k: acceptable, delight(-some), desire, things desired, matter, pleasant(-ure), purpose, willingly

H2657.d: from חֵ֫פֶץ with suffixes; my delight (is) in her; Cheptsi-bah, a fanciful name for Palestine.

H2658.d: a primitive root; properly, to pry into; by implication, to delve, to explore.

H2659.d: a primitive root (perhaps rath. the same as חָפַר through the idea of detection): to blush; figuratively, to be ashamed, disappointed; causatively, to shame, reproach.
H2659.k: be ashamed, be confounded, be brought to confusion (unto shame), come (be put to) shame, bring reproach

H2660.d: from חָפַר or חָפֵר ; a pit of shame; Chepher, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites.

H2661.d: from חָפַר ; a hole; only in connection with פֵּרוֹת , which ought rather to be joined as one word, thus chapharperah ; by reduplication from חָפַר ; a burrower, i.e. probably a rat.

H2662.d: patronymically from חֵ֫פֶר ; a Chephrite (collectively) or descendants of Chepher.

H2663.d: dual of חֵ֫פֶר ; double pit; Chapharajim, a place in Palestine.

H2664.d: a primitive root; to seek; causatively, to conceal oneself (i.e. let be sought), or mask.
H2664.k: change, (make) diligent (search), disquise self, hide, search (for, out)

H2665.d: from חָפַשׂ ; something covert, i.e. a trick.

H2666.d: a primitive root; to spread loose; figuratively, to manumit.

H2667.d: from חָפַשׁ ; something spread loosely, i.e. a carpet.

H2669.d: and chophshiyth ; from חָפַשׁ ; prostration by sickness (with בָּ֫יִת , a hospital).

H2670.d: from חָפַשׁ ; exempt (from bondage, tax or care).

H2671.d: from חָצַץ ; properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunder-bolt; (by interchange for עֵץ ) the shaft of a spear.
H2671.k: + archer, arrow, dart, shaft, staff, wound

H2672.d: or chatseb ; a primitive root; to cut or carve (wood), stone or other material); by implication, to hew, split, square, quarry, engrave.
H2672.k: cut, dig, divide, grave, hew (out, -er), made, mason

H2673.d: a primitive root (compare זֵד )); to cut or split in two; to halve:--divide, X live out half, reach to the midst, participle

H2674.d: a collective form of חָצֵר ; village; Chatsor, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine and of one in Arabia.

H2675.d: from חָצוֹר and a Aramaizing form of the feminine of חָדָשׁ (compare חֲדַת ); new Chatsor, a place in Palestine.

H2676.d: from חָצָה ; the middle (of the night).

H2677.d: from חָצָה ; the half or middle.
H2677.k: half, middle, mid(-night), midst, part, two parts

H2678.d: or chetsiy ; prolongation from חֵץ ; an arrow.

H2679.d: from חֵ֫צִי and the plural of מְנוּחָה , with the article interposed; midst of the resting- places; Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth, an Israelite.

H2680.d: patronymically from חֲצִי הַמְּנֻחוֹת ; a Chatsi-ham-Menachtite or descendant of Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth.

H2681.d: a collateral form of חָצֵר ; a court or abode.

H2682.d: perhaps originally the same as חָצִיר , from the greenness of a courtyard; grass; also a leek (collectively).

H2683.d: from an unused root meaning to hold firmly; the bosom (as comprised between the arms).

H2684.d: a collateral form of חֵ֫צֶן , and meaning the same.

H2685.d: (Aramaic) a primitive root; properly, to shear or cut close; figuratively, to be severe.

H2686.d: a primitive root (compare חָצָה ); properly, to chop into, pierce or sever; hence, to curtail, to distribute (into ranks); as denom. from חֵץ , to shoot an arrow.
H2686.k: archer, X bands, cut off in the midst

H2687.d: from חָצָץ ; properly, something cutting; hence, gravel (as grit); also (like חֵץ ) an arrow.

H2688.d: or Chatsatson Tamar ; from חָצַץ and תָּמָר ; division (i.e. perhaps row) of (the) palm-tree; Chatsetson-tamar, a place in Palestine.

H2689.d: by reduplication from חָצַר ; a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note).

H2690.d: a primitive root; properly, to surround with a stockade, and thus separate from the open country; but used only in the reduplicated form chatsotser ; or (2 Chronicles 5:12) chatsorer ; as dem. from NONE ; to trumpet, i.e. blow on that instrument.

H2691.d: (masculine and feminine); from חָצַר in its original sense; a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls).

H2692.d: from חָצֵר and אַדָּר ; (the) village of Addar; Chatsar-Addar, a place in Palestine.

H2693.d: from חָצֵר and a feminine of גַּד ; (the) village of (female) Fortune; Chatsar-Gaddah, a place in Palestine.

H2694.d: from חָצֵר and תִּיכוֹן with the article interposed; village of the middle; Chatsar-hat-Tikon, a place in Palestine.

H2695.d: by an orthographical variation for חֶצְרוֹן ; enclosure; Chetsro, an Israelite.

H2696.d: from חָצֵר ; court-yard; Chetsron, the name of a place in Palestine; also of two Israelites.

H2697.d: patronymically from חֶצְרוֹן ; a Chetsronite or (collectively) descendants of Chetsron.

H2698.d: feminine plural of חָצֵר ; yards; Chatseroth, a place in Palestine.

H2699.d: plural masculine of חָצֵר ; yards; Chatserim, a place in Palestine.

H2700.d: from חָצֵר and מָ֫וֶת ; village of death; Chatsarmaveth, a place in Arabia.

H2701.d: from חָצֵר and סוּסָה ; village of cavalry; Chatsar-Susah, a place in Palestine.

H2702.d: from חָצֵר and the plural of סוּס ; village of horses; Chatsar-Susim, a place in Palestine.

H2703.d: from חָצֵר and a derivative of עַ֫יִן ; village of springs; Chatsar-Enon, a place in Palestine.

H2704.d: from חָצֵר and the same as עֵינָן ; village of springs; Chatsar-Enan, a place in Palestine.

H2705.d: from חָצֵר and שׁוּעָל ; village of (the) fox; Chatsar-Shual, a place in Palestine.

H2706.d: from חָקַק ; an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage).
H2706.k: appointed, bound, commandment, convenient, custom, decree(-d), due, law, measure, X necessary, ordinance(- nary), portion, set time, statute, task

H2707.d: a primitive root; to carve; by implication, to delineate; also to entrench.
H2707.k: carved work, portrayed, set a print

H2708.d: feminine of חֹק , and meaning substantially the same.
H2708.k: appointed, custom, manner, ordinance, site, statute

H2709.d: from an unused root probably meaning to bend; crooked; Chakupha, one of the Nethinim.

H2710.d: a primitive root; properly, to hack, i.e. engrave (Judges 5:14, to be a scribe simply); by implication, to enact (laws being cut in stone or metal tablets in primitive times) or (gen.) prescribe.
H2710.k: appoint, decree, governor, grave, lawgiver, note, pourtray, print, set

H2711.d: from חָקַק ; an enactment, a resolution.

H2712.d: or (fully) Chuwqoq ; from חָקַק ; appointed; Chukkok or Chukok, a place in Palestine.

H2713.d: a primitive root; properly, to penetrate; hence, to examine intimately.
H2713.k: find out, (make) search (out), seek (out), sound, try

H2715.d: or (fully) chowr ; from חָרַר ; properly, white or pure (from the cleansing or shining power of fire (compare חֹרִי ); hence (figuratively) noble (in rank).

H2716.d: from an unused (and vulgar) root probably meaning to evacuate the bowels: excrement; -dung. Also chariy .

H2717.d: or chareb ; a primitive root; to parch (through drought) i.e. (by analogy,) to desolate, destroy, kill.
H2717.k: decay, (be) desolate, destroy(-er), (be) dry (up), slay, X surely, (lay, lie, make) waste

H2718.d: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to חָרַב ; to demolish.

H2719.d: from חָרַב ; drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement.
H2719.k: axe, dagger, knife, mattock, sword, tool

H2721.d: a collaterally form of חָ֫רֶב ; drought or desolation.
H2721.k: desolation, drought, dry, heat, X utterly, waste

H2722.d: from חָרַב ; desolate; Choreb, a (generic) name for the Sinaitic mountains.

H2723.d: feminine of חֹ֫רֶב ; properly, drought, i.e. (by implication) a desolation.

H2726.d: or Charbownah ; of Persian origin; Charbona or Charbonah, a eunuch of Xerxes.

H2727.d: a primitive root; properly, to leap suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to be dismayed.

H2728.d: from חָרַג ; the leaping insect, i.e. a locust.

H2729.d: a primitive root; to shudder with terror; hence, to fear; also to hasten (with anxiety).
H2729.k: be (make) afraid, be careful, discomfit, fray (away), quake, tremble

H2731.k: care, X exceedingly, fear, quaking, trembling

H2732.d: the same as חֲרָדָה ; Charadah, a place in the Desert.

H2733.d: patrial from a derivative of חָרַד (compare עֵין חֲרֹד ); a Charodite, or inhabitant of Charod.

H2734.d: a primitive root (compare חָרַר ); to glow or grow warm; figuratively (usually) to blaze up, of anger, zeal, jealousy. See תְּתַחֲרֶה .
H2734.k: be angry, burn, be displeased, X earnestly, fret self, grieve, be (wax) hot, be incensed, kindle, X very, be wroth

H2735.d: from חֹר and a collateral (masculine) form of גֻּדְגֹּ֫דָה , with the article interposed; hole of the cleft: Chor-hag-Gidgad, a place in the Desert.

H2736.d: from חָרָה and יָהּ ; fearing Jah; Charhajah, an Israelite.

H2737.d: from an unused root meaning to perforate; properly, pierced, i.e. a bead of pearl, gems or jewels (as strung).

H2738.d: or (shortened) charul ; apparently, a passive participle of an unused root probably meaning to be prickly; properly, pointed, i.e. a bramble or other thorny weed: nettle.

H2739.d: from passive participle of חָרַם and אַף ; snub-nosed; Charumaph, an Israelite.

H2740.d: or (shortened) charon ; from חָרָה ; a burning of anger.

H2741.d: a patrial from (probably) a collateral form of חָרִיף ; a Charuphite or inhabitant of Charuph (or Chariph).

H2742.d: or charuts ; passive participle of חָרַץ ; properly, incised or (active) incisive; hence (as noun masculine or feminine) a trench (as dug), gold (as mined), a threshing-sledge (having sharp teeth); (figuratively) determination; also eager.
H2742.k: decision, diligent, (fine) gold, pointed things, sharp, threshing instrument, wall

H2743.d: the same as חָרוּץ ; earnest; Charuts, an Israelite.

H2744.d: a fuller form of חַרְחֻר ; inflammation; Charchur, one of the Nethinim.

H2745.d: from the same as חָ֫רֶס ; perhaps shining; Charchas, an Israelite.

H2747.d: from a primitive root meaning to engrave; a chisel or graver; also a style for writing.

H2748.d: from the same as חֶ֫רֶט ; a horoscopist (as drawing magical lines or circles).

H2750.d: from חָרָה ; a burning (i.e. intense) anger.

H2751.d: from the same as חוּר ; white bread.

H2752.d: from חֹר ; cave-dweller or troglodyte; a Chorite or aboriginal Idumaean.

H2753.d: or Chowriy ; the same as חֹרִי ; Chori, the name of two men.

H2754.d: or charit ; from the same as חֶ֫רֶט ; properly, cut out (or hollow), i.e. (by implication) a pocket.

H2755.d: from the plural of חַרְאֵי and the plural of יוֹנִים ; excrements of doves, or perhaps rather the plural of a single word charapyown ; of similar or uncertain derivation, probably a kind of vegetable.

H2756.d: from חָרַף ; autumnal; Chariph, the name of two Israelites.

H2757.d: or charits ; from חָרַץ ; properly, incisure or (passively) incised (compare חָרוּץ ); hence, a threshing-sledge (with sharp teeth): also a slice (as cut).

H2758.d: from חָרַשׁ ; ploughing or its season.

H2759.d: from חָרַשׁ in the sense of silence; quiet, i.e. sultry (as feminine noun, the sirocco or hot east wind).

H2760.d: a primitive root; to braid (i.e. to entangle or snare) or catch (game) in a net.

H2761.d: (Aramaic) a root probably allied to the equivalent of חָרַר ; to scorch.

H2762.d: from חָרַך ; properly, a net, i.e. (by analogy) lattice.

H2763.d: a primitive root; to seclude; specifically (by a ban) to devote to religious uses (especially destruction); physical and reflexive, to be blunt as to the nose.
H2763.k: make accursed, consecrate, (utterly) destroy, devote, forfeit, have a flat nose, utterly (slay, make away)

H2764.d: or (Zecheriah 14:11) cherem ; from חָרַם ; physical (as shutting in) a net (either literally or figuratively); usually a doomed object; abstr. extermination.
H2764.k: (ac-)curse(-d, -d thing), dedicated thing, things which should have been utterly destroyed, (appointed to) utter destruction, devoted (thing), net

H2765.d: from חָרַם ; devoted; Chorem, a place in Palestine.

H2766.d: from חָרַם ; snub-nosed; Charim, an Israelite.

H2767.d: from חָרַם ; devoted; Chormah, a place in Palestine.

H2768.d: from חָרַם ; abrupt; Chermon, a mount of Palestine.

H2769.d: plural of חֶרְמוֹן ; Hermons, i.e. its peaks.

H2771.d: from חָרַר ; parched; Charan, the name of a man and also of a place.

H2772.d: patrial from חֹרוֹנָ֫יִם ; a Choronite or inhabitant of Choronaim.

H2773.d: dual of a derivative from חֹר ; double cave-town; Choronajim, a place in Moab.

H2774.d: of uncertain derivation; Charnepher, an Israelite.

H2775.d: from an unused root meaning to scrape; the itch; also (perhaps from the mediating idea of חַרְסוּת ) the sun.

H2776.d: the same as חָ֫רֶס ; shining; Cheres, a mountain in Palestine.

H2777.d: from חָ֫רֶס (apparently in the sense of a red tile used for scraping); a potsherd, i.e. (by implication) a pottery; the name of a gate at Jerusalem.

H2778.d: a primitive root; to pull off, i.e. (by implication) to expose (as by stripping); specifically, to betroth (as if a surrender); figuratively, to carp at, i.e. defame; denominative (from חֹ֫רֶף ) to spend the winter.
H2778.k: betroth, blaspheme, defy, jeopard, rail, reproach, upbraid

H2779.d: from חָרַף ; properly, the crop gathered, i.e. (by implication) the autumn (and winter) season; figuratively, ripeness of age.

H2780.d: from חָרַף ; reproachful; Chareph, an Israelite.

H2781.d: from חָרַף ; contumely, disgrace, the pudenda.

H2782.d: a primitive root; properly, to point sharply, i.e. (literally) to wound; figuratively, to be alert, to decide.
H2782.k: bestir self, decide, decree, determine, maim, move

H2783.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָרַץ in the sense of vigor; the loin (as the seat of strength).

H2784.d: of uncertain derivation; a fetter; figuratively, a pain.

H2785.d: from חָרַץ ; a sour grape (as sharp in taste).

H2786.d: a primitive root; to grate the teeth.

H2787.d: a primitive root; to glow, i.e. literally (to melt, burn, dry up) or figuratively (to show or incite passion.

H2789.d: a collateral form mediating between חָ֫רֶס and חֶ֫רֶשׁ ; a piece of pottery.

H2790.d: a primitive root; to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to engrave, plough; hence (from the use of tools) to fabricate (of any material); figuratively, to devise (in a bad sense); hence (from the idea of secrecy) to be silent, to let alone; hence (by implication) to be deaf (as an accompaniment of dumbness).
H2790.k: X altogether, cease, conceal, be deaf, devise, ear, graven, imagine, leave off speaking, hold peace, plow(-er, man), be quiet, rest, practise secretly, keep silence, be silent, speak not a word, be still, hold tongue, worker

H2791.d: from חָרַשׁ ; magical craft; also silence.

H2793.d: from חָרַשׁ ; a forest (perhaps as furnishing the material for fabric).

H2794.d: active participle of חָרַשׁ ; a fabricator or mechanic.

H2795.d: from חָרַשׁ ; deaf (whether literally or spir.).

H2796.d: from חָרַשׁ ; a fabricator or any material.
H2796.k: artificer, (+) carpenter, craftsman, engraver, maker, + mason, skilful, (+) smith, worker, workman, such as wrought

H2797.d: from חֶ֫רֶשׁ ; magician; Charsha, one of the Nethinim.

H2798.d: plural of חָרָשׁ ; mechanics, the name of a valley in Jerusalem.

H2800.d: the same as חֲרֹ֫שֶׁת ; Charosheth, a place in Palestine.

H2802.d: from חָרַת (but equivalent to חֹ֫רֶשׁ ); forest; Chereth, a thicket in Palestine.

H2803.d: a primitive root; properly, to plait or interpenetrate, i.e. (literally) to weave or (gen.) to fabricate; figuratively, to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute.
H2803.k: (make) account (of), conceive, consider, count, cunning (man, work, workman), devise, esteem, find out, forecast, hold, imagine, impute, invent, be like, mean, purpose, reckon(-ing be made), regard, think

H2805.d: from חָשַׁב ; a belt or strap (as being interlaced).

H2806.d: from חָשַׁב and דִּין ; considerate judge; Chasbaddanah, an Israelite.

H2807.d: from חָשַׁב ; estimation; Cashubah, an Israelite.

H2808.d: from חָשַׁב ; properly, contrivance; by implication, intelligence.

H2809.d: the same as חֶשְׁבּוֹן ; Cheshbon, a place East of the Jordan.

H2810.d: from חָשַׁב ; a contrivance, i.e. actual (a warlike machine) or mental (a machination).

H2811.d: or Chashabyahuw ; from חָשַׁב and יָהּ ; Jah has regarded; Chashabjah, the name of nine Israelites.

H2812.d: feminine of חֶשְׁבּוֹן ; inventiveness; Chashnah, an Israelite.

H2813.d: from חֶשְׁבּוֹן and יָהּ ; thought of Jah; Chashabnejah, the name of two Israelites.

H2814.d: a primitive root; to hush or keep quiet.
H2814.k: hold peace, keep silence, be silent, (be) still

H2815.d: from חָשַׁב ; intelligent; Chashshub, the name of two or three Israelites.

H2816.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָשַׁך ; the dark.

H2817.d: or Chasuphao ; from חָשַׂף ; nakedness; Chasupha, one of the Nethinim.

H2818.d: (Aramaic) a collateral root to one corresponding to חוּשׁ in the sense of readiness; to be necessary (from the idea of convenience) or (transitively) to need.

H2819.d: from a root corresponding to חֲשַׁח ; necessity.

H2820.d: a primitive root; to restrain or (reflex.) refrain; by implication, to refuse, spare, preserve; also (by interch. with חָשַׁך ) to observe.
H2820.k: assuage, X darken, forbear, hinder, hold back, keep (back), punish, refrain, reserve, spare, withhold

H2821.d: a primitive root; to be dark (as withholding light); transitively, to darken.
H2821.k: be black, be (make) dark, darken, cause darkness, be dim, hide

H2822.d: from חָשַׁך ; the dark; hence (literally) darkness; figuratively, misery, destruction, death, ignorance, sorrow, wickedness.

H2825.d: or chashekah ; from חָשַׁך ; darkness; figuratively, misery.

H2826.d: a primitive root; to make (intrans. be) unsteady, i.e. weak.

H2827.d: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to חָשַׁל ; to weaken, i.e. crush.

H2828.d: from the same as חַשְׁמַנִּים ; enriched; Chashum, the name of two or three Israelites.

H2829.d: the same as חַשְׁמַנִּים ; opulent; Cheshmon, a place in Palestine.

H2830.d: of uncertain derivation; probably bronze or polished spectrum metal.

H2831.d: from an unused root (probably meaning firm or capacious in resources); apparently wealthy.

H2832.d: feminine of חַשְׁמַנִּים ; fertile; Chasmonah, a place in the Desert.

H2833.d: from an unused root probably meaning to contain or sparkle; perhaps a pocket (as holding the Urim and Thummim), or rich (as containing gems), used only of the gorget of the highpriest.

H2834.d: a primitive root; to strip off, i.e. generally to make naked (for exertion or in disgrace), to drain away or bail up (a liquid).
H2834.k: make bare, clean, discover, draw out, take, uncover

H2835.d: from חָשַׂף ; properly, drawn off, i.e. separated; hence, a small company (as divided from the rest).

H2836.d: a primitive root; to cling, i.e. join, (figuratively) to love, delight in; elliptically (or by interchangeable for חָשַׂך ) to deliver.
H2836.k: have a delight, (have a) desire, fillet, long, set (in) love

H2838.d: or chashuwq ; past participle of חָשַׁק ; attached, i.e. a fence-rail or rod connecting the posts or pillars.

H2839.d: from חָשַׁק ; conjoined, i.e. a wheel-spoke or rod connecting the hub with the rim.

H2840.d: from an unused root meaning to bind together; combined, i.e. the nave or hub of a wheel (as holding the spokes together).

H2841.d: from the same as חִשֻּׁרֵי ; properly, a combination or gathering, i.e. of watery clouds.

H2842.d: by variation for קָשׁ ; dry grass.

H2843.d: patronymically from חוּשָׁה ; a Chushathite or descendant of Chushah.

H2844.d: from חָתַת ; concretely, crushed; also afraid; abstractly, terror.

H2845.d: from חָתַת ; terror; Cheth, an aboriginal Canaanite.

H2846.d: a primitive root; to lay hold of; especially to pick up fire.

H2848.d: from חָתַל ; swathed, i.e. a bandage.

H2850.d: patronymically from חֵת ; a Chittite, or descendant of Cheth.

H2852.d: a primitive root; properly, to cut off, i.e. (figuratively) to decree.

H2855.d: from חָתַל ; enswathed; Chethlon, a place in Palestine.

H2856.d: a primitive root; to close up; especially to seal.
H2856.k: make an end, mark, seal (up), stop

H2857.d: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to חָתַם ; to seal.

H2858.d: feminine active participle of חָתַם ; a seal.

H2859.d: a primitive root; to give (a daughter) away in marriage; hence (generally) to contract affinity by marriage.
H2859.k: join in affinity, father in law, make marriages, mother in law, son in law

H2860.d: from חָתַן ; a relative by marriage (especially through the bride); figuratively, a circumcised child (as a species of religious espousal).

H2863.d: from חָתַף ; properly, rapine; figuratively, robbery.

H2864.d: a primitive root; to force a passage, as by burglary; figuratively, with oars.

H2865.d: a primitive root; properly, to prostrate; hence, to break down, either (literally) by violence, or (figuratively) by confusion and fear.
H2865.k: abolish, affright, be (make) afraid, amaze, beat down, discourage, (cause to) dismay, go down, scare, terrify

H2867.d: the same as חֲתַת ; Chathath, an Israelite.

H2869.d: (Aramaic) from טְאֵב ; the same as טוֹב ; good.

H2870.d: from טוֹב and אֵל ; pleasing (to) God; Tabeel, the name of a Syrian and of a Persian.

H2871.d: passive participle of טָבַל ; properly, dyed, i.e. a turban (probably as of colored stuff).

H2872.d: from an unused root meaning to pile up; properly, accumulated; i.e. (by implication) a summit.

H2873.d: a primitive root; to slaughter (animals or men).

H2874.d: from טָבַח ; properly, something slaughtered; hence, a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstr. butchery (or concretely, a place of slaughter).
H2874.k: X beast, slaughter, X slay, X sore

H2875.d: the same as טָ֫בַח ; massacre; Tebach, the name of a Mesopotamian and of an Israelite.

H2876.d: from טָבַח ; properly, a butcher; hence, a lifeguardsman (because he was acting as an executioner); also a cook (usually slaughtering the animal for food).

H2877.d: (Aramaic) the same as טַבָּח ; a lifeguardsman.

H2878.d: feminine of טָ֫בַח and meaning the same.

H2879.d: feminine of טַבָּח ; a female cook.

H2880.d: from טִבְחָה ; slaughter; Tibchath, a place in Syria.

H2881.d: a primitive root; to dip, to immerse.

H2882.d: from טָבַל and יָהּ ; Jah has dipped; Tebaljah, an Israelite.

H2884.d: plural of טַבַּ֫עַת ; rings; Tabbaoth, one of the Nethinim.

H2885.d: from טָבַע ; properly, a seal (as sunk into the wax), i.e. signet (for sealing); hence (generally) a ring of any kind.

H2886.d: from טוֹב and רִמּוֹן ; pleasing (to) Rimmon; Tabrimmon, a Syrian.

H2887.d: probably of foreign derivation; Tebeth, the tenth Heb. month.

H2888.d: of uncertain derivation; Tabbath, a place East of the Jordan.

H2889.d: or tahor ; from טָהֵר ; pure (in a physical, chemical, ceremonial or moral sense).

H2891.d: a primitive root; properly, to be bright; i.e. (by implication) to be pure (physical sound, clear, unadulterated; Levitically, uncontaminated; morally, innocent or holy).
H2891.k: be (make, make self, pronounce) clean, cleanse (self), purge, purify(-ier, self)

H2892.d: from טָהֵר ; literally brightness; ceremonially purification.

H2893.d: feminine of טֹ֫הַר ; ceremonial purification; moral purity.

H2894.d: a primitive root; to sweep away.

H2895.d: a primitive root, to be (transitively, do or make) good (or well) in the widest sense.
H2895.k: be (do) better, cheer, be (do, seem) good, (make) goodly, X please, (be, do, go, play) well

H2896.d: from טוֹב ; good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well).
H2896.k: beautiful, best, better, bountiful, cheerful, at ease, X fair (word), (be in) favour, fine, glad, good (deed, -lier, -liest, -ly, -ness, -s), graciously, joyful, kindly, kindness, liketh (best), loving, merry, X most, pleasant, + pleaseth, pleasure, precious, prosperity, ready, sweet, wealth, welfare, (be) well ((-favoured))

H2897.d: the same as טוֹב ; good; Tob, a region apparently East of the Jordan.

H2898.d: from טוֹב ; good (as a noun), in the widest sense, especially goodness (superlative concretely, the best), beauty, gladness, welfare.
H2898.k: fair, gladness, good(-ness, thing, -s), joy, go well with

H2899.d: from טוֹב and אֲדֹנִיָּה ; pleasing (to) Adonijah; Tob-Adonijah, an Israelite.

H2900.d: or Towbiyahuw ; from טוֹב and יָהּ ; goodness of Jehovah; Tobijah, the name of three Israelites and of one Samaritan.

H2902.d: a primitive root; to smear, especially with lime.

H2903.d: from an unusued root meaning to go around or bind; a fillet for the forehead.

H2904.d: a primitive root; to pitch over or reel; hence (transitively) to cast down or out.
H2904.k: carry away, (utterly) cast (down, forth, out), send out

H2905.d: from an unused root meaning to range in a regular manner; a row; hence, a wall.

H2906.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to צוּר ; a rock or hill.

H2907.d: a primitive root; to pounce as a bird of prey.

H2908.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to טָוָה ; hunger (as twisting).

H2909.d: a primitive root; to stretch a bow, as an archer.

H2910.d: from טָחָה (or ט֫וּחַ ) in the sense of overlaying; (in the plural only) the kidneys (as being covered); hence (figuratively) the inmost thought.

H2911.d: from טָחַן ; a hand mill; hence, a millstone.

H2912.d: a primitive root; to grind meal; hence, to be a concubine (that being their employment).

H2913.d: from טָחַן ; a hand mill; hence (figuratively) chewing.

H2914.d: from an unused root meaning to burn; a boil or ulcer (from the inflammation), especially a tumor in the anus or pudenda (the piles).

H2915.d: from (the equiv. of) ט֫וּחַ ; mortar or plaster.

H2916.d: from an unused root meaning apparently to be sticky (rath. perb. a demon. from טוּא , through the idea of dirt to be swept away); mud or clay; figuratively, calamity.

H2917.d: (Aramaic) perhaps, by interchange, for a word corresponding to טִיט ; clay.

H2918.d: feminine of (an equivalent to) טוּר ; a wall; hence, a fortress or a hamlet.

H2921.d: a primitive root; properly, to cover with pieces; i.e. (by implication) to spot or variegate (as tapestry).

H2922.d: apparently from טָלָא in the (orig.) sense of covering (for protection); a lamb (compare טָלֶה ).

H2923.d: from the plural of טְלָאּים ; lambs; Telaim, a place in Palestine.

H2924.d: by variation for טְלָאּים ; a lamb.

H2926.d: a primitive root; properly, to strew over, i.e. (by implication) to cover in or plate (with beams).

H2927.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to טָלַל ; to cover with shade.

H2928.d: from an unused root meaning to break up or treat violently; oppression; Telem, the name of a place in Idumaea, also of a temple doorkeeper.

H2929.d: from the same as NONE ; oppressive; Talmon, a temple doorkeeper.

H2930.d: a primitive root; to be foul, especially in a ceremial or moral sense (contaminated).
H2930.k: defile (self), pollute (self), be (make, make self, pronounce) unclean, X utterly

H2931.d: from טָמֵא ; foul in a relig. sense.

H2933.d: a collateral form of טָמֵא ; to be impure in a religious sense.

H2934.d: a primitive root; to hide (by covering over).

H2935.d: from an unused root probably meaning to weave; a basket (of interlaced osiers).

H2937.d: a primitive root; to wander;,causatively to lead astray.

H2938.d: a primitive root; to taste; figuratively, to perceive.

H2939.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to טָעַם ; to taste; causatively to feed.

H2940.d: from טָעַם ; properly, a taste, i.e. (figuratively) perception; by implication, intelligence; transitively, a mandate.
H2940.k: advice, behaviour, decree, discretion, judgment, reason, taste, understanding

H2941.d: (Aramaic) from טְעַם ; properly, a taste, i.e. (as in טָ֫עַם ) a judicial sentence.
H2941.k: account, X to be commanded, commandment, matter

H2942.d: (Aramaic) from טְעַם , and equivalent to טַ֫עַם ; properly, flavor; figuratively, judgment (both subjective and objective); hence, account (both subj. and obj.).
H2942.k: + chancellor, + command, commandment, decree, + regard, taste, wisdom

H2943.d: a primitive root; to load a beast.

H2945.d: from טָפַף (perhaps referring to the tripping gait of children); a family (mostly used collectively in the singular).

H2946.d: a primitive root; to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively, to nurse a child (as promotive of growth); or perhaps a denom. from טֶ֫פַח , from dandling on the palms.

H2947.d: from טָפַח ; a spread of the hand, i.e. a palm- breadth (not "span" of the fingers); architecturally, a corbel (as a supporting palm).

H2950.d: a primitive root; properly, to stick on as a patch; figuratively, to impute falsely.

H2951.d: of foreign derivation; a military governor.

H2952.d: a primitive root; apparently to trip (with short steps) coquettishly.

H2953.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to צָפַר , and meaning the same as צִפֹּ֫רֶן ; a finger-nail; also a hoof or claw.

H2954.d: a primitive root; properly, apparently to be thick; figuratively, to be stupid.

H2955.d: probably from נָטַף ; a dropping (of ointment); Taphath, an Israelitess.

H2956.d: a primitive root; to drive on; figuratively, to follow close.

H2958.d: a variation of טֶ֫רֶם ; not yet.

H2961.d: from an unused root apparently meaning to be moist; properly, dripping; hence, fresh (i.e. recently made such).

H2962.d: from an unused root apparently meaning to interrupt or suspend; properly, non-occurrence; used adverbially, not yet or before.

H2963.d: a primitive root; to pluck off or pull to pieces; causatively to supply with food (as in morsels).
H2963.k: catch, X without doubt, feed, ravin, rend in pieces, X surely, tear (in pieces)

H2964.d: from טָרַף ; something torn, i.e. a fragment, e.g. a fresh leaf, prey, food.

H2965.d: from טָרַף ; recently torn off, i.e. fresh.

H2966.d: feminine (collectively) of טָ֫רֶף ; prey, i.e. flocks devoured by animals.
H2966.k: ravin, (that which was) torn (of beasts, in pieces)

H2967.d: (Aramaic) from a name of foreign derivation; a Tarpelite (collectively) or inhabitants of Tarpel, a place in Assyria.

H2969.d: a primitive root; to be suitable.

H2970.d: or Ya.azanyahuw ; from הֶאֱזִין and יָהּ ; heard of Jah; Jaazanjah, the name of four Israelites. Compare יְזַנְיָה .

H2971.d: from אוֹר ; enlightener; Jair, the name of four Israelites.

H2972.d: patronymically from יָאּיר ; a Jairite or descendant of Jair.

H2973.d: a primitive root; properly, to be slack, i.e. (figuratively) to be foolish.

H2974.d: a primitive root (probably rather the same as יָאַל through the idea of mental weakness); properly, to yield, especially assent; hence (pos.) to undertake as an act of volition.
H2974.k: assay, begin, be content, please, take upon, X willingly, would

H2975.d: of Egyptian origin; a channel, e.g. a fosse, canal, shaft; specifically the Nile, as the one river of Egypt, including its collateral trenches; also the Tigris, as the main river of Assyria.

H2976.d: a primitive root; to desist, i.e. (figuratively) to despond.
H2976.k: (cause to) despair, one that is desperate, be no hope

H2977.d: from the same root as אָשְׁוִיֹּת and יָהּ ; founded of Jah; Joshijah, the name of two Israelites.

H2979.d: from the same as אֲתָרִים ; stepping; Jeatherai, an Israelite.

H2981.d: from יָבַל ; produce, i.e. a crop or (figuratively) wealth.

H2982.d: from בּוּס ; trodden, i.e. threshing-place; Jebus, the aboriginal name of Jerusalem.

H2983.d: patrial from יְבוּס ; a Jebusite or inhabitant of Jebus.

H2984.d: from בָּחַר ; choice; Jibchar, an Israelite.

H2985.d: from בִּין ; intelligent; Jabin, the name of two Canaanitish kings.

H2986.d: a primitive root; properly, to flow; causatively, to bring (especially with pomp).

H2989.d: the same as יִבְלֵי ; Jabal, an antediluvian.

H2991.d: from בָּלַע and עָם ; devouring people; Jibleam, a place in Palestine.

H2992.d: a primitive root of doubtful meaning; used only as a denominative from יָבָם ; to marry a (deceased) brother's widow.
H2992.k: perform the duty of a husband's brother, marry

H2993.d: from (the orig. of) יָבַם ; a brother-in-law.

H2994.d: feminine participle of יָבַם ; a sister-in-law.

H2995.d: from בָּנָה and אֵל : built of God; Jabneel, the name of two places in Palestine.

H2996.d: from בָּנָה ; a building; Jabneh, a place in Palestine.

H2997.d: from בָּנָה and יָהּ ; built of Jah; Jibnejah, an Israelite.

H2998.d: from בָּנָה and יָהּ ; building of Jah; Jibnijah, an Israelite.

H2999.d: probably from בָּקַק ; pouring forth; Jabbok, a river east of the Jordan.

H3000.d: from בָּרַך and יָהּ : blessed of Jah; Jeberekjah, an Israelite.

H3001.d: a primitive root; to be ashamed, confused or disappointed; also (as failing) to dry up (as water) or wither (as herbage).
H3001.k: be ashamed, clean, be confounded, (make) dry (up), (do) shame(-fully), X utterly, wither (away)

H3003.d: the same as יָבֵשׁ (also Yabeysh ; often with the addition of גִּלְעָד , i.e. Jabesh of Gilad); Jobesh, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine.

H3005.d: from the same as בְּשָׂמִים ; fragrant; Jibsam, an Israelite.

H3006.d: a variation of יַבָּשָׁה ; dry ground.

H3008.d: from גָּאַל ; avenger; Jigal, the name of three Israelites.

H3009.d: a primitive root; to dig or plow.

H3011.d: feminine from גָּבַהּ ; hillock; Jogbehah, a place East of the Jordan.

H3012.d: from גָּדַל and יָהּ ; magnified of Jah; Jigdaljah, an Israelite.

H3013.k: afflict, cause grief, grieve, sorrowful, vex

H3014.d: a primitive root (probably rather the same as יָגָה through the common idea of dissatisfaction); to push away; -be removed.

H3017.d: probably from גּוּר ; a lodging; Jagur, a place in Palestine.

H3018.d: from יָגַע ; toil; hence, a work, produce, property (as the result of labor).

H3020.d: from גָּלָה ; exiled; Jogli, an Israelite.

H3021.d: a primitive root; properly, to gasp; hence, to be exhausted, to tire, to toil.

H3022.d: from יָגַע ; earnings (as the product of toil); -that which he laboured for.

H3026.d: (Aramaic) from a word derived from an unused root (meaning to gather) and a derivation of a root corresponding to שָׂהֲדִי ; heap of the testimony; Jegar-Sahadutha, a cairn East of the Jordan.

H3027.d: a primitive word; a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.), in distinction from כָּף , the closed one); used (as noun, adverb, etc.) in a great variety of applications, both literally and figuratively, both proximate and remote (as follows).
H3027.k: (+ be) able, X about, + armholes, at, axletree, because of, beside, border, X bounty, + broad, (broken-)handed, X by, charge, coast, + consecrate, + creditor, custody, debt, dominion, X enough, + fellowship, force, X from, hand(-staves, -y work), X he, himself, X in, labour, + large, ledge, (left-)handed, means, X mine, ministry, near, X of, X order, ordinance, X our, parts, pain, power, X presumptuously, service, side, sore, state, stay, draw with strength, stroke, + swear, terror, X thee, X by them, X themselves, X thine own, X thou, through, X throwing, + thumb, times, X to, X under, X us, X wait on, (way-)side, where, + wide, X with (him, me, you), work, + yield, X yourselves

H3030.d: of uncertain derivation; Jidalah, a place in Palestine.

H3031.d: from the same as דְּבָשׁ ; perhaps honeyed; Jidbash, an Israelite.

H3032.d: a primitive root; properly, to handle (compare יָדָה ), i.e. to throw, e.g. lots.

H3033.d: from יְדִיד ; properly, affection; concretely, a darling object.

H3034.d: a primitive root; used only as denominative from יָד ; literally, to use (i.e. hold out) the hand; physically, to throw (a stone, an arrow) at or away; especially to revere or worship (with extended hands); intensively, to bemoan (by wringing the hands).

H3035.d: from יָדָה ; praised; Jiddo, an Israelite.

H3036.d: from יָדָה ; thankful; Jadon, an Israelite.

H3037.d: from יָדַע ; knowing; Jaddua, the name of two Israelites.

H3038.d: or Yduthuwn ; or Ydiythuwn ; probably from יָדָה ; laudatory; Jeduthun, an Israelite.

H3039.d: from the same as דּוֹד ; loved.

H3040.d: feminine of יְדִיד ; beloved; Jedidah, an Israelitess.

H3041.d: from יְדִיד and יָהּ ; beloved of Jah; Jedidejah, a name of Solomon.

H3042.d: from יָדָה and יָהּ ; praised of Jah; Jedajah, the name of two Israelites.

H3043.d: from יָדַע and אֵל ; knowing God; Jediael, the name of three Israelites.

H3044.d: from דָּלַף ; tearful; Jidlaph, a Mesopotamian.

H3045.d: a primitive root; to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.) (as follow).
