H8670.d: from שׁוּר in the sense of arrival; a gift.

H8672.d: or (masculine) tishtah ; perhaps from שָׁעָה through the idea of a turn to the next or full number ten; nine or (ord.) ninth.

H8674.d: of foreign derivation; Tattenai, a Persian.

G1.d: of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first. Often used (usually an, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from ἄνευ ) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of ἅμα ).

G2.d: of Hebrew origin ( אַהֲרוֹן ); Aaron, the brother of Moses.

G3.d: of Hebrew origin ( אֲבַדּוֹן ); a destroying angel.

G4.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and βάρος ; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome.

G5.d: of Chaldee origin ( אַב ); father as a vocative.

G6.d: of Hebrew origin ( הָ֫בֶל ); Abel, the son of Adam.

G7.d: of Hebrew origin ( אֲבִיָּה ); Abijah, the name of two Israelites.

G8.d: of Hebrew origin ( אֶבְיָתָר ); Abiathar, an Israelite.

G9.d: of foreign origin (compare אָבֵל ); Abilene, a region of Syria.

G10.d: of Hebrew origin ( אֲבִיהוּד ); Abihud, an Israelite.

G11.d: of Hebrew origin ( אַבְרָהָם ); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)

G12.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a variation of βυθός ; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss".

G13.d: of Hebrew origin (compare חָגָב ); Agabus, an Israelite.

G14.d: from ἀγαθός and ἔργον ; to work good.

G15.d: from ἀγαθοποιός ; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty).

G17.d: from ἀγαθός and ποιέω ; a well-doer, i.e. virtuous.

G18.d: a primary word; "good" (in any sense, often as noun). Compare καλός .

G19.d: from ἀγαθός ; goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence.

G21.d: from agan (much) and ἅλλομαι ; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult.
G21.k: be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly)

G22.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and γάμος ; unmarried.

G23.d: from agan (much) and achthos (grief; akin to the base of ἀγκάλη ); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant.
G23.k: be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation

G25.d: perhaps from agan (much) (or compare עָגַב ); to love (in a social or moral sense). Compare φιλέω .

G26.d: from ἀγαπάω ; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast.

G28.d: of Hebrew origin ( הָגָר ); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham.

G29.d: of foreign origin (compare אּגְּרָה ); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service.

G30.d: from aggos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of ἀγκάλη ); a receptacle.

G31.d: from ἄγγελος ; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept.

G32.d: from aggello (probably derived from ἄγω ; compare ἀγέλη ) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor.

G33.d: imperative of ἄγω ; properly, lead, i.e. come on.

G35.d: from Α (as negative particle) and γενεαλογέω ; unregistered as to birth.

G36.d: from Α (as negative particle) and γένος ; properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble.

G37.d: from ἅγιος ; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate.

G38.d: from ἁγιάζω ; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier.

G39.d: neuter of ἅγιος ; a sacred thing (i.e. spot).

G40.d: from hagos (an awful thing) (compare ἁγνός , θάλπω ); sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated).

G41.d: from ἅγιος ; sanctity (i.e. properly, the state).

G42.d: from ἅγιος ; sacredness (i.e. properly, the quality).

G43.d: from agkos (a bend, "ache"); an arm (as curved).

G44.d: from the same as ἀγκάλη ; a hook (as bent).

G45.d: from the same as ἀγκάλη ; an "anchor" (as crooked).

G46.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and the same as γναφεύς ; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth).

G47.d: from ἁγνός ; cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity.

G48.d: from ἁγνός ; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally).

G49.d: from ἁγνίζω ; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration.

G50.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and νοιέω ; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination).
G50.k: (be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown

G51.d: from ἀγνοέω ; a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming.

G53.d: from the same as ἅγιος ; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect.

G54.d: from ἁγνός ; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness.

G55.d: adverb from ἁγνός ; purely, i.e. honestly.

G56.d: from Α (as negative particle) and γνῶσις ; ignorance (properly, the state).

G57.d: from Α (as negative particle) and γνωστός ; unknown.

G58.d: from ageiro (to gather; probably akin to ἐγείρω ); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare.

G59.d: from ἀγορά ; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem.

G60.d: from ἀγορά ; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar.

G61.d: from ἄγω ; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish).

G62.d: from Α (as negative particle) and γράμμα ; unlettered, i.e. illiterate.

G63.d: from ἀγρός and αὐλέω (in the sense of αὐλή ); to camp out.

G64.d: from ἄγρα ; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap.

G65.d: from ἄγριος and ἐλαία ; an oleaster.

G66.d: from ἀγρός ; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce).

G67.d: apparently from ἄγριος and ἵππος ; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods.

G68.d: from ἄγω ; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet.
G68.k: country, farm, piece of ground, land

G69.d: ultimately from Α (as negative particle) and ὕπνος ; to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake.

G70.d: from ἀγρυπνέω ; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake.

G71.d: a primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce.
G71.k: be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open

G72.d: reduplicated from ἄγω ; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living.

G73.d: from ἄγω ; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety.

G74.d: from ἀγών ; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish.

G75.d: from ἀγών ; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something).

G76.d: of Hebrew origin ( אָדָם ); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative).

G77.d: from Α (as negative particle); and δαπάνη ; costless, i.e. gratuitous.

G78.d: probably of Hebrew origin (compare עֶ֫דִי ); Addi, an Israelite.

G79.d: feminine of ἀδελφός ; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically).

G80.d: from Α (as a connective particle) and delphus (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like Α ).

G81.d: from ἀδελφός ; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity.

G82.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and δῆλος ; hidden, figuratively, indistinct.

G85.d: from a derivative of adeo (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress (of mind).
G85.k: be full of heaviness, be very heavy

G86.d: from Α (as negative particle) and εἴδω ; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls.

G87.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of διακρίνω ; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial.

G88.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of διά and λείπω ; unintermitted, i.e. permanent.

G89.d: adverb from ἀδιάλειπτος ; uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion).

G90.d: from a derivative of a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of διαφθείρω ; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine).

G91.d: from ἄδικος ; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically).
G91.k: hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong

G92.k: evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong

G93.d: from ἄδικος ; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act).

G94.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and δίκη ; unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen.

G96.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and δόκιμος ; unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally).

G97.d: from Α (as a negative particle); and δόλος ; undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated.

G98.d: from Adramutteion (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium.

G99.d: from Adria (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian).

G101.d: from ἀδύνατος ; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible.

G102.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and δυνατός ; unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible.
G102.k: could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak

G104.d: from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); "ever," by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly.

G105.d: from the same as ἀήρ ; an eagle (from its wind-like flight).

G106.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and ζύμη ; unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week.

G107.d: of Hebrew origin (compare עַזּוּר ); Azor, an Israelite.

G108.d: of Hebrew origin ( אַשְׁדּוֹד ); Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in Palestine.

G109.d: from aemi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. respire; by analogy, to blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient). Compare ψύχω .

G110.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and θάνατος ; deathlessness.

G111.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of themis (statute; from the base of τίθημι ); illegal; by implication, flagitious.

G112.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and θεός ; godless.

G113.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of τίθημι (in the sense of enacting); lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal.

G114.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of τίθημι ; to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate.
G114.k: cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject

G116.d: plural of Athene (the goddess of wisdom, who was reputed to have founded the city); Athenæ, the capitol of Greece.

G117.d: from Ἀθῆναι ; an Athenæan or inhabitant of Athenæ.

G118.d: from athlos (a contest in the public lists); to contend in the competitive games.

G120.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and θυμός ; to be spiritless, i.e. disheartened.

G121.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of τίθημι (meaning a penalty); not guilty.

G122.d: from aix (a goat); belonging to a goat.

G123.d: from aisso (to rush) and ἅλς (in the sense of the sea; a beach (on which the waves dash).

G124.d: from Αἴγυπτος ; an Ægyptian or inhabitant of Ægyptus.

G125.d: of uncertain derivation; Ægyptus, the land of the Nile.

G126.d: from ἀεί ; everduring (forward and backward, or forward only).

G127.d: perhaps from Α (as a negative particle) and εἴδω (through the idea of downcast eyes); bashfulness, i.e. (towards men), modesty or (towards God) awe.

G128.d: from aitho (to scorch) and ops (the face, from ὀπτάνομαι ); an Æthiopian (as a blackamoor).

G129.d: of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred.

G130.d: from αἷμα and a derivative of ἐκχέω ; an effusion of blood.

G131.d: from αἷμα and ῥέω ; to flow blood, i.e. have a hæmorrhage.
G131.k: diseased with an issue of blood

G133.d: from αἰνέω ; a praising (the act), i.e. (specially) a thank(-offering).

G135.d: from a derivative of αἶνος (in its primary sense); an obscure saying ("enigma"), i.e. (abstractly) obscureness.

G136.d: apparently a prime word; properly, a story, but used in the sense of ἔπαινος ; praise (of God).

G137.d: of Hebrew origin (a derivative of עַ֫יִן , place of springs); Ænon, a place in Palestine.

G138.d: probably akin to αἴρω ; to take for oneself, i.e. to prefer. Some of the forms are borrowed from a cognate hellomai hel'-lom-ahee; which is otherwise obsolete.

G139.d: from αἱρέομαι ; properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion.
G139.k: heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect

G140.d: from a derivative of αἱρέομαι ; to make a choice.

G141.d: from the same as αἱρετίζω ; a schismatic.

G142.d: a primary root; to lift up; by implication, to take up or away; figuratively, to raise (the voice), keep in suspense (the mind), specially, to sail away (i.e. weigh anchor); by Hebraism (compare נָשָׂא ) to expiate sin.
G142.k: away with, bear (up), carry, lift up, loose, make to doubt, put away, remove, take (away, up)

G143.d: of uncertain derivation; to apprehend (properly, by the senses).

G145.d: from a derivative of αἰσθάνομαι ; properly, an organ of perception, i.e. (figuratively) judgment.

G148.d: from αἰσχρός and λόγος ; vile conversation.

G149.d: neuter of αἰσχρός ; a shameful thing, i.e. indecorum.

G150.d: from the same as αἰσχύνομαι ; shameful, i.e. base (specially, venal).

G152.d: from αἰσχύνομαι ; shame or disgrace (abstractly or concretely).

G153.d: from aischos (disfigurement, i.e. disgrace); to feel shame (for oneself).

G154.d: of uncertain derivation; to ask (in genitive case). Compare πυνθάνομαι .
G154.k: ask, beg, call for, crave, desire, require

G155.d: from αἰτέω ; a thing asked or (abstractly) an asking.

G156.d: from the same as αἰτέω ; a cause (as if asked for), i.e. (logical) reason (motive, matter), (legal) crime (alleged or proved).

G157.d: from a derivative of αἰτία ; a thing charged.

G158.d: neuter of αἴτιος ; a reason or crime (like αἰτία ).

G159.d: from the same as αἰτέω ; causative, i.e. (concretely) a causer.

G160.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and φαίνω (compare ἐξαίφνης ) (meaning non-apparent); unexpected, i.e. (adverbially) suddenly.

G163.k: lead away captive, bring into captivity

G164.d: from aichme (a spear) and a derivative of the same as ἅλωσις ; properly, a prisoner of war, i.e. (genitive case) a captive.

G165.d: from the same as ἀεί ; properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity (also past); by implication, the world; specially (Jewish) a Messianic period (present or future). Compare χρόνος .
G165.k: age, course, eternal, (for) ever(-more), (n-)ever, (beginning of the, while the) world (began, without end)

G166.d: from αἰών ; perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well).

G167.d: from ἀκάθαρτος ; impurity (the quality), physically or morally.

G169.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of καθαίρω (meaning cleansed); impure (ceremonially, morally (lewd) or specially, (demonic)).

G170.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and καιρός (meaning unseasonable); to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. to fail of a proper occasion.

G171.d: adverb from the same as ἀκαιρέομαι ; inopportunely.

G172.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and κακός ; not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting.

G173.d: probably from the same as ἀκμήν ; a thorn.

G175.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and καρπός ; barren (literally or figuratively).

G176.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of καταγινώσκω ; unblamable.

G177.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of κατά and καλύπτω ; unveiled.

G178.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of κατακρίνω ; without (legal) trial.

G179.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of καταλύω ; indissoluble, i.e. (figuratively) permanent.

G180.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of καταπαύω ; unrefraining.

G182.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of καθίστημι ; inconstant.

G183.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of κατέχω ; unrestrainable.

G184.d: of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood; corresponding to חֵ֫לֶק and דָּם ); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem.

G185.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of κεράννυμι ; unmixed, i.e. (figuratively) innocent.

G186.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and κλίνω ; not leaning, i.e. (figuratively) firm.

G187.d: from the same as ἀκμήν ; to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature.

G188.d: accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to ake (a point) and meaning the same; adverbially, just now, i.e. still.

G189.d: from ἀκούω ; hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard).
G189.k: audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor

G190.d: from Α (as a particle of union) and keleuthos (a road); properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. to accompany (specially, as a disciple).

G191.d: a primary verb; to hear (in various senses).
G191.k: give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand

G193.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and κράτος ; powerless, i.e. without self-control.

G194.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of κεράννυμι ; undiluted.

G195.d: from the same as ἀκριβέστατος ; exactness.

G196.d: superlative of akribes (a derivative of the same as ἄκρον ); most exact.

G197.d: neuter of the comparative of the same as ἀκριβέστατος ; (adverbially) more exactly.

G198.d: from the same as ἀκριβέστατος ; to be exact, i.e. ascertain.

G199.d: adverb from the same as ἀκριβέστατος ; exactly.

G200.d: apparently from the same as ἄκρον ; a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation).

G202.d: from akroaomai (to listen; apparently an intensive of ἀκούω ); a hearer (merely).

G203.d: from ἄκρον and probably a modified form of posthe (the penis or male sexual organ); the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person.

G204.d: from ἄκρον and γωνία ; belonging to the extreme corner.

G205.d: from ἄκρον and this (a heap); properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty.

G206.d: neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of ἀκμήν ; the extremity.
G206.k: one end… other, tip, top, uttermost participle

G207.d: probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); Akulas, an Israelite.

G208.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and κυρόω ; to invalidate.

G209.d: adverb from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of κωλύω ; in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely.

G210.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and ἑκών ; unwilling.

G211.d: neuter of alabastros (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone; properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material).

G212.d: from ἀλαζών ; braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) self-confidence.

G214.d: from alale ( a shout, "halloo"); to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang.

G215.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of λαλέω ; unspeakable.

G216.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and λαλέω ; mute.

G218.d: from Α (as particle of union) and the base of λιπαρός ; to oil (with perfume).

G219.d: from ἀλέκτωρ and φωνή ; cock-crow, i.e. the third night-watch.

G220.d: from aleko (to ward off); a cock or male fowl.

G221.d: from Alexandreia (the city so called); an Alexandreian or inhabitant of Alexandria.

G222.d: from the same as Ἀλεξανδρεύς ; Alexandrine, or belonging to Alexandria.

G223.d: from the same as (the first part of) ἀλέκτωρ and ἀνήρ ; man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man.

G226.d: from ἀληθής ; to be true (in doctrine and profession).

G227.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and λανθάνω ; true (as not concealing).

G229.d: from the same as ἄλευρον ; to grind.

G230.k: indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in) truth, verily, very

G231.d: from ἅλς ; a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by implication) a fisher.

G232.d: from ἁλιεύς ; to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish.

G235.d: neuter plural of ἄλλος ; properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations).
G235.k: and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet

G238.d: from ἄλλος and agoreo (to harangue (compare ἀγορά )); to allegorize.
G238.k: be an allegory (the Greek word itself)

G239.d: of Hebrew origin (imperative of הָלַל and יָהּ ); praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation.

G240.d: Genitive plural from ἄλλος reduplicated; one another.
G240.k: each other, mutual, one another, (the other), (them-, your-)selves, (selves) together (sometimes with meta or pros )

G241.d: from ἄλλος and γένος ; foreign, i.e. not a Jew.

G242.d: middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to jump; figuratively, to gush.

G243.d: a primary word; "else," i.e. different (in many applications).

G244.d: from ἀλλότριος and ἐπίσκοπος ; overseeing others' affairs, i.e. a meddler (specially, in Gentile customs).

G245.d: from ἄλλος ; another's, i.e. not one's own; by extension foreign, not akin, hostile.

G246.d: from ἄλλος and φυλή ; foreign, i.e. (specially) Gentile.

G248.d: from the same as ἅλων ; to tread out grain.

G249.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and λόγος ; irrational.

G250.d: of foreign origin (compare ἀκάνθινος ); aloes (the gum).

G253.d: comparative of a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and λύπη ; more without grief.

G254.d: of uncertain derivation; a fetter or manacle.

G255.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of λυσιτελεῖ ; gainless, i.e. (by implication) pernicious.

G256.d: of Hebrew origin (compare חֵ֫לֶף ); Alphæus, an Israelite.

G257.d: probably from the base of εἱλίσσω ; a threshing-floor (as rolled hard), i.e. (figuratively) the grain (and chaff, as just threshed).

G768.d: of Hebrew origin ( אָשֵׁר ); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe.

G769.d: from ἀσθενής ; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty.

G770.d: from ἀσθενής ; to be feeble (in any sense).
G770.k: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak

G771.d: from ἀσθενέω ; a scruple of conscience.

G772.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of σθενόω ; strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral).
G772.k: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing)

G773.d: of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore.

G774.d: from Ἀσία ; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia.

G775.d: from Ἀσία and ἀρχή ; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor.

G777.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and σῖτος ; without (taking) food.

G778.d: probably from the same as σκεῦος ; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive).

G779.d: from the same as ἀσκέω ; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle.

G780.d: adverb from a derivative of the base of ἡδονή ; with pleasure.

G781.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and σοφός ; unwise.

G782.d: from Α (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of σπάω ; to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome.

G783.d: from ἀσπάζομαι ; a greeting (in person or by letter).

G784.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and σπιλόω ; unblemished (physically or morally).

G785.d: of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp".

G786.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σπένδω ; literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless.

G787.d: of Latin origin; an assarius or as , a Roman coin.

G788.d: neuter comparative of the base of ἐγγύς ; more nearly, i.e. very near.

G789.d: probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia MInor.

G790.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of ἵστημι ; to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless.

G791.d: from astu (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome.

G792.d: probably from the base of στρώννυμι ; a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively.

G793.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of στηρίζω ; unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating.

G794.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of stergo (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards kindred.

G795.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and stoichos (an aim); to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth.

G796.d: from ἀστράπτω ; lightning; by analogy, glare.

G797.d: probably from ἀστήρ ; to flash as lightning.

G798.d: neuter from ἀστήρ ; properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial).

G799.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of συγκρίνω ; incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian.

G800.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and σύμφωνος ; inharmonious (figuratively).

G801.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and συνετός ; unintelligent; by implication, wicked.

G802.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of συντίθεμαι ; properly, not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts.

G804.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); secure (literally or figuratively).

G806.d: adverb from ἀσφαλής ; securely (literally or figuratively).

G807.d: from ἀσχήμων ; to be (i.e. act) unbecoming.

G808.d: from ἀσχήμων ; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda.

G809.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of ἔχω (in the sense of its congener σχῆμα ); properly, shapeless, i.e. (figuratively) inelegant.

G810.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of σώζω ; properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication) profligacy.

G811.d: adverb from the same as ἀσωτία ; dissolutely.

G812.d: from ἄτακτος ; to be (i.e. act) irregular.

G813.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of τάσσω ; unarranged, i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously).

G815.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and τέκνον ; childless.

G816.d: from a compound of Α (as a particle of union) and teino (to stretch); to gaze intently.
G816.k: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes

G817.d: a particle probably akin to ἄνευ ; aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or figuratively).

G818.d: from ἄτιμος ; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat.
G818.k: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully

G819.d: from ἄτιμος ; infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity, (objectively) disgrace.

G820.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and τιμή ; (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured.
G820.k: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree)

G821.d: from ἄτιμος ; used like ἀτιμάζω , to maltreat.

G822.d: from the same as ἀήρ ; mist.

G823.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of τομώτερος ; uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time).

G824.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and τόπος ; out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked.

G825.d: from Attalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia.

G827.d: of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn.

G828.d: from Latin ("august"); Augustus , a title of the Roman emperor.

G829.d: from αὐτός and the base of ἡδονή ; self-pleasing, i.e. arrogant.

G830.d: from αὐτός and the same as αἱρετίζω ; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication) voluntary.
G830.k: of own accord, willing of self

G831.d: from a compound of αὐτός and an obsolete hentes (a worker); to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate.

G832.d: from αὐλός ; to play the flute.

G833.d: from the same as ἀήρ ; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion.

G835.d: middle voice from αὐλή ; to pass the night (properly, in the open air).

G836.d: from the same as ἀήρ ; a flute (as blown).

G837.d: a prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), i.e. enlarge (literal or figurative, active or passive).

G839.d: from a derivative of the same as ἀήρ (meaning a breeze, i.e. the morning air); properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of ἡμέρα ) to-morrow.

G840.d: from a (presumed) derivative of the same as ἀήρ (meaning blown); rough (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe.

G841.d: from αὐτάρκης ; self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence.

G842.d: from αὐτός and ἀρκέω ; self-complacent, i.e. contented.

G843.d: from αὐτός and a derivative or κατακρίνω ; self-condemned.

G844.d: from αὐτός and the same as μάτην ; self-moved ("automatic"), i.e. spontaneous.

G845.d: from αὐτός and ὀπτάνομαι ; self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness.

G846.d: from the particle au (perhaps akin to the base of ἀήρ through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the comparative ἑαυτοῦ ) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons. Compare αὑτοῦ .
G846.k: her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-)self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which

G847.d: genitive (i.e. possessive) of αὐτός , used as an adverb of location; properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. in this (or that) place.

G848.d: contracted for ἑαυτοῦ ; self (in some oblique case or reflexively, relation).
G848.k: her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them(-selves), they

G849.d: from αὐτός and χείρ ; self-handed, i.e. doing personally.

G850.d: from auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of ἀήρ ) (dust, as dried by wind); properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure.

G851.d: from ἀπό and αἱρέομαι ; to remove (literally or figuratively).

G852.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and φαίνω ; non-apparent).

G853.d: from ἀφανής ; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed).

G855.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of φαίνω ; non-manifested, i.e. invisible.

G856.d: from a compound of ἀπό and the base of ἑδραῖος ; a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy.

G857.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and φείδομαι ; unsparingness, i.e. austerity (asceticism).

G858.d: from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e. (figuratively) simplicity.

G860.d: from ἅπτομαι ; probably a ligament (as fastening).

G861.d: from ἄφθαρτος ; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness.

G862.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of φθείρω ; undecaying (in essence or continuance).

G863.d: from ἀπό and hiemi (to send; an intensive form of eimi, to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow).
G863.k: cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up

G864.d: from ἀπό and the base of ἱκανός ; to go (i.e. spread) forth (by rumor).

G865.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and φιλάγαθος ; hostile to virtue.
G865.k: despiser of those that are good

G866.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and φιλάργυρος ; unavaricious.
G866.k: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre

G867.d: from ἀφικνέομαι ; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication) departure.

G868.d: from ἀπό and ἵστημι ; to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.
G868.k: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self

G869.d: adverb from ἀφανής (contraction); unawares, i.e. unexpectedly.

G870.d: adverb from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and φόβος ; fearlessly.

G871.d: from ἀπό and ὁμοιόω ; to assimilate closely.

G872.d: from ἀπό and ὁράω ; to consider attentively.

G873.d: from ἀπό and ὁρίζω ; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.

G874.d: from a compound of ἀπό and ὁρμάω ; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively) an opportunity.

G875.d: from ἀφρός ; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy).

G876.d: apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. slaver.

G877.d: from ἄφρων ; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness.

G878.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and φρήν ; properly, mindless, i.e. stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving.

G879.d: from a compound of ἀπό and ὕπνος ; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber.

G880.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and φωνή ; voiceless, i.e. mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning.

G881.d: of Hebrew origin ( אָחָז ); Achaz, an Israelite.

G882.d: of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe.

G883.d: from Ἀχαΐα ; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian.

G884.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of χαρίζομαι ; thankless, i.e. ungrateful.

G885.d: probably of Hebrew origin (compare יוֹקִים ); Achim, an Israelite.

G886.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and χειροποίητος ; unmanufactured, i.e. inartificial.

G887.d: of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract.

G888.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of χρή (compare χρεία ); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious.

G889.d: from ἀχρεῖος ; to render useless, i.e. spoil.

G890.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and χρηστός ; inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental.

G891.d: or achris akh'-rece; akin to ἄκρον (through the idea of a terminus); (of time) until or (of place) up to. Compare μέχρι .
G891.k: as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while

G892.d: perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive).

G893.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and ψεῦδος ; veracious.

G894.d: of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity).

G895.d: from Α (as a negative particle) and ψυχή ; lifeless, i.e. inanimate (mechanical).

G896.d: of Hebrew origin ( בַּ֫עַל ); Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry).

G897.d: of Hebrew origin ( בָּבֶל ); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)).

G898.d: from the same as βάθος ; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of dignity).

G899.d: from the same as βαθύς ; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery.

G901.d: from the base of βάσις ; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively.

G902.d: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of βάσις ; a palm twig (as going out far).

G903.d: of Hebrew origin ( בִּלְעָם ); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher).

G904.d: of Hebrew origin ( בָּלָק ); Balak, a Moabite.

G905.d: probably remotely from βάλλω (as a depository); a pouch (for money).

G906.d: a primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense). Compare ῥίπτω .
G906.k: arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust

G907.d: from a derivative of βάπτω ; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism.

G910.d: from βαπτίζω ; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner.

G911.d: a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye).

G912.d: of Chaldee origin ( גָּאוֹן and אֲבַגְתָא ); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite.

G913.d: of Hebrew origin ( בָּרָק ); Barak, an Israelite.

G914.d: of Hebrew origin ( בֶּרֶכְיָה ); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite.

G915.d: of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e. non-Greek).

G918.d: of Chaldee origin ( בַּר and תַּלְמָי ); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a Christian apostle.

G919.d: of Chaldee origin ( בַּר and יְהוֹשׁ֫וּעַ ); son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite.

G920.d: of Chaldee origin ( בַּר and יוֹנָה ); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite.

G921.d: of Chaldee origin ( בַּר and נְבִיָּאה ); son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite.

G922.d: probably from the same as βάσις (through the notion of going down; compare βάθος ); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority.

G923.d: of Chaldee origin ( בַּר and probably צְבָא ); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites.

G924.d: of Chaldee origin ( בַּר and טָמֵא ); son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite.

G926.d: from the same as βάρος ; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave.

G927.d: from βαρύς and τιμή ; highly valuable.

G931.d: perhaps remotely from the same as βάσις (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture.

G932.d: from βασιλεύς ; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively).

G935.d: probably from βάσις (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively).

G936.d: from βασιλεύς ; to rule (literally or figuratively).

G937.d: from βασιλεύς ; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent.

G939.d: from baino (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot.

G940.d: akin to φάσκω ; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations).

G941.d: perhaps remotely derived from the base of βάσις (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.).

G942.d: of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub.

G943.d: of Hebrew origin ( בָּת ); a bath, or measure for liquids.

G945.d: from Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and λόγος ; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously.

G946.d: from βδελύσσω ; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry.

G948.d: from a (presumed) derivative of bdeo (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry).

G949.d: from the base of βάσις (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively).

G952.d: from the base of βάσις and belos (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked.

G954.d: of Chaldee origin (by parody on בַּ֫עַל זְבוּב ); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan.

G955.d: of Hebrew origin ( בְּלִיַּ֫עַל ); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan.

G956.d: from βάλλω ; a missile, i.e. spear or arrow.

G957.d: neuter of a compound of a derivative of βάλλω (used for the comparative of ἀγαθός ); better.

G958.d: of Hebrew origin ( בִּנְיָמִן ); Benjamin, an Israelite.

G959.d: from a provincial form of φέρω and νίκη ; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family.

G960.d: perhaps a provincial from a derivative of πέραν (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line); Berœa, a place in Macedonia.

G961.d: from Βέροια ; a Berœoean or native of Berœa.

G962.d: of Hebrew origin ( בָּ֫יִת and עֲבָרָה ); ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan.

G963.d: of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine.

G964.d: of Chaldee origin (compare בָּ֫יִת and חָ֫סֶד ); house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem.

G965.d: of Hebrew origin ( בֵּית לְעַפְרָה ); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine.

G966.d: of Chaldee origin (compare בָּ֫יִת and צַיָּדִים ); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine.

G967.d: of Chaldee origin (compare בָּ֫יִת and פַּגֵּי ); fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine.

G968.d: from the base of βάσις ; a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal.

G970.d: probably akin to βίος (through the idea of vital activity); force.

G971.d: from βίος ; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized.

G973.d: from βιάζω ; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic.

G974.d: a diminutive of βιβλίον ; a booklet.

G975.d: a diminutive of βίβλος ; a roll.

G976.d: properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing.

G977.d: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of βόσκω ); to eat.

G978.d: of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia.

G979.d: a primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood.

G981.d: from βιόω ; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode).

G982.d: from a derivative of βιόω ; relating to the present existence.
G982.k: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life

G984.d: a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure.

G985.d: from blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit.

G986.d: perhaps the same as the base of βλαστάνω ; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa.

G987.d: from βλάσφημος ; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously.
G987.k: (speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil

G989.d: from a derivative of βλάπτω and φήμη ; scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God).

G990.d: from βλέπω ; vision (properly concrete; by implication, abstract).

G991.d: a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively). Compare ὀπτάνομαι .
G991.k: behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed

G992.d: from βάλλω ; fit to be cast (i.e. applied).

G993.d: of Chaldee origin ( בְּנֵי and רְגַז ); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles.

G994.d: apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way).

G995.d: from βοάω ; a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.).

G996.d: from βοηθός ; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel.

G997.d: from βοηθός ; to aid or relieve.

G998.d: from βοή and theo (to run); a succorer.

G999.d: akin to βαθύνω ; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern.

G1000.d: from βάλλω ; a throw (as a measure of distance).

G1001.d: from βολίς ; to heave the lead.

G1002.d: from βάλλω ; a missile, i.e. javelin.

G1003.d: of Hebrew origin ( בֹּ֫עַז ); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite.

G1005.d: of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind).

G1006.d: a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare βιβρώσκω , βοῦς ); to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze.

G1007.d: of Hebrew origin ( בְּעוֹר ); Bosor (i.e. Beor), a Moabite.

G1008.d: from βόσκω ; herbage (as if for grazing).

G1009.d: of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes).

G1010.d: from βουλεύω ; an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin.

G1011.d: from βουλή ; to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve.
G1011.k: consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose

G1012.d: from βούλομαι ; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose.

G1014.d: middle voice of a primary verb; to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be willing. Compare θέλω .
G1014.k: be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing)

G2253.d: from a presumed compound of the base of ἥμισυ and θνήσκω ; half dead, i.e. entirely exhausted.

G2254.d: dative case plural of ἐγώ ; to (or for, with, by) us.

G2255.d: neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to ἅμα (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as noun) half.

G2256.d: from the base of ἥμισυ and ὥρα ; a half-hour.

G2257.d: genitive case plural of ἐγώ ; of (or from) us.

G2258.d: imperfect of εἰμί ; I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were).
G2258.k: + agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were

G2259.d: of uncertain affinity; at which time.

G2260.d: from ἤ and περ ; than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed).

G2261.d: probably from ἔπος ; properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind.

G2262.d: of Hebrew origin ( עֵר ); Er, an Israelite.

G2263.d: perhaps by transposition from ἔρημος (through the idea of stillness); tranquil.

G2264.d: compound of heros (a "hero") and εἶδος ; heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings.

G2265.d: plural of a derivative of Ἡρώδης ; Herodians, i.e. partisans of Herod.

G2266.d: from Ἡρώδης ; Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family.

G2268.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְשַׁעְיָה ); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite.

G2269.d: of Hebrew origin ( עֵשָׂו ); Esau, an Edomite.

G2270.d: from the same as ἡσύχιος ; to keep still (intransitively), i.e. refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech.
G2270.k: cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest

G2271.d: feminine of ἡσύχιος ; (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language.

G2272.d: a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of ἑδραῖος and perhaps ἔχω ; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing).

G2273.d: from ἤ and τοί ; either indeed.

G2274.d: from the same as ἥττον ; to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower.

G2275.d: from ἡττάω ; a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss.

G2276.d: neuter of comparative of heka (slightly) used for that of κακός ; worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb).

G2277.d: third person singular imperative of εἰμί ; let him (or it) be.

G2278.d: from ἦχος ; to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate.

G2279.d: of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar; figuratively, a rumor.

G2280.d: of uncertain origin; Thaddæus, one of the Apostles.

G2281.d: probably prolonged from ἅλς ; the sea (genitive case or specially).

G2282.d: probably akin to thallo (to warm); to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to foster.

G2283.d: of Hebrew origin ( תָּמָר ); Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess.

G2284.d: from θάμβος ; to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. astound.

G2285.d: akin to an obsolete tapho (to dumbfound); stupefaction (by surprise), i.e. astonishment.

G2287.d: from (the feminine form of) θάνατος and φέρω ; death-bearing, i.e. fatal.

G2288.d: from θνήσκω ; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively).

G2289.d: from θάνατος to kill (literally or figuratively).
G2289.k: become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify

G2290.d: a primary verb; to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter.

G2291.d: of Hebrew origin ( תָּ֫רַח ); Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham.

G2292.d: another form for θαρσέω ; to exercise courage. Compare τολμάω .
G2292.k: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident

G2293.d: from θάρσος ; to have courage. Compare θαῤῥέω .

G2295.d: apparently from a form of θεάομαι ; wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract).

G2296.d: from θαῦμα ; to wonder; by implication, to admire.
G2296.k: admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder

G2297.d: from θαῦμα ; wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle.

G2298.d: from θαυμάζω ; wondered at, i.e. (by implication) wonderful.

G2299.d: feminine of θεός ; a female deity.

G2300.d: a prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit. Compare ὀπτάνομαι .

G2301.d: from θέατρον ; to expose as a spectacle.

G2302.d: from θεάομαι ; a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively).

G2303.d: probably neuter of θεῖος (in its original sense of flashing); sulphur.

G2304.d: from θεός ; godlike (neuter as noun, divinity).

G2306.d: from θεῖον and εἶδος ; sulphur-like, i.e. sulphurous.

G2307.d: from the prolonged form of θέλω ; a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination.

G2308.d: from θέλω ; determination (properly, the act), i.e. option.

G2309.d: or ethelo , in certain tenses theleo , and etheleo , which are otherwise obsolete apparently strengthened from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι ; to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas βούλομαι properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in.
G2309.k: desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly))

G2310.d: from a derivative of τίθημι ; something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively).

G2311.d: from θεμέλιος ; to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate.

G2312.d: from θεός and διδάσκω ; divinely instructed.

G2314.d: from θεός and μάχομαι ; an opponent of deity.

G2315.d: from θεός and a presumed derivative of πνέω ; divinely breathed in.

G2316.d: of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with ὁ ) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very.

G2318.d: from θεός and σέβομαι ; reverent of God, i.e. pious.

G2319.d: from θεός and the base of στυγνητός ; hateful to God, i.e. impious.

G2321.d: from θεός and φίλος ; friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian.

G2322.d: from θεραπεύω ; attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics.

G2323.d: from the same as θεράπων ; to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease).

G2324.d: apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of θέρος ; a menial attendant (as if cherishing).

G2325.d: from θέρος (in the sense of the crop); to harvest.

G2326.d: from θερίζω ; reaping, i.e. the crop.

G2329.d: from the base of θέρος ; warmth.

G2330.d: from a primary thero (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. summer.

G2331.d: from Θεσσαλονίκη ; a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice.

G2332.d: from Thessalos (a Thessalian) and νίκη ; Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor.

G2333.d: of uncertain origin; Theudas, an Israelite.

G2334.d: from a derivative of θεάομαι (perhaps by addition of ὁράω ); to be a spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge)). Compare ὀπτάνομαι .
G2334.k: behold, consider, look on, perceive, see

G2335.d: from the same as θεωρέω ; spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle.

G2336.d: from τίθημι ; a receptacle, i.e. scabbard.

G2337.d: from thele (the nipple); to suckle, (by implication) to suck.

G2338.d: from the same as θηλάζω ; female.

G2339.d: from ther (a wild animal, as game); hunting, i.e. (figuratively) destruction.

G2340.d: from θήρα ; to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at.

G2341.d: from a compound of θηρίον and μάχομαι ; to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men).

G2342.d: diminutive from the same as θήρα ; a dangerous animal.

G2343.d: from θησαυρός ; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively).
G2343.k: lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up)

G2344.d: from τίθημι ; a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or figuratively).

G2345.d: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary thigo (to finger); to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure.

G2346.d: akin to the base of τρίβος ; to crowd (literally or figuratively).
G2346.k: afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble

G2347.k: afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble

G2348.d: a strengthened form of a simpler primary thano than'-o (which is used for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or figuratively).

G2350.d: from θόρυβος ; to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor.
G2350.k: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar

G2351.d: from the base of θροέω ; a disturbance.

G2352.d: a primary verb; to crush. Compare ῥήγνυμι .

G2353.d: from τρέφω ; stock (as raised on a farm).

G2355.d: from the base of θροέω ; wailing.

G2356.d: from a derivative of θρησκός ; ceremonial observance.

G2357.d: probably from the base of θροέω ; ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious.

G2358.d: from a prolonged compound of the base of θροέω ; and a derivative of ἅπτομαι (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory.

G2359.d: genitive case trichos, etc.; of uncertain derivation; hair. Compare κόμη .

G2360.d: from threomai to wail; to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten.

G2361.d: perhaps from τρέφω (in the sense of thickening); a clot.

G2362.d: from thrao (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate.

G2363.d: of uncertain derivation; Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor.

G2364.d: apparently a primary word (compare "daughter"); a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant).

G2366.d: from θύω (in the sense of blowing) a storm.

G2367.d: from a derivative of θύω (in the sense of blowing; denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood.

G2368.d: from θυμιάω ; an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself.

G2369.d: from a derivative of θυμιάω ; a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple).

G2370.d: from a derivative of θύω (in the sense of smoking); to fumigate, i.e. offer aromatic fumes.

G2371.d: from a presumed compound of θυμός and μάχομαι ; to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated.

G2372.d: from θύω ; passion (as if breathing hard). Compare ψυχή .

G2373.d: from θυμός ; to put in a passion, i.e. enrage.

G2374.d: apparently a primary word (compare "door"); a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively).

G2375.d: from θύρα ; a large shield (as door-shaped).

G2376.d: from θύρα ; an aperture, i.e. window.

G2377.d: from θύρα and ouros (a watcher); a gate- warden.

G2378.d: from θύω ; sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or figuratively).

G2379.d: from a derivative of θυσία ; a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative).

G2380.d: a primary verb; properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose).

G2381.d: of Chaldee origin (compare תְאוֹמִים ); the twin; Thomas, a Christian.

G2382.d: of uncertain affinity; the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet.

G2383.d: of Hebrew origin ( יָאּיר ); Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite.

G2384.d: of Hebrew origin ( יַעֲקֹב ); Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the Israelites; also an Israelite.

G2385.d: the same as Ἰακώβ Græcized; Jacobus, the name of three Israelites.

G2387.d: of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian.

G2388.d: probably of Hebrew origin (compare יָנָה ); Janna, an Israelite.

G2389.d: of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian.

G2390.d: middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure (literally or figuratively).

G2391.d: of Hebrew origin ( יָ֫רֶד ); Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian.

G2393.d: probably of foreign origin (see יָשְׁפֵה ); "jasper", a gem.

G2394.d: future active participle masculine of ἰάομαι ; about to cure; Jason, a Christian.

G2396.d: second person singular imperative active of εἴδω ; used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!.

G2397.d: from εἴδω ; a sight (comparative figuratively "idea"), i.e. aspect.

G2398.d: of uncertain affinity; pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by implication, private or separate.
G2398.k: X his acquaintance, when they were alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our, thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their (own)

G2399.d: from ἴδιος ; a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot").

G2400.d: second person singular imperative middle voice of εἴδω ; used as imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see.

G2401.d: of Hebrew origin ( אֱדוֹם ); Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine.

G2402.d: a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat); perspiration.

G2403.d: of Hebrew origin ( אּיזָ֫בֶל ); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher).

G2404.d: from ἱερός and πόλις ; holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor.

G2405.d: from ἱερατεύω ; priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function.
G2405.k: office of the priesthood, priest's office

G2406.d: from ἱερατεύω ; the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively).

G2407.d: prolongation from ἱερεύς ; to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions.

G2408.d: of Hebrew origin ( יִרְמְיָה ); Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an Israelite.

G2409.d: from ἱερός ; a priest (literally or figuratively).

G2410.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְרֵחוֹ ); Jericho, a place in Palestine.

G2411.d: neuter of ἱερός ; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas ναός denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere).

G2412.d: from ἱερός and the same as πρέπω ; reverent.

G2414.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְרוּשָׁלַ֫םִ ); Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine. Compare Ἱερουσαλήμ .

G2415.d: from Ἱεροσόλυμα ; a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma.

G2416.d: from ἱερόσυλος ; to be a temple-robber (figuratively).

G2417.d: from ἱερόν and συλάω ; a temple-despoiler.

G2418.d: from a compound of ἱερόν and the base of ἔργον ; to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively).

G2419.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְרוּשָׁלַ֫םִ ); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine. Compare Ἱεροσόλυμα .

G2420.d: from ἱερός ; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office.

G2421.d: of Hebrew origin ( יִשַׁי ); Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite.

G2422.d: of Hebrew origin ( יִפְתָּח ); Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite.

G2423.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְכָנְיָה ); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite.

G2424.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְהוֹשׁ֫וּעַ ); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites.

G2425.d: from hiko (hikano or hikneomai, akin to ἥκω ) (to arrive); competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character).
G2425.k: able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy

G2427.d: from ἱκανός ; to enable, i.e. qualify.

G2428.d: from a derivative of the base of ἱκανός (through the idea of approaching for a favor); intreaty.

G2430.d: perhaps from εἰκών ; image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor.

G2431.d: from the same as ἵλεως ; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing.

G2433.d: middle voice from the same as ἵλεως ; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious.

G2435.d: neuter of a derivative of ἱλάσκομαι ; an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple).

G2436.d: perhaps from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι ; cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it.

G2437.d: neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation; (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe.

G2438.d: perhaps from the same as ἅμα ; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge).

G2440.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); a dress (inner or outer).
G2440.k: apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture

G2442.d: middle voice from himeros (a yearning; of uncertain affinity); to long for.

G2443.d: probably from the same as the former part of ἑαυτοῦ (through the demonstrative idea; compare ὁ ); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result). Compare ἵνα μή .
G2443.k: albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to

G2444.d: from ἵνα and τίς ; for what reason ?, i.e. why?.

G2445.d: of Hebrew origin ( יָפוֹ ); Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine.

G2446.d: of Hebrew origin ( יַרְדֵּן ); the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine.

G2447.d: perhaps from eimi (to go) or hiemi (to send); rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents).

G2448.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְהוּדָה or perhaps יֻטָּה ); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine.

G2449.d: feminine of Ἰουδαῖος (with γῆ implied); the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine.

G2450.d: from Ἰουδαῖος ; to become a Judæan, i.e. "Judaize".

G2451.d: from Ἰουδαῖος ; Judaïc, i.e. resembling a Judæan.

G2452.d: adverb from Ἰουδαϊκός ; Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan.

G2453.d: from Ἰουδά (in the sense of Ἰούδας as a country); Judæan, i.e. belonging to Jehudah.

G2454.d: from Ἰουδαΐζω ; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages.

G2455.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְהוּדָה ); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region.

G2456.d: feminine of the same as Ἰούλιος ; Julia, a Christian woman.

G2457.d: of Latin origin; Julius, a centurion.

G2458.d: of Latin origin; Junias, a Christian.

G2459.d: of Latin origin ("just"); Justus, the name of three Christian.

G2460.d: from ἵππος ; an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps.

G2461.d: neuter of a derivative of ἵππος ; the cavalry force.

G2463.d: perhaps from ἐρέω (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities); a rainbow ("iris").

G2464.d: of Hebrew origin ( יִצְחָק ); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham.

G2465.d: from ἴσος and ἄγγελος ; like an angel, i.e. angelic.

G2466.d: of Hebrew origin ( יִשָּׂשָׂכָר ); Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant).

G2467.d: assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of εἴδω ; to know.

G2468.d: second person imperative present of εἰμί ; be thou.
G2468.k: + agree, be, X give thyself wholly to

G2469.d: of Hebrew origin (probably אּישׁ and קִרְיָא ); inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor.

G2470.d: probably from εἴδω (through the idea of seeming); similar (in amount and kind).

G2471.d: likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity.

G2472.d: from ἴσος and τιμή ; of equal value or honor.

G2473.d: from ἴσος and ψυχή ; of similar spirit.

G2474.d: of Hebrew origin ( יִשְׂרָאֵל ); Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively).

G2475.d: from Ἰσραήλ ; an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively).

G2476.d: a prolonged form of a primary stao stah'-o (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses); to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively). Compare τίθημι .
G2476.k: abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up)

G2477.d: from a derivative of εἴδω ; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview).

G2478.k: boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant

G2479.d: from a derivative of is (force; compare eschon, a form of ἔχω ); forcefulness (literally or figuratively).

G2480.d: from ἰσχύς ; to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively).
G2480.k: be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work

G2481.d: adverb from ἴσος ; likely, i.e. perhaps.

G2482.d: probably of foreign origin; Italia, a region of Europe.

G2483.d: from Ἰταλία ; Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia.

G2484.d: of Hebrew origin ( יְטוּר ); Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine.

G2485.d: diminutive from ἰχθύς ; a petty fish.

G2487.d: from ikneomai (to arrive; compare ἥκω ); a track (figuratively).

G2488.d: of Hebrew origin ( יוֹתָם ); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite.

G2489.d: feminine of the same as Ἰωάννης ; Joanna, a Christian.

G2490.d: a form of Ἰωάννης ; Joannas, an Israelite.

G2491.d: of Hebrew origin ( יוֹחָנָן ); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites.

G2492.d: of Hebrew origin ( אּיּוֹב ); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch.

G2493.d: of Hebrew origin ( יוֹאֵל ); Joel, an Israelite.
