G4350.d: from πρός and κόπτω ; to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively).

G4351.d: from πρός and κυλιόω ; to roll towards, i.e. block against.

G4352.d: from πρός and a probable derivative of κύων (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore).

G4354.d: from πρός and λαλέω ; to talk to, i.e. converse with.

G4355.d: from πρός and λαμβάνω ; to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality).

G4357.d: from πρός and μένω ; to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in.
G4357.k: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with)

G4358.d: from πρός and a derivative of the same as ὁρμή (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at.

G4359.d: from πρός and ὀφείλω ; to be indebted additionally.

G4360.d: from πρός and a form of ochtheo (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at.

G4361.d: from πρός and the same as πεινάω ; hungering further, i.e. intensely hungry.

G4362.d: from πρός and πήγνυμι ; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross).

G4363.d: from πρός and πίπτω ; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm).

G4364.d: middle voice from πρός and ποιέω ; to do forward for oneself, i.e. pretend (as if about to do a thing).

G4365.d: from πρός and πορεύομαι ; to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as προπορεύομαι ).

G4366.d: from πρός and ῥήγνυμι ; to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood).

G4367.d: from πρός and τάσσω ; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin.

G4368.d: feminine of a derivative of προΐστημι ; a patroness, i.e. assistant.

G4369.d: from πρός and τίθημι ; to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex, repeat.
G4369.k: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more

G4370.d: from πρός and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join.

G4371.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of πρός and φάγω ; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare ὀψάριον ).

G4372.d: from πρό and a derivative of σφάζω ; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made.

G4374.d: from πρός and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat.
G4374.k: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to

G4375.d: from a presumed compound of πρός and φιλέω ; friendly towards, i.e. acceptable.

G4376.d: from προσφέρω ; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice.

G4377.d: from πρός and φωνέω ; to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim, summon.

G4378.d: from a comparative of πρός and cheo (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e. affusion.

G4379.d: from πρός and psauo (to touch); to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in order to relieve).

G4380.d: from προσωπολήπτης ; to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality.

G4381.d: from πρόσωπον and λαμβάνω ; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality.

G4383.d: from πρός and ops (the visage, from ὀπτάνομαι ); the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person.
G4383.k: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence

G4384.d: from πρό and τάσσω ; to pre-arrange, i.e. prescribe.

G4385.d: from πρό and teino (to stretch); to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging).

G4386.d: neuter of πρότερος as adverb (with or without the article); previously.

G4387.d: comparative of πρό ; prior or previous.

G4388.d: middle voice from πρό and τίθημι ; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine).

G4389.d: middle voice from πρό and the base of τροπή ; to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage.

G4390.d: from πρό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede.

G4391.d: from πρό and ὑπάρχω ; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously.

G4392.d: from a compound of πρό and φαίνω ; an outward showing, i.e. pretext.

G4393.d: from πρό and φέρω ; to bear forward, i.e. produce.

G4395.d: from προφήτης ; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office.

G4396.d: from a compound of πρό and φημί ; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet.

G4397.d: from προφήτης ; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic").

G4398.d: feminine of προφήτης ; a female foreteller or an inspired woman.

G4399.d: from πρό and φθάνω ; to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate.

G4400.d: middle voice from πρό and a derivative of χείρ ; to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose.

G4401.d: from πρό and χειροτονέω ; to elect in advance.

G4402.d: from πρό and χορός ; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian.

G4403.d: feminine of prumnus (hindmost); the stern of a ship.

G4404.d: adverb from πρό ; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch.

G4405.d: feminine of a derivative of πρωΐ as noun; day-dawn.

G4406.d: from πρωΐ ; dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season).

G4407.d: from πρωΐ ; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal.

G4408.d: feminine of a presumed derivative of πρό as noun; the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel.

G4409.d: from πρῶτος ; to be first (in rank or influence).

G4410.d: from πρῶτος and καθέδρα ; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council.

G4411.d: from πρῶτος and κλισία ; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals.

G4412.d: neuter of πρῶτος as adverb (with or without ὁ ); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance).
G4412.k: before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all)

G4413.d: contracted superlative of πρό ; foremost (in time, place, order or importance).
G4413.k: before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former

G4414.d: from πρῶτος and ἵστημι ; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion).

G4416.d: from πρῶτος and the alternate of τίκτω ; first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively).

G4417.d: a form of πίπτω ; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation).

G4419.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of πτέρυξ ; a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner).

G4420.d: from a derivative of πέτομαι (meaning a feather); a wing.

G4422.d: probably akin to the alternate of πίπτω (through the idea of causing to fall) or to πέτομαι (through that of causing to fly away); to scare.

G4424.d: from Ptolemaios (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine.

G4425.d: from πτύω ; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle).

G4426.d: from a presumed derivative of πτύω (and thus akin to πτοέω ); to frighten.

G4428.d: probably akin to petannumi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to πέτομαι through the idea of expansion, and to πτύω through that of flattening; compare πατέω ); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll.

G4429.d: a primary verb (compare πτύσσω ); to spit.

G4430.d: from the alternate of πίπτω ; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion).

G4431.d: from the alternate of πίπτω ; a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or figuratively).

G4432.d: from πτωχεύω ; beggary, i.e. indigence (literally or figuratively).

G4433.d: from πτωχός ; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively).

G4434.d: from ptosso (to crouch); akin to πτοέω and the alternate of πίπτω ); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas πένης properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed).

G4435.d: from a primary pux (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing).

G4436.d: from Putho (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying).

G4437.d: from the same as σκηνοποιός ; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently.

G4438.d: from a derivative of the same as πυγμή ; to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively).

G4439.d: apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively).

G4440.d: from πύλη ; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule.

G4441.d: middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from ἐρωτάω , which properly means a request as a favor; and from αἰτέω , which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from ζητέω , which implies a search for something hidden; and from δέομαι , which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence).

G4442.d: a primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning).

G4444.d: apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle.

G4445.d: from πυρά ; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever.

G4446.d: from πυρέσσω ; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever).

G4447.d: from πυρά ; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming.

G4448.d: from πῦρ ; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust).
G4448.k: burn, fiery, be on fire, try

G4450.d: from πῦρ ; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored.

G4451.d: from πυρόω ; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test).

G4452.d: another form of the base of -πώς ; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See μηδέπω , μήπω , οὐδέπω , οὔπω , πώποτε .

G4453.d: probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell.

G4454.d: apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass.

G4455.d: from -πω and ποτέ ; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time.
G4455.k: at any time, + never (…to any man), + yet, never man

G4456.d: apparently from poros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous).

G4458.d: adverb from the base of πού ; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition. See εἴ πως , μήπως . Compare πῶς .

G4459.d: adverb from the base of ποῦ ; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!. (Occasionally unexpressed in English).

G4460.d: of Hebrew origin ( רָחָב ); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess. See also Ῥαχάβ .

G4461.d: of Hebrew origin ( רָב with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor.

G4462.d: or rhabbouni of Chaldee origin; corresponding to ῥαββί.

G4463.d: from ῥάβδος ; to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado.

G4464.d: from the base of ῥαπίζω ; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty).

G4465.d: from ῥάβδος and ἔχω ; a rod- (the Latin fasces ) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner).

G4466.d: of Hebrew origin ( רְעוּ ); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch.

G4467.d: from a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and ἔργον ; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime.

G4468.d: from the same as ῥᾳδιούργημα ; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity.

G4469.d: of Chaldee origin (compare רֵק ); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification).

G4470.d: from ῥήγνυμι ; a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth.

G4471.d: of Hebrew origin ( רָמָה ); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine.

G4472.d: from a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively).

G4474.d: from a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, "rap"); to slap. Compare τύπτω .
G4474.k: smite (with the palm of the hand)

G4475.k: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand

G4476.d: from a primary rhapto (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω through the idea of puncturing); a needle.

G4477.d: from the same as Ῥαάβ ; Rachab, a Canaanitess.

G4478.d: of Hebrew origin ( רָחֵל ); Rachel, the wife of Jacob.

G4479.d: of Hebrew origin ( רִבְקָה ); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac.

G4480.d: of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding).

G4481.d: by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin ( כִּיּוּן ); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol.

G4482.d: a primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form rheuo is used; to flow ("run"; as water).

G4483.d: for certain tenses of which a prolonged form ereo is used; and both as alternate for ἔπω perhaps akin (or identical) with ῥέω (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. speak or say. Compare λέγω .

G4484.d: of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy.

G4485.d: from ῥήγνυμι ; something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall).

G4486.d: or rhesso both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi (see in κατάγνυμι )) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; κατάγνυμι being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and θραύω a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like λύω ) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions.

G4487.d: from ῥέω ; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever.

G4488.d: probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for רְפָיָה ); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite.

G4489.d: from ῥέω ; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate.

G4490.d: adverb from a derivative of ῥέω ; out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly.

G4491.d: apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively).

G4492.d: from ῥίζα ; to root (figuratively, become stable).

G4493.d: from ῥίπτω ; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant).

G4494.d: from a derivative of ῥίπτω (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves).

G4495.d: from a derivative of ῥίπτω ; to toss up.

G4496.d: a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω , through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from βάλλω , which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from teino (see in ἐκτείνω ), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse.

G4497.d: of Hebrew origin ( רְחַבְעָם ); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite.

G4498.d: probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl.

G4499.d: probably from rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean.

G4500.d: adverb from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash.

G4501.d: probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively).

G4502.d: of Hebrew origin ( רְאוּבֵן ); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite.

G4503.d: of Hebrew origin ( רוּת ); Ruth, a Moabitess.

G4504.d: of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian.

G4505.d: prolongation from ῥύομαι in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded).

G4506.d: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to ῥέω (through the idea of a current; compare ῥύσις ); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue.

G4508.d: from ῥύπος ; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked.

G4509.d: of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity.

G4510.d: from ῥύπος ; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally).

G4511.d: from ῥύομαι in the sense of its congener ῥέω ; a flux (of blood).

G4512.d: from ῥύομαι ; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face).

G4514.d: from Ῥώμη ; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun).

G4515.d: adverb from a presumed derivative of Ῥώμη ; Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language.

G4516.d: from the base of ῥώννυμι ; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy.

G4517.d: prolongation from rhoomai (to dart; probably akin to ῥύομαι ); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye).

G4518.d: of Chaldee or ( שְׁבַק with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress.

G4519.d: of Hebrew origin ( צָבָא in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God.

G4520.d: from a derivative of σάββατον ; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven).

G4521.d: of Hebrew origin ( שַׁבָּת ); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications.

G4522.d: from a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing.

G4523.d: probably from Σαδώκ ; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite.

G4524.d: of Hebrew origin ( צָדוֹק ); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite.

G4525.d: akin to σείω ; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb).

G4526.d: of Hebrew origin ( שָׂק ); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief).

G4527.d: of Hebrew origin ( שָׁ֫לַח ); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch.

G4528.d: of Hebrew origin ( שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל ); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite.

G4529.d: probably from σάλος (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus.

G4530.d: probably from the same as σαλεύω ; Salim, a place in Palestine.

G4531.d: from σάλος ; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite.
G4531.k: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up

G4532.d: of Hebrew origin ( שָׁלֵם ); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine.

G4533.d: of Hebrew origin ( שַׂלְמוֹן ); Salmon, an Israelite.

G4534.d: perhaps of similar origin to Σαλαμίς ; Salmone, a place in Crete.

G4535.d: probably from the base of σαίνω ; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow.

G4536.d: perhaps from σάλος (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet.

G4537.d: from σάλπιγξ ; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively).

G4539.d: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from שָׁלוֹם ); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess.

G4540.d: of Hebrew origin ( שֹׁמְרוֹן ); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine.

G4541.d: from Σαμάρεια ; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria.

G4542.d: feminine of Σαμαρείτης ; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria.

G4543.d: from Σάμος and Thraike (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean.

G4544.d: of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean.

G4545.d: of Hebrew origin ( שְׁמוּאֵל ); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite.

G4546.d: of Hebrew origin ( שִׁמְשׁוֹן ); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite.

G4547.d: neuter of a derivative of sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad.

G4549.d: of Hebrew origin ( שָׁאוּל ); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul. Compare Σαῦλος .

G4550.d: from σήπω ; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally). Compare πονηρός .

G4551.d: feminine of σάπφειρος ; Sapphire, an Israelitess.

G4552.d: of Hebrew origin ( סַפִּיר ); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem.

G4553.d: apparently of Hebrew origin ( שָׂרַג ); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work.

G4554.d: plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor.

G4555.d: from the same as σάρδιος ; sardine ( λίθος being implied), i.e. a gem, so called.

G4556.d: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian ( λίθος being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called.

G4557.d: from the base of σάρδιος and onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called.

G4558.d: of Hebrew origin ( צָרְפַת ); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine.

G4559.d: from σάρξ ; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate.

G4560.d: from σάρξ ; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft.

G4561.d: probably from the base of σαρόω ; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such).

G4562.d: of Hebrew origin ( שְׂרוּג ); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch.

G4563.d: from a derivative of sairo (to brush off; akin to σύρω ); meaning a broom; to sweep.

G4564.d: of Hebrew origin ( שָׂרָה ); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham.

G4565.d: of Hebrew origin ( NONE ); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine.

G4566.d: of Hebrew origin ( שָׂטָן ); Satan, i.e. the devil. Compare Σατανᾶς .

G4567.d: of Chaldee origin corresponding to מַעְבָּדִים (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil.

G4568.d: of Hebrew origin ( סְאָה־ ); a certain measure for things dry.

G4569.d: of Hebrew origin, the same as Σαούλ ; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul.

G4570.d: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively).

G4571.d: accusative case singular of σύ ; thee.

G4572.d: genitive case from σέ and αὐτός , also dative case of the same, seautoi , and accusative case seauton , likewise contracted sautou , sautoi , and sauton , respectively; of (with, to) thyself.

G4573.d: middle voice from a derivative of σέβομαι ; to venerate, i.e. adore.

G4574.d: from σεβάζομαι ; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc).

G4575.d: from σεβάζομαι ; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial.

G4576.d: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore.

G4577.d: probably from σύρω through its congener eiro (to fasten; akin to αἱρέομαι ); a chain (as binding or drawing).

G4578.d: from σείω ; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake.

G4579.d: apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern).

G4580.d: of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian.

G4581.d: from Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria.

G4582.d: from selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι , through the idea of attractiveness); the moon.

G4583.d: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of σελήνη ; to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy.

G4584.d: of Hebrew origin ( שִׁמְעִי ); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite.

G4585.d: probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour.

G4588.d: of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman.

G4589.d: of Hebrew origin ( שֵׁת ); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch.

G4590.d: of Hebrew origin ( שֵׁם ); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch.

G4591.d: from sema (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate.

G4592.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of σημαίνω ; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally.

G4593.d: from σημεῖον ; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance).

G4594.d: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ὁ (t changed to s) and ἡμέρα ; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto).

G4595.d: apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish.

G4596.d: from Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric).

G4597.d: apparently of Hebrew origin ( סָס ); a moth.

G4598.d: from σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω ; moth-eaten.

G4599.d: from sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of ἵστημι ); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power).

G4600.d: of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face.

G4601.d: from σιγή ; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively).

G4602.d: apparently from sizo (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence. Compare σιωπάω .

G4605.d: of Hebrew origin ( צִידוֹן ); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine.

G4606.d: from Σιδών ; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon.

G4607.d: of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans). Compare φονεύς .

G4608.d: of Hebrew origin ( שֵׁכָר ); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor.

G4609.d: contraction for Σιλουανός ; Silas, a Christian.

G4610.d: of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian. Compare Σίλας .

G4611.d: of Hebrew origin ( שִׁלֹ֫חַ ); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem.

G4612.d: of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron).

G4613.d: of Hebrew origin ( שִׁמְעוֹן ); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites. Compare Συμεών .

G4614.d: of Hebrew origin ( סִינַי ); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia.

G4615.d: perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant).

G4616.d: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it).

G4618.d: from a derivative of σῖτος ; grain-fed, i.e. fattened.

G4619.d: from a derivative of σῖτος ; grained, i.e. fatted.

G4620.d: from σῖτος and μέτρον ; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food).

G4621.d: also plural irregular neuter sita of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat.

G4622.d: of Hebrew origin ( צִיּוֹן ); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant).

G4623.d: from siope (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from σιγή , which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like κωφός properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water).

G4624.d: from σκάνδαλον ; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure).

G4625.d: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of κάμπτω ; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin).
G4625.k: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock

G4626.d: apparently a primary verb; to dig.

G4627.d: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing).

G4628.d: apparently from skello (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank).

G4629.d: from a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of σκοπός through the idea of noticeableness); clothing.

G4630.d: apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite.

G4631.d: from σκεῦος ; furniture, i.e. spare tackle.

G4632.d: of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]).

G4633.d: apparently akin to σκεῦος and σκιά ; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively).

G4634.d: from σκῆνος and πήγνυμι ; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes).

G4635.d: from σκηνή and ποιέω ; a manufacturer of tents.

G4636.d: from σκηνή ; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit).

G4637.d: from σκῆνος ; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion).

G4638.d: from σκηνόω ; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul).

G4639.d: apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)).

G4640.d: akin to skairo (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus).

G4641.d: feminine of a compound of σκληρός and καρδία ; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception.

G4642.d: from the base of σκέλος ; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe).

G4644.d: from σκληρός and τράχηλος ; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate.

G4645.d: from σκληρός ; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn.

G4646.d: from the base of σκέλος ; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse.

G4647.d: perhaps from the base of σκέλος and ὀπτάνομαι ; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability).

G4648.d: from σκοπός ; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard. Compare ὀπτάνομαι .
G4648.k: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark

G4649.d: from skeptomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to σκάπτω through the idea of concealment; compare σκέπασμα ); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal.

G4650.d: apparently from the same as σκορπίος (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal.

G4651.d: probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of σκοπός and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting).

G4653.d: from σκότος ; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively).

G4654.d: from σκότος ; to obscure (literally or figuratively).

G4655.d: from the base of σκιά ; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively).

G4656.d: from σκότος ; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively).

G4657.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of εἰς and κύων and βάλλω ; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure).

G4658.d: probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage.

G4659.d: from skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι ; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance.

G4660.d: apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass.

G4661.d: neuter from σκύλλω ; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty.

G4662.d: from σκώληξ and a derivative of βιβρώσκω ; worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots.

G4663.d: of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm.

G4665.d: of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called.

G4667.d: the same as σμύρνα ; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor.

G4669.d: from Σμύρνα ; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic).

G4670.d: plural of Hebrew origin ( סְדֹם ); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine.

G4671.d: dative case of σύ ; to thee.

G4672.d: of Hebrew origin ( שְׁלֹמֹה ); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David.

G4673.d: probably akin to the base of σωρεύω ; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier.

G4675.d: genitive case of σύ ; of thee, thy.
G4675.k: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy

G4676.d: of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse).

G4677.d: of Hebrew origin ( שׁוֹשָׁן feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess.

G4678.d: from σοφός ; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual).

G4679.d: from σοφός ; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error.

G4680.d: akin to saphes (clear); wise (in a most general application). Compare φρόνιμος .

G4681.d: probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe.

G4682.d: prolongation from spairo (to grasp; apparently strengthened from σπάω through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy.

G4683.d: from sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of σπαράσσω meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom).

G4686.d: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of αἱρέομαι in the sense of its cognate εἱλίσσω ; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors).

G4687.d: probably strengthened from σπάω (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively).

G4688.d: of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman).

G4689.d: apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend").

G4690.d: from σπείρω ; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting).

G4691.d: from σπέρμα and λέγω ; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk).

G4692.d: probably strengthened from πούς ; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly.

G4693.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort.

G4694.d: of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea.

G4695.d: from σπίλος ; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively).

G4696.d: of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace.

G4697.d: middle voice from σπλάγχνον ; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity.

G4698.d: probably strengthened from splen (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy.

G4701.d: from σπείρω ; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage.

G4702.d: from σπόρος ; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field.

G4703.d: from σπείρω ; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown).

G4704.d: from σπουδή ; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest.
G4704.k: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study

G4706.d: neuter of σπουδαιότερος as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly.

G4707.d: comparative of σπουδαῖος ; more prompt, more earnest.

G4708.d: adverb from σπουδαιότερος ; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise.

G4710.d: from σπεύδω ; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness.

G4711.d: from σπείρω (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle.

G4712.d: or masculine (in plural) stadios from the base of ἵστημι (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course.

G4713.d: from the base of ἵστημι (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank.

G4714.d: from the base of ἵστημι ; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy.

G4715.d: from the base of καύχησις ; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin.

G4716.d: from the base of ἵστημι ; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ.

G4717.d: from σταυρός ; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness.

G4718.d: probably from the base of στέφανος ; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined).

G4719.d: from the base of ἵστημι ; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk).

G4720.d: the same as στάχυς ; Stachys, a Christian.

G4721.d: strengthened from a primary tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof.

G4722.d: from στέγη ; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently).

G4723.d: a contraction from στερεός (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile".

G4724.d: probably strengthened from the base of ἵστημι ; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with).

G4725.d: from the base of στέφανος ; a wreath for show.

G4727.d: from στενός ; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly.

G4728.d: probably from the base of ἵστημι ; narrow (from obstacles standing close about).

G4729.d: from the same as στενοχωρία ; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp.

G4730.d: from a compound of στενός and χώρα ; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity.

G4731.d: from ἵστημι ; stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively).

G4732.d: from στερεός ; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively).

G4733.d: from στερεόω ; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability).

G4734.d: probably contraction for stephanotos (crowned; from στεφανόω ); Stephanas, a Christian.

G4735.d: from an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, διάδημα ), literally or figuratively.

G4736.d: the same as στέφανος ; Stephanus, a Christian.

G4737.d: from στέφανος ; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively).

G4738.d: from ἵστημι (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest.

G4739.d: from the perfect tense of ἵστημι ; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere.

G4741.d: from a presumed derivative of ἵστημι (like στερεός ); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm.

G4742.d: from a primary stizo (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service.

G4743.d: feminine of στίγμα ; a point of time, i.e. an instant.

G4744.d: apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. flash intensely.

G4745.d: probably from ἵστημι ; a colonnade or interior piazza.

G4746.d: from a primary steibo (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed.

G4747.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of στοιχέω ; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively).

G4748.d: from a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety.

G4749.d: from στέλλω ; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity).

G4750.d: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of τομώτερος ; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon).

G4751.d: from στόμα ; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach".

G4752.d: from στρατεύομαι ; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger).

G4753.d: from στρατεύομαι ; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic).

G4754.d: middle voice from the base of στρατιά ; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations.

G4755.d: from the base of στρατιά and ἄγω or ἡγέομαι ; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens.

G4756.d: feminine of a derivative of stratos (an army; from the base of στρώννυμι , as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries.

G4757.d: from a presumed derivative of the same as στρατιά ; a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively).

G4758.d: from a compound of the base of στρατιά and λέγω (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army.

G4759.d: from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω ; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω ; a ruler of an army, i.e. præfect.

G4760.d: from the base of στρατιά and the same as πεδινός ; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops.

G4761.d: from a derivative of στρέφω ; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert.

G4762.d: strengthened from the base of τροπή ; to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively).
G4762.k: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about)

G4763.d: from a presumed derivative of στρῆνος ; to be luxurious.

G4764.d: akin to στερεός ; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness).

G4765.d: diminutive of strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow.

G4766.d: or simpler stronnuo , prolongation from a still simpler stroo , (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to στερεός through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch).

G4767.d: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate); hated, i.e. odious.

G4768.d: from the same as στυγνητός ; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech).

G4769.d: from stuo (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of ἵστημι ); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support.

G4770.d: from στοά ; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy.

G4771.d: the personal pronoun of the second person singular; thou. See also σέ , σοί , σοῦ ; and for the plural ὑμᾶς , ὑμεῖς , ὑμῖν , ὑμῶν .

G4773.d: from σύν and γένος ; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman.

G4774.d: from a compound of σύν and γινώσκω ; fellow knowledge, i.e. concession.

G4775.d: from σύν and κάθημαι ; to seat oneself in company with.

G4776.d: from σύν and καθίζω ; to give (or take) a seat in company with.

G4777.d: from σύν and κακοπαθέω ; to suffer hardship in company with.

G4778.d: from σύν and κακουχέω ; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together.

G4779.d: from σύν and καλέω ; to convoke.

G4780.d: from σύν and καλύπτω ; to conceal altogether.

G4781.d: from σύν and κάμπτω ; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict.

G4782.d: from σύν and καταβαίνω ; to descend in company with.

G4783.d: from συγκατατίθεμαι ; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with.

G4784.d: middle from σύν and κατατίθημι ; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with.

G4785.d: from σύν and a compound of κατά and ψηφίζω ; to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among.

G4786.d: from σύν and κεράννυμι ; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate.

G4787.d: from σπαράσσω and κινέω ; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition).

G4788.d: from σύν and κλείω ; to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to.

G4789.d: from σύν and κληρονόμος ; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common.

G4790.d: from σύν and κοινωνέω ; to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in.
G4790.k: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of

G4791.d: from σύν and κοινωνός ; a co-participant.

G4792.d: from σύν and κομίζω ; to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others.

G4793.d: from σύν and κρίνω ; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance).

G4794.d: from σύν and κύπτω ; to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by.

G4795.d: from a comparative of σύν and kureo (to light or happen; from the base of κύριος ); concurrence, i.e. accident.

G4796.d: from σύν and χαίρω ; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate.

G4797.d: or sugchuno from σύν and cheo (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind).
G4797.k: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar

G4798.d: from σύν and χράομαι ; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common.

G4799.d: from συγχέω ; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance.

G4800.d: from σύν and ζάω ; to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively).

G4801.d: from σύν and the base of ζεῦγος ; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage).

G4802.d: from σύν and ζητέω ; to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil.

G4803.d: from συζητέω ; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion.

G4804.d: from συζητέω ; a disputant, i.e. sophist.

G4805.d: from συζεύγνυμι ; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian.

G4806.d: from σύν and ζωοποιέω ; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively).

G4807.d: of Hebrew origin ( שִׁקְמִים ) in imitation of συκομωραία ; a sycamore-fig tree.

G4809.d: from σῦκον and moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree. Compare συκάμινος .

G4810.d: apparently a primary word; a fig.

G4811.d: from a compound of σῦκον and a derivative of φαίνω ; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort).
G4811.k: accuse falsely, take by false accusation

G4812.d: from the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω ; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce.

G4813.d: from a derivative of sullo (to strip; probably akin to αἱρέομαι ; compare σκῦλον ); to despoil.

G4814.d: from σύν and λαλέω ; to talk together, i.e. converse.

G4815.d: from σύν and λαμβάνω ; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid.

G4816.d: from σύν and λέγω in its original sense; to collect.

G4817.d: from σύν and λογίζομαι ; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate.

G4818.d: from σύν and λυπέω ; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone.

G4819.d: from σύν and the base of βάσις ; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place).

G4820.d: from σύν and βάλλω ; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack.
G4820.k: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder

G4821.d: from σύν and βασιλεύω ; to be co-regent (figuratively).

G4822.d: from σύν and bibazo (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of βάσις ); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach.
G4822.k: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove

G4823.d: from σύν and βουλεύω ; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine.

G4824.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος ; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court.

G4825.d: from σύν and βουλή ; a consultor, i.e. adviser.

G4826.d: from the same as Σίμων ; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites.

G4827.d: from a compound of σύν and μανθάνω ; a co-learner (of Christianity).

G4828.d: from σύν and μαρτυρέω ; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence.

G4829.d: middle voice from σύν and μερίζω ; to share jointly, i.e. participate in.

G4830.d: from σύν and μέτοχος ; a co-participant.

G4831.d: from a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι ; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary.

G4832.d: from σύν and μορφή ; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar.

G4833.d: from σύμμορφος ; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate.

G4834.d: from συμπαθής ; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate.
G4834.k: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of

G4835.d: from συμπάσχω ; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative.

G4836.d: from σύν and παραγίνομαι ; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid.

G4837.d: from σύν and παρακαλέω ; to console jointly.

G4838.d: from σύν and παραλαμβάνω ; to take along in company.

G4839.d: from σύν and παραμένω ; to remain in company, i.e. still live.

G4840.d: from σύν and πάρειμι ; to be at hand together, i.e. now present.

G4841.d: from σύν and πάσχω (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize").

G4842.d: from σύν and πέμπω ; to despatch in company.

G4843.d: from σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω ; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one.

G4844.d: from σύν and πίνω ; to partake a beverage in company.

G4845.d: from σύν and πληρόω ; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete).

G4846.d: from σύν and πνίγω ; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd.

G4847.d: from σύν and πολίτης ; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian).

G4848.d: from σύν and πορεύομαι ; to journey together; by implication, to assemble.

G4849.d: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω ; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests.

G4850.d: from σύν and πρεσβύτερος ; a co-presbyter.

G4851.d: from σύν and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage.
G4851.k: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for)

G4852.d: from σύν and φημί ; to say jointly, i.e. assent to.

G4853.d: from σύν and a derivative of φυλή ; a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country.

G4854.d: from σύν and a derivative of φύω ; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to.

G4855.d: from σύν and φύω ; passive, to grow jointly.

G4856.d: from σύμφωνος ; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact).

G4858.d: from σύμφωνος ; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note).

G4859.d: from σύν and φωνή ; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement).

G4860.d: from σύν and ψηφίζω ; to compute jointly.

G4861.d: from σύν and ψυχή ; co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment.

G4862.d: a primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than μετά or παρά ), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc. In composition it has similar applications, including completeness.

G4863.d: from σύν and ἄγω ; to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably).
G4863.k: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in

G4864.d: from (the reduplicated form of) συνάγω ; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church.

G4865.d: from σύν and ἀγωνίζομαι ; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant).

G4866.d: from σύν and ἀθλέω ; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly.

G4867.d: from σύν and athroizo (to hoard); to convene.

G4868.d: from σύν and αἴρω ; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account).

G4869.d: from σύν and αἰχμάλωτος ; a co-captive.

G4870.d: from σύν and ἀκολουθέω ; to accompany.

G4871.d: from σύν and halizo (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene.

G4872.d: from σύν and ἀναβαίνω ; to ascend in company with.

G4873.d: from σύν and ἀνακεῖμαι ; to recline in company with (at a meal).
G4873.k: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat)

G4874.d: from σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι ; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with.

G4875.d: middle from σύν and ἀναπαύω ; to recruit oneself in company with.

G4876.d: from σύν and a derivative of ἀντί ; to meet with; figuratively, to occur.

G4878.d: from σύν and ἀντιλαμβάνομαι ; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist).

G4879.d: from σύν and ἀπάγω ; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield).

G4880.d: from σύν and ἀποθνήσκω ; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to.

G4881.d: from σύν and ἀπόλλυμι ; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with.

G4882.d: from σύν and ἀποστέλλω ; to despatch (on an errand) in company with.

G4883.d: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ἁρμός and λέγω (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly.

G4884.d: from σύν and ἁρπάζω ; to snatch together, i.e. seize.

G4885.d: from σύν and αὐξάνω ; to increase (grow up) together.

G4886.d: from σύν and δεσμόν ; a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control.

G4887.d: from σύν and δέω ; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively).

G4888.d: from σύν and δοξάζω ; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with.

G4889.d: from σύν and δοῦλος ; a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine).

G4890.d: from (the alternate of) συντρέχω ; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse.

G4891.d: from σύν and ἐγείρω ; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to.

G4892.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of σύν and the base of ἑδραῖος ; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal.

G4893.d: from a prolonged form of συνείδω ; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness.

G4894.d: from σύν and εἴδω ; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of.
G4894.k: consider, know, be privy, be ware of

G4895.d: from σύν and εἰμί (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. present at the time.

G4896.d: from σύν and eimi (to go); to assemble.

G4897.d: from σύν and εἰσέρχομαι ; to enter in company with.
G4897.k: go in with, go with into

G4898.d: from σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω ; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller.

G4899.d: from a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι ; chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian).

G4900.d: from σύν and ἐλαύνω ; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation).

G4901.d: from σύν and ἐπιμαρτυρέω ; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence.

G4902.d: middle voice from σύν and a primary hepo (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with.

G4903.d: from συνεργός ; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate.

G4904.d: from a presumed compound of σύν and the base of ἔργον ; a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor.
G4904.k: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow

G4905.d: from σύν and ἔρχομαι ; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally).
G4905.k: accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort

G4906.d: from σύν and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to take food in company with.
