G5114.d: comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than κόπτω , as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen.

G5115.d: from the base of τίκτω ; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric).

G5116.d: neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite.

G5117.d: apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas χώρα is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard.
G5117.k: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where

G5118.d: from tosos (so much; apparently from ὁ and ὅς ) and οὗτος (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space).
G5118.k: as large, so great (long, many, much), these many

G5119.d: from (the neuter of) ὁ and ὅτε ; the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution).

G5120.d: properly, the genitive case of ὁ ; sometimes used for τούτου ; of this person.

G5121.d: contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ἐναντίον ; on the contrary.

G5122.d: contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ὄνομα ; the name (is).

G5123.d: contraction for τοῦτο and ἐστί ; that is.

G5124.d: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of οὗτος ; that thing.
G5124.k: here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore)

G5125.d: dative case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος ; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things).
G5125.k: such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those

G5126.d: accusative case singular masculine of οὗτος ; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition).

G5127.d: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος ; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing).
G5127.k: here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus

G5128.d: accusative case plural masculine of οὗτος ; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition).

G5129.d: dative case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος ; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing).
G5129.k: here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this

G5130.d: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος ; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things).
G5130.k: such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those

G5131.d: from the base of τρώγω ; a he-goat (as a gnawer).

G5132.d: probably contracted from τέσσαρες and πεζῇ ; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest).

G5133.d: from τράπεζα ; a money-broker or banker.

G5134.d: from the base of titrosko (to wound; akin to the base of θραύω , τρίβος , τρίζω , etc.); a wound.

G5135.d: from τραῦμα ; to inflict a wound.

G5136.d: from τράχηλος ; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare).

G5137.d: probably from τρέχω (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life.

G5138.d: perhaps strengthened from the base of ῥήγνυμι (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy).

G5139.d: from a derivative of τραχύς ; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria.

G5140.d: or neuter tria a primary (plural) number; "three".

G5141.d: strengthened from a primary treo (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear.

G5142.d: a primary verb (properly, threpho; but perhaps strengthened from the base of τροπή through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear).

G5143.d: apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho; compare θρίξ ); which uses dremo drem'-o (the base of δρόμος ) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively).

G5145.d: plural from τρεῖς and ἑκατόν ; three hundred.

G5146.d: from τρεῖς and βέλος ; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop).

G5147.d: from tribo (to "rub"; akin to teiro, truo, and the base of τράγος , τραῦμα ); a rut or worn track.

G5148.d: from a compound of τρεῖς and ἔτος ; a three years' period (triennium).

G5149.d: apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy).

G5150.d: neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and μήν as noun; a three months' space.

G5152.d: neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and στέγη as noun; a third roof (story).

G5153.d: from τρίς and χίλιοι ; three times a thousand.

G5154.d: ordinal from τρεῖς ; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly.

G5155.d: from θρίξ ; hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair).

G5156.d: from τρέμω ; a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear.

G5157.d: from an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. revolution (figuratively, variation).

G5158.d: from the same as τροπή ; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character.
G5158.k: (even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way

G5159.d: from τρόπος and φορέω ; to endure one's habits.

G5160.d: from τρέφω ; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages).

G5161.d: from τροφή ; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian.

G5162.d: from τρέφω ; a nourisher, i.e. nurse.

G5163.d: from τροχός ; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct.

G5164.d: from τρέχω ; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects.

G5165.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl.

G5166.d: from a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage.

G5167.d: from truzo (to murmur; akin to τρίζω , but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing).

G5168.d: from a derivative of truo (to wear away; akin to the base of τραῦμα , τρίβος and τρώγω ); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye. Compare τρύπημα .

G5169.d: from a derivative of the base of τρυμαλιά ; an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye.

G5170.d: from τρυφή ; luxurious; Tryphæna, a Christian woman.

G5171.d: from τρυφή ; to indulge in luxury.

G5172.d: from thrupto (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. luxury or debauchery.

G5173.d: from τρυφή ; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female.

G5174.d: from Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor.

G5175.d: of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor.

G5176.d: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of τραῦμα and τρίβος through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of τρυγών and τρίζω through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat.

G5177.d: probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of τίκτω through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with εἰ ), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with οὐ , extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were). Compare τύπτω .
G5177.k: be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special

G5178.d: from a derivative of τύπτω (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death.

G5179.d: from τύπτω ; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning).
G5179.k: en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print

G5180.d: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from παίω and πατάσσω , which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or πλήσσω with the fist (or a hammer), or ῥαπίζω with the palm; as well as from τυγχάνω , an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience).

G5181.d: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of κύριος ; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian.

G5182.d: from turbe (Latin turba , a crowd; akin to θόρυβος ); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb.

G5183.d: from Τύρος ; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus.

G5184.d: of Hebrew origin ( צֹר ): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine.

G5185.d: from, τυφόω ; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally).

G5186.d: from τυφλός ; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure.

G5187.d: from a derivative of τύφω ; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit.
G5187.k: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud

G5188.d: apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame.

G5189.d: from a derivative of τύφω ; stormy (as if smoky).

G5190.d: from a derivative of τυγχάνω ; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian.

G5191.d: from ὑάκινθος ; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. deep blue.

G5192.d: of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon.

G5194.d: perhaps from the same as ὑετός (as being transparent like rain); glass.

G5195.d: from ὕβρις ; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse.

G5196.d: from ὑπέρ ; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury.

G5197.d: from ὑβρίζω ; an insulter, i.e. maltreater.

G5198.d: from ὑγιής ; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine).
G5198.k: be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some)

G5199.d: from the base of αὐξάνω ; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine).

G5200.d: from the base of ὑετός ; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh).

G5201.d: from ὕδωρ ; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply.

G5202.d: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω ; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages.

G5203.d: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical".

G5204.d: and genitive case, hudatos , etc. from the base of ὑετός ; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively.

G5205.d: from a primary huo (to rain); rain, especially a shower.

G5206.d: from a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι ; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God).

G5207.d: apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship.

G5208.d: perhaps akin to ξύλον ; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel.

G5209.d: accusative case of ὑμεῖς ; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition).

G5210.d: irregular plural of σύ ; you (as subjective of verb).

G5211.d: from Humen (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity.

G5212.d: from ὑμεῖς ; yours, i.e. pertaining to you.

G5213.d: irregular dative case of ὑμεῖς ; to (with or by) you.

G5214.d: from ὕμνος ; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song.

G5215.d: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate; probably akin to ᾄδω ; compare עֲבוֹט ); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms).

G5216.d: genitive case of ὑμεῖς ; of (from or concerning) you.

G5217.d: from ὑπό and ἄγω ; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively.

G5218.d: from ὑπακούω ; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission.

G5219.d: from ὑπό and ἀκούω ; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority.

G5220.d: from ὑπό and ἀνήρ ; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman.

G5221.d: from ὑπό and a derivative of ἀντί ; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with.

G5222.d: from ὑπαντάω ; an encounter or concurrence (with εἰς for infinitive, in order to fall in with).

G5223.d: from ὑπάρχω ; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth.

G5224.d: neuter plural of present participle active of ὑπάρχω as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions.
G5224.k: goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast

G5225.d: from ὑπό and ἄρχομαι ; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb).

G5226.d: from ὑπό and eiko (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender.

G5227.d: from ὑπό and ἐναντίος ; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent.

G5228.d: a primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than. In the comparative, it retains many of the above applications.
G5228.k: (+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very

G5229.d: middle voice from ὑπέρ and αἴρω ; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty.
G5229.k: exalt self, be exalted above measure

G5230.d: from ὑπέρ and the base of ἀκμήν ; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth.

G5231.d: from ὑπέρ and ἄνω ; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank).

G5232.d: from ὑπέρ and αὐξάνω ; to increase above ordinary degree.

G5233.d: from ὑπέρ and the base of βάσις ; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach.

G5234.d: adverb from present participle active of ὑπερβάλλω ; excessively.

G5235.d: from ὑπέρ and βάλλω ; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent).

G5236.d: from ὑπερβάλλω ; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with εἰς or κατά ) pre- eminently.
G5236.k: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure

G5237.d: from ὑπέρ and εἴδω ; to overlook, i.e. not punish.

G5238.d: from ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος ; above those parts, i.e. still farther.

G5239.d: from ὑπέρ and ἐκτείνω ; to extend inordinately.

G5240.d: from ὑπέρ and the alternate form of ἐκχέω ; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow.

G5241.d: from ὑπέρ and ἐντυγχάνω ; to intercede in behalf of.

G5242.d: from ὑπέρ and ἔχω ; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority.

G5244.d: from ὑπέρ and φαίνω ; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty.

G5245.d: from ὑπέρ and νικάω ; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory.

G5246.d: from ὑπέρ and ὄγκος ; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent.

G5247.d: from ὑπερέχω ; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character).

G5248.d: from ὑπέρ and περισσεύω ; to super-abound.

G5249.d: from ὑπέρ and περισσῶς ; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly.

G5250.d: from ὑπέρ and πλεονάζω ; to superabound.

G5251.d: from ὑπέρ and ὑψόω ; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position.

G5252.d: from ὑπέρ and φρονέω ; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant.

G5253.d: neuter of a derivative of ὑπέρ ; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story.

G5254.d: from ὑπό and ἔχω ; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience.

G5255.d: from ὑπακούω ; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive.

G5256.d: from ὑπηρέτης ; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve.

G5257.d: from ὑπό and a derivative of eresso (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable).

G5258.d: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to ὑπό through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor.

G5259.d: a primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)). In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.
G5259.k: among, by, from, in, of, under, with

G5260.d: from ὑπό and βάλλω ; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion.

G5261.d: from a compound of ὑπό and γράφω ; an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively).

G5262.d: from ὑποδείκνυμι ; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration).

G5263.d: from ὑπό and δεικνύω ; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish).

G5264.d: from ὑπό and δέχομαι ; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably.

G5265.d: from ὑπό and δέω ; to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals.

G5266.d: from ὑποδέω ; something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal.

G5267.d: from ὑπό and δίκη ; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned.

G5268.d: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and ζυγός ; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey.

G5269.d: from ὑπό and ζώννυμι ; to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck).

G5270.d: from ὑπό and κάτω ; down under, i.e. beneath.

G5271.d: middle voice from ὑπό and κρίνω ; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend).

G5272.d: from ὑποκρίνομαι ; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy").

G5273.d: from ὑποκρίνομαι ; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite".

G5274.d: from ὑπό and λαμβάνω ; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume).

G5275.d: from ὑποτρέχω and λείπω ; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive).

G5276.d: neuter of a presumed compound of ὑπό and ληνός ; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat.

G5277.d: a prolonged form for ὑπολείπω ; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath.

G5278.d: from ὑπό and μένω ; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere.
G5278.k: abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind

G5279.d: from ὑπό and μιμνήσκω ; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory.
G5279.k: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance

G5280.d: from ὑπομιμνήσκω ; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection.

G5281.d: from ὑπομένω ; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy.

G5282.d: from ὑπό and νοιέω ; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture.

G5284.d: from ὑπό and πλέω ; to sail under the lee of.

G5285.d: from ὑπό and πνέω ; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze.

G5286.d: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and πούς ; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively).

G5287.d: from a compound of ὑπό and ἵστημι ; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively).

G5288.d: from ὑπό and στέλλω ; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve).

G5289.d: from ὑποστέλλω ; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy.

G5290.d: from ὑπό and στρέφω ; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively).
G5290.k: come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again)

G5291.d: from ὑπό and στρώννυμι ; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet).

G5293.d: from ὑπό and τάσσω ; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey.
G5293.k: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto

G5294.d: from ὑπό and τίθημι ; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest.

G5295.d: from ὑπό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past.

G5296.d: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of τύπος ; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation.

G5297.d: from ὑπό and φέρω ; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship.

G5298.d: from ὑπό and χωρέω ; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly.

G5299.d: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι ; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions).

G5300.d: apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine").

G5302.d: from ὕστερος ; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient).
G5302.k: come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse

G5303.d: from ὑστερέω ; a deficit; specially, poverty.
G5303.k: that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want

G5304.d: from ὑστερέω ; a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury.

G5305.d: neuter of ὕστερος as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually.

G5306.d: comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind); later.

G5307.d: from huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted.

G5308.d: from ὕψος ; lofty (in place or character).

G5309.d: from a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν ; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant.

G5310.d: superlative from the base of ὕψος ; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens.

G5311.d: from a derivative of ὑπέρ ; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity.

G5312.d: from ὕψος ; to elevate (literally or figuratively).

G5313.d: from ὑψόω ; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively).

G5315.d: a primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively).

G5316.d: prolongation for the base of φῶς ; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative).
G5316.k: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think

G5317.d: of Hebrew origin ( פָּ֫לֶג ); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch.

G5318.d: from φαίνω ; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally.
G5318.k: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly)

G5319.d: from φανερός ; to render apparent (literally or figuratively).

G5320.d: adverb from φανερός ; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly.

G5321.d: from φανερόω ; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment.

G5322.d: from φαίνω ; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern.

G5323.d: of Hebrew origin ( פְּנוּאֵל ); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite.

G5324.d: from a derivative of φαίνω ; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle).

G5325.d: from a derivative of φαντάζω ; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy").

G5326.d: from φαντάζω ; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre.

G5327.d: properly, strengthened from the base of πέραν or rather of ῥήγνυμι ; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent).

G5328.d: of foreign origin ( פַּרְעֹה ); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king.

G5329.d: of Hebrew origin ( פָּ֫רֶץ ); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite.

G5330.d: of Hebrew origin (compare פָּרַשׁ ); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary.

G5331.d: from φαρμακεύς ; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively).

G5332.d: from pharmakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician.

G5334.d: from φημί (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω ); a saying, i.e. report.

G5335.d: prolongation from the same as φημί ; to assert.

G5336.d: from pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder).

G5337.d: apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked.

G5338.d: probably akin to the base of φῶς (compare φθέγγομαι ); brilliancy.

G5339.d: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently.

G5340.d: adverb from participle of φείδομαι ; abstemiously, i.e. stingily.

G5341.d: by transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout).

G5342.d: a primary verb -- for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio oy'-o; and enegko en-eng'-ko; to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows).
G5342.k: be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold

G5343.d: apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish.

G5344.d: of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman.

G5345.d: from φημί ; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame").

G5346.d: properly, the same as the base of φῶς and φαίνω ; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say. Compare λέγω .

G5347.d: of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman.

G5348.d: apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at.

G5349.d: from φθείρω ; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable.

G5350.d: probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί ; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim.

G5351.d: probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave).

G5352.d: from derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of φθείρω ) and ὀπώρα (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves).

G5353.d: from φθέγγομαι ; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental).

G5354.d: from φθόνος ; to be jealous of.

G5355.d: probably akin to the base of φθείρω ; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite).

G5356.d: from φθείρω ; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively).

G5357.d: of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial").

G5358.d: from φίλος and ἀγαθός ; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue.

G5359.d: from Philadelphos (the same as φιλάδελφος ), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor.

G5360.k: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren

G5361.d: from φίλος and ἀδελφός ; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal.

G5362.d: from φίλος and ἀνήρ ; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife.

G5363.d: from the same as φιλανθρώπως ; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy").

G5364.d: adverb from a compound of φίλος and ἄνθρωπος ; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely.

G5366.d: from φίλος and ἄργυρος ; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious.

G5367.d: from φίλος and αὐτός ; fond of self, i.e. selfish.

G5368.d: from φίλος ; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while ἀγαπάω is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as θέλω and βούλομαι , or as θυμός and νοῦς respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness).

G5369.d: from φίλος and ἡδονή ; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous.

G5371.d: from φιλέω ; friendly; Philemon, a Christian.

G5372.d: from φιλέω ; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity.

G5374.d: from Φίλιπποι ; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi.

G5375.d: plural of Φίλιππος ; Philippi, a place in Macedonia.

G5376.d: from φίλος and ἵππος ; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites.

G5377.d: from φίλος and θεός ; fond of God, i.e. pious.

G5378.d: from φίλος and λόγος ; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian.

G5379.d: from φιλόνεικος ; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute.

G5380.d: from φίλος and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to νῖκος ); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious.

G5382.d: from φίλος and ξένος ; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable.

G5383.d: from a compound of φίλος and πρῶτος ; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction.

G5384.d: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.).

G5386.d: from φίλος and σοφός ; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher".

G5387.d: from φίλος and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian.

G5388.d: from φίλος and τέκνον ; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal.

G5389.d: middle voice from a compound of φίλος and τιμή ; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something).

G5390.d: adverb from φιλόφρων ; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly.

G5391.d: from φίλος and φρήν ; friendly of mind, i.e. kind.

G5393.d: active participle of the base of φλόξ ; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian.

G5394.d: from φλόξ ; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion).

G5395.d: from a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze.

G5396.d: from φλύαρος ; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously.

G5397.d: from phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater.

G5399.d: from φόβος ; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere.

G5400.d: neuter of a derivative of φοβέω ; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent.

G5401.d: from a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright.

G5402.d: feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of φῶς ); Phœbe, a Christian woman.

G5403.d: from φοῖνιξ ; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine.

G5405.d: probably the same as φοῖνιξ ; Phœnix, a place in Crete.

G5406.d: from φόνος ; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος is a special term for a public bandit).

G5407.d: from φονεύς ; to be a murderer (of).

G5408.d: from an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder.

G5409.d: from φόρος ; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment.

G5410.d: of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Ἄππιος ; a station on the Appian road.

G5411.d: from φέρω ; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas τέλος is usually a general toll on goods or travel).

G5412.d: from φόρτος ; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety).

G5413.d: diminutive of φόρτος ; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service.

G5414.d: from φέρω ; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship.

G5415.d: of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus , a Christian.

G5416.d: neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω ; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment.

G5417.d: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum ; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment.

G5418.d: from φράσσω ; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively).

G5419.d: probably akin to φράσσω through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound.

G5420.d: apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν ; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence).

G5421.d: of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison).

G5422.d: from φρεναπάτης ; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude.

G5423.d: from φρήν and ἀπάτη ; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer.

G5424.d: probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare φράσσω ); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties).

G5425.d: apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear).

G5426.d: from φρήν ; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience).
G5426.k: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think

G5428.d: from φρονέω ; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight.

G5429.d: from φρήν ; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative).

G5431.d: from a derivative of φρήν ; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious.

G5432.d: from a compound of πρό and ὁράω ; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect. Compare τηρέω .

G5433.d: akin to βρύω , βρύχω ; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult.

G5434.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of φλόξ ); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig.

G5435.d: probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor.

G5436.d: probably from φεύγω ; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian.

G5437.d: from φεύγω ; a fleeing, i.e. escape.

G5438.d: from φυλάσσω ; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively.

G5440.d: neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω ; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts.

G5441.d: from φυλάσσω ; a watcher or sentry.

G5442.d: probably from φυλή through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid. Compare τηρέω .

G5443.d: from φύω (compare φύλλον ); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan.

G5444.d: from the same as φυλή ; a sprout, i.e. leaf.

G5445.d: from a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough.

G5446.d: from φύσις ; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive. Compare ψυχικός .

G5447.d: adverb from φυσικός ; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively.

G5448.d: from φύσις in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty).

G5449.d: from φύω ; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage.

G5451.d: from φυτεύω ; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable.

G5452.d: from a derivative of φύω ; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine.

G5453.d: a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively.

G5454.d: of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place.

G5455.d: from φωνή ; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation.

G5456.d: probably akin to φαίνω through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language.

G5457.d: from an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω , φημί ); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative).

G5458.d: from φῶς ; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy.

G5459.d: from φῶς and φέρω ; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively).

G5460.d: from φῶς ; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively).

G5461.d: from φῶς ; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively).
G5461.k: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see

G5463.d: a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well.
G5463.k: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice

G5465.d: from the base of χάσμα ; to lower (as into a void).

G5466.d: probably of Hebrew or ( כַּשְׂדִּי ); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates.

G5467.d: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious.

G5468.d: from a compound of χαλινός and the reduplicated form of ἄγω ; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively).

G5469.d: from χαλάω ; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit).

G5471.d: from χαλκός ; a copper-worker or brazier.

G5472.d: from χαλκός and perhaps εἶδος ; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony".

G5473.d: diminutive from χαλκός ; a copper dish.

G5474.d: neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre.

G5475.d: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it).

G5476.d: adverb perhaps from the base of χάσμα through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate.

G5477.d: of Hebrew origin ( כְּנַ֫עַן ); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine.

G5478.d: from Χαναάν ; a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine.

G5479.d: from χαίρω ; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight.
G5479.k: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous)

G5480.d: from the same as χάραξ ; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue).

G5481.d: from the same as χάραξ ; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation).

G5482.d: from charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to γράφω through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege).

G5483.d: middle voice from χάρις ; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue.

G5484.d: accusative case of χάρις as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of.
G5484.k: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully

G5485.d: from χαίρω ; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude).
G5485.k: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy)

G5486.d: from χαρίζομαι ; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty.

G5487.d: from χάρις ; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor.

G5488.d: of Hebrew origin ( חָרָן ); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia.

G5489.d: from the same as χάραξ ; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over).

G5490.d: from a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval).

G5491.d: from a form of the same as χάσμα ; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water).

G5492.d: from the same as χειμών ; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale.

G5493.d: from the base of χειμών and ῥέω ; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent.

G5494.d: from a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of χάσμα through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter.

G5495.d: perhaps from the base of χειμών in the sense of its congener the base of χάσμα (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument).

G5496.d: from χειραγωγός ; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person).

G5497.d: from χείρ and a reduplicated form of ἄγω ; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person).
G5497.k: some to lead by the hand

G5498.d: neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω ; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)).

G5499.d: from χείρ and a derivative of ποιέω ; manufactured, i.e. of human construction.

G5500.d: from a comparative of χείρ and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint.

G5501.d: irregular comparative of κακός ; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally).

G5502.d: plural of Hebrew origin ( כְּרוּב ); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim).

G5503.d: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of χάσμα through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively.

G5504.d: of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto.

G5506.d: from χίλιοι and ἄρχω ; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel.

G5507.d: plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand.

G5508.d: of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean.

G5509.d: of foreign origin ( כֻּתֹּ֫נֶת ); a tunic or shirt.

G5510.d: perhaps akin to the base of χάσμα ( χαλάω ) or χειμών (as descending or empty); snow.

G5511.d: of uncertain derivation; a military cloak.

G5512.d: from a derivative probably of χεῖλος ; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at.

G5514.d: feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloë, a Christian female.

G5515.d: from the same as Χλόη ; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored.

G5516.d: the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter ( στίγμα as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral.

G5517.d: from χόος ; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene.

G5518.d: of uncertain derivation; a chœnix or certain dry measure.

G5520.d: from χολή ; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric").

G5521.d: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Χλόη (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.).

G5522.d: from the base of χειμών ; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt.

G5523.d: of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine.

G5524.d: from a compound of χορός and ἄγω ; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish.

G5525.d: of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir".

G5526.d: from χόρτος ; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance).

G5528.d: apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation.

G5529.d: of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod.

G5530.d: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from χείρ , to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner. Compare χράω ; χρή .

G5531.d: probably the same as the base of χράομαι ; to loan.

G5532.d: from the base of χράομαι or χρή ; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution.
G5532.k: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want

G5533.d: from a derivative of χράω and ὀφειλέτης ; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person.

G5534.d: third person singular of the same as χράομαι or χράω used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be.

G5535.d: from χρεία ; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of.

G5536.d: something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price.

G5537.d: from χρῆμα ; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of χράομαι ), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of χρεία ) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title.
G5537.k: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak

G5538.d: from χρηματίζω ; a divine response or revelation.

G5540.d: from χράομαι ; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body).

G5541.d: middle voice from χρηστός ; to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently.

G5542.d: from a compound of χρηστός and λέγω ; fair speech, i.e. plausibility.

G5543.d: from χράομαι ; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals).

G5544.d: from χρηστός ; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor).

G5545.d: from χρίω ; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit.

G5546.d: from Χριστός ; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ.

G5547.d: from χρίω ; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus.

G5548.d: probably akin to χράομαι through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service.

G5549.d: from χρόνος ; to take time, i.e. linger.

G5550.d: of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from καιρός , which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from αἰών , which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay.
G5550.k: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while

G5551.d: from a presumed compound of χρόνος and the base of τρίβος ; to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger).

G5553.d: diminutive of χρυσός ; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin.

G5554.d: from χρυσός and δακτύλιος ; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry.

G5555.d: from χρυσός and λίθος ; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite").

G5556.d: from χρυσός and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase").

G5557.d: perhaps from the base of χράομαι (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin.

G5558.d: from χρυσός ; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments.

G5559.d: probably akin to the base of χράομαι through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin).

G5560.d: apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping.

G5561.d: feminine of a derivative of the base of χάσμα through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants). Compare τόπος .
G5561.k: coast, county, fields, ground, land, region

G5562.d: from χώρα ; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively).
G5562.k: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive

G5563.d: from χώρα ; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away.

G5564.d: diminutive of χώρα ; a spot or plot of ground.
G5564.k: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession

G5565.d: adverb from χώρα ; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition).

G5566.d: of Latin origin; the north-west wind.

G5567.d: probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare ψώχω ); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes).

G5568.d: from ψάλλω ; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms. Compare ᾠδή .

G5569.d: from ψευδής and ἀδελφός ; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate.

G5570.d: from ψευδής and ἀπόστολος ; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher.

G5571.d: from ψεύδομαι ; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked.

G5572.d: from ψευδής and διδάσκαλος ; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine.

G5573.d: from ψευδής and λέγω ; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine.

G5574.d: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood.

G5575.d: from ψευδής and a kindred form of μάρτυς ; a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony.

G5576.d: from ψευδομάρτυρ ; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence.

G5578.d: from ψευδής and προφήτης ; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor.

G5580.d: from ψευδής and Χριστός ; a spurious Messiah.

G5581.d: from ψευδής and ὄνομα ; untruly named.

G5582.d: from ψεύδομαι ; a fabrication, i.e. falsehood.

G5584.d: from the base of ψάλλω (compare ψῆφος ); to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for.

G5585.d: from ψῆφος ; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute.

G5586.d: from the same as ψηλαφάω ; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote.

G5587.d: from a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to ψεύδομαι ); whispering, i.e. secret detraction.

G5588.d: from the same as ψιθυρισμός ; a secret calumniator.

G5589.d: diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψάλλω (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel.

G5590.d: from ψύχω ; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from πνεῦμα , which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from ζωή , which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew נָ֫פֶשׁ , ר֫וּחַ and חָי ).
G5590.k: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you

G5591.d: from ψυχή ; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from πνευματικός , which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from φυσικός , which is the lower or bestial nature).

G5594.d: a primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from πνέω , which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of ἀήρ , which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively).

G5595.d: from the base of ψωμίον ; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish.

G5596.d: diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψώχω ; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful.

G5597.d: prolongation from the same base as ψάλλω ; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand).

G5598.d: the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality.

G5599.d: a primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh.

G5600.d: including the oblique forms, as well as es ; e ; etc. the subjunctive of εἰμί ; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with εἰ and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be.
G5600.k: + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were

G5601.d: of Hebrew origin ( עוֹבֵד ); Obed, an Israelite.

G5602.d: from an adverb form of ὅδε ; in this same spot, i.e. here or hither.

G5603.d: from ᾄδω ; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while ὕμνος denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and ψαλμός still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation).

G5604.d: akin to ὀδύνη ; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth.

G5605.d: from ὠδίν ; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively).

G5606.d: perhaps from the alternate of φέρω ; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne).

G5607.d: including the feminine ousa ; and the neuter on present participle of εἰμί ; being.

G5608.d: middle voice from an apparently primary onos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier πίμπρημι ).

G5610.d: apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively).
G5610.k: day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time

G5611.d: from ὥρα ; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)).

G5612.d: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar".

G5613.d: probably adverb of comparative from ὅς ; which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows).
G5613.k: about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed

G5614.d: of Hebrew origin ( יָשַׁע and נָא ); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration.

G5615.d: from ὡς and an adverb from αὐτός ; as thus, i.e. in the same way.
G5615.k: even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner

G5616.d: from ὡς and εἰ ; as if.
G5616.k: about, as (it had been, it were), like (as)

G5617.d: of Hebrew origin ( הוֹשֵׁ֫עַ ); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite.

G5618.d: from ὡς and περ ; just as, i.e. exactly like.

G5619.d: from ὥσπερ and εἰ ; just as if, i.e. as it were.

G5620.d: from ὡς and τέ ; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow).
G5620.k: (insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore

G5621.d: diminutive of οὖς ; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear.

G5622.d: from a derivative of the base of ὠφέλιμος ; usefulness, i.e. benefit.

G5623.d: from the same as ὠφέλεια ; to be useful, i.e. to benefit.

G5624.d: from a form of ὄφελος ; helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous.
